use: Use as instructions for formula feeding.
body:
Formula feeding

Formula is safe and complete food for your baby.

Choosing formula:

- Regular iron-fortified formula is right for most babies.
- Store brands are just as good as name brands.
- Do not switch formulas often for normal fussiness. Ask us first.

Making formula:

- Follow the package directions exactly.
- Use safe drinking water. For babies under 2 months, boil the water and let it cool.
- Warm the bottle in a bowl of warm water. Never use a microwave.

How much:

- Newborn: 1 to 2 ounces every 2 to 3 hours
- 2 months: 3 to 4 ounces every 3 to 4 hours
- 4 months: 4 to 6 ounces every 4 hours
- These amounts are only a guide. Feed when your baby is hungry.

Storage:

- Throw away formula left in a bottle 1 hour after the feed starts.
- Mixed formula not yet used can stay in the fridge for 24 hours.

Never:

- Add water to make formula last longer
- Add cereal to a bottle
- Give cow's milk before 12 months

Call your baby's doctor if your baby vomits often, has fewer wet diapers, or has blood in the stool.

use: Use as instructions for safe infant sleep.
body:
Safe sleep for your baby

Follow the ABCs every sleep, with every caregiver.

- Alone: your baby sleeps alone, not with adults, children, or pets.
- Back: always put your baby on the back to sleep.
- Crib: use a firm, flat crib, bassinet, or play yard with only a fitted sheet.

Keep the sleep space empty:

- No pillows, blankets, bumpers, toys, or positioners.
- Dress your baby in a sleep sack instead of using a blanket.

More tips:

- Share a room with your baby for at least 6 months, but not a bed.
- Offer a pacifier at sleep time once breastfeeding is going well.
- Keep your baby from getting too hot.
- Keep your home and car smoke-free.
- Do not let your baby sleep in a swing, bouncer, or car seat outside the car.

Tummy time: when your baby is awake and someone is watching, place your baby on the tummy. Do this a few minutes, several times a day.

Call your baby's doctor with questions about sleep.

Call 911 if your baby is not breathing, turns blue, or is limp.

use: Use as instructions for umbilical cord care.
body:
Cord care

The cord stump dries up and falls off in 1 to 3 weeks.

What to do:

- Keep it clean and dry.
- Give sponge baths until it falls off.
- Fold the diaper down below the stump.
- You do not need alcohol wipes.
- Do not pull it off, even if it is barely hanging on.

What is normal:

- Turning brown, then black, as it dries
- A few drops of dried blood or a little clear fluid at the base
- A mild smell as it dries

Call your baby's doctor if:

- Redness spreads onto the skin around it
- It has a bad smell or yellow or green pus
- It bleeds and does not stop with gentle pressure
- It has not fallen off by 3 weeks

Go to the ER if your baby has a fever of 100.4 F or higher.

use: Use as instructions about newborn jaundice.
body:
Newborn jaundice

Jaundice makes the skin and eyes look yellow. About 6 in 10 babies get it in the first week. Most cases are mild and go away on their own.

Your baby's bilirubin level was _ at _ hours old.

What helps:

- Feed often, at least 8 to 12 times a day.
- Do not put your baby in the sun to treat it. It does not work well and can burn.

Next bilirubin check or visit: _

Call your baby's doctor today if your baby:

- Looks more yellow, or the yellow spreads to the belly or legs
- Is very sleepy and hard to wake for feeds
- Is not feeding well
- Has fewer wet or dirty diapers than expected
- Has pale stools or dark urine

Go to the ER if your baby:

- Is very hard to wake
- Arches the back or has a high-pitched cry
- Has a fever of 100.4 F or higher

use: Use as instructions about normal newborn findings that worry parents.
body:
Normal newborn things

These are normal and go away on their own:

- Cone-shaped head after birth
- Soft spots on the head that pulse
- White, cheesy coating on the skin
- Fine hair on the back and shoulders
- Swollen breasts, in boys or girls
- Swollen labia or scrotum
- A little blood or mucus from the vagina in baby girls
- Eyes that cross sometimes, until about 4 months
- Peeling skin
- Lots of sneezing and hiccups
- A rash of small red spots with white centers in the first days
- Black, sticky first stools in the first 2 days

Call your baby's doctor right away if your baby:

- Has a fever of 100.4 F or higher. Take the temperature in the bottom.
- Will not eat
- Looks very yellow
- Grunts with every breath
- Has very pale skin
- Cannot be calmed
- Has fewer than 6 wet diapers a day after day 5

Fever in the first 3 months is an emergency. Go to the ER.

Call 911 if your baby has blue or gray lips or face.

use: Use as instructions about vitamin D drops for breastfed babies.
body:
Vitamin D drops for your baby

Breast milk is low in vitamin D. Vitamin D helps your baby build strong bones.

Does my baby need drops?

- Yes, if your baby drinks any breast milk, even if you also use formula.
- No, if your baby drinks about 32 ounces of formula a day.

When to start: in the first few days after birth.

Your baby's dose: _

How to give it:

- Read the label. Products are different strengths. More is not better.
- Put the drop on your nipple before a feed, or on a clean finger your baby is sucking.

Call your baby's doctor with questions about vitamin D or if your baby stops feeding well.

use: Use as instructions about infant car seat safety.
body:
Car seat safety

You need a car seat to take your baby home from the hospital.

How to use it:

- Keep the seat rear-facing, in the back seat, as long as your seat allows. This is usually past age 2.
- Never put it in front of an airbag.
- Put the straps at or below your baby's shoulders.
- Pull the straps tight enough that you cannot pinch extra strap at the shoulder.
- Put the chest clip at armpit level.
- No bulky coats under the straps. Buckle your baby in, then put a blanket over the top.
- Do not add padding or inserts that did not come with the seat.
- Do not use a seat that has been in a crash or is past its expiration date.

Get the install checked for free at many fire stations or hospitals, before your due date.

Call your baby's doctor with car seat questions.

use: Use as instructions after newborn circumcision or for care of the uncircumcised penis.
body:
Penis care

If your baby was circumcised:

- Put petroleum jelly on the tip with every diaper change for about 1 week.
- A yellow crust is normal. Do not wipe it off.
- If a plastic ring was used, it falls off on its own in 5 to 8 days. Do not pull it.
- Clean gently with warm water only.

If your baby is not circumcised:

- Do not pull back the foreskin. It separates on its own over several years.
- Wash the outside like any other skin.

Call your baby's doctor if:

- Bleeding is more than a few drops, or makes a spot bigger than a quarter
- Your baby has no wet diaper in 8 hours
- Redness or swelling spreads, or there is pus
- The plastic ring has not fallen off in 10 days

Go to the ER if your baby has a fever of 100.4 F or higher.

use: Use as instructions about normal infant crying and never shaking a baby.
body:
Crying and coping

All babies cry. Crying often gets worse around 2 weeks and peaks around 6 to 8 weeks. It gets better by 3 to 4 months. Some babies cry for hours, even when nothing is wrong.

Try:

- Feeding or burping
- A clean diaper
- Swaddling, only until your baby starts to roll
- Holding your awake baby on their side
- Rocking or swaying
- Shushing sounds or white noise
- A walk in the stroller or a car ride

If you feel angry or at your limit:

- Put your baby on the back in the crib.
- Leave the room and close the door.
- Take 10 minutes to calm down. Call someone you trust.
- It is OK to let your baby cry while you calm down.

Never shake a baby. Shaking can cause brain damage or death. Make sure everyone who cares for your baby knows this.

Call your baby's doctor if crying comes with fever, vomiting, poor feeding, or your baby seems in pain.

Call 911 if your baby is limp, hard to wake, or has trouble breathing.

use: Use for the A&P of a breastfeeding problem visit; keep the If groups that apply.
body:
#Breastfeeding difficulty: _low milk supply / nipple pain or damage / engorgement / mastitis spectrum / poor transfer or ankyloglossia / D-MER or aversion
Likely _ductal narrowing given focal tender induration, afebrile / perceived low supply given normal weight gain / nipple pain given shallow latch.
Infant _ days old, _ g, _% from birth weight. Voids _, stools _/24 hr. Feeds _/24 hr, _ min. LATCH _ or observed feed _. Pumping _ mL x _/day. Temp _, breast exam _.

DDx:
>_; most likely given _, _
>Bacterial mastitis, phlegmon, or abscess; considered but unlikely given _, breast US if firm mass or fluctuance
>Inflammatory breast cancer; considered but unlikely given _, imaging if recurrent at same site, urgent referral if suspected
>Perinatal depression or anxiety; considered but unlikely given EPDS _, _

- Observed feed: position, latch, swallowing, milk transfer
- EPDS _
- Lactation consult _
- F/u _

If low milk supply:

- Infant weight trend decides true vs perceived low supply; reassure if gaining well
- Milk removal 8 or more times/24 hr by feeds, hand expression, or pump
- Breast compression during feeds; hands-on pumping
- Check flange fit and suction; pumping should not hurt
- Assess causes: pregnancy, retained placenta, PCOS, hypothyroidism, breast surgery, glandular insufficiency, Sheehan after PPH, meds, heavy smoking or alcohol
- TSH _
- Galactogogues only after milk removal optimized; no herb proven, fenugreek may cause diarrhea or allergy
- START metoclopramide 10 mg PO TID x 7 to 14 days _
- Metoclopramide risks: sedation, anxiety, depression, EPS, rare tardive dyskinesia with boxed warning
- Domperidone not FDA approved; FDA advises against use for milk supply

If nipple pain or damage:

- Latch correction: deep latch, flanged lips, audible swallowing
- Observe a pumping session if pumping; adjust flange and suction
- Pain >2 wk: assess for dermatitis, infection, vasospasm, ankyloglossia
- START triamcinolone 0.1% ointment to nipple BID after feeds x 2 wk for dermatitis
- START mupirocin 2% ointment to fissures _ for weeping or yellow crust
- HSV or zoster lesions: no feeding or expressed milk from that side until healed

If vasospasm (blanching, purple color change, burning pain):

- Warmth after feeds, avoid cold to nipples
- START nifedipine ER 30 mg PO daily x 2 wk if pain persists

If suspected nipple candida (pink shiny nipple, infant thrush):

- Candida as a cause of deep breast pain is unproven; no sterilizing pump parts for yeast
- START miconazole or clotrimazole cream to nipples _
- Treat infant thrush if present _
- START fluconazole 200 mg PO once, then 100 mg PO daily x 7 to 10 days if resistant
- Avoid fluconazole with domperidone or erythromycin, QT risk

If engorgement:

- Feed on demand; do not pump to empty
- Reverse pressure softening and hand express small volumes before latch
- Ice and light lymphatic drainage
- START ibuprofen 800 mg PO q8h PRN

If ductal narrowing or inflammatory mastitis:

- CONT feeding on demand; no extra pumping, no pumping to empty
- No deep massage, heat, nipple shields, saline soaks, or castor oil
- Ice up to every hour, supportive bra
- START ibuprofen 800 mg PO q8h
- START acetaminophen 1000 mg PO q8h
- START sunflower or soy lecithin 5 to 10 g PO daily
- Nipple bleb: do not unroof; START triamcinolone 0.1% cream to bleb, wipe off before feeds
- No abx; abx raise risk of progression to bacterial mastitis
- Treat hyperlactation if present _

If bacterial mastitis (spreading erythema, systemic sxs >24 hr, or no response):

- START cephalexin 500 mg PO QID x 10 to 14 days
- START dicloxacillin 500 mg PO QID x 10 to 14 days, alternative first line
- CONT feeding from affected breast; milk is safe for infant
- Milk cx if no improvement after 48 hr of abx, recurrent, NICU infant, or high MRSA risk
- Admit for IV abx only if severe sepsis, cannot tolerate PO, or known MDRO

If MRSA or second line needed:

- START clindamycin 300 mg PO QID x 10 to 14 days
- START TMP-SMX DS 1 tab PO BID x 10 to 14 days
- Avoid TMP-SMX if infant G6PD deficiency; caution if infant preterm, jaundiced, or <30 days

If abscess or phlegmon:

- Breast US _
- Abscess: needle aspiration with cx or drain placement, breast surgery or IR _
- CONT breastfeeding from affected breast after drainage
- Abx 10 to 14 days, shorter if cellulitis resolves quickly
- Phlegmon may need longer abx; serial exam and US until resolved

If recurrent at same site:

- Milk cx before treating
- Breast imaging to exclude mass or granulomatous mastitis
- Progressive erythema, retraction, or peau d'orange: urgent breast surgery and oncology referral

If poor transfer or ankyloglossia:

- Full feeding assessment before any frenotomy
- No frenotomy if feeding normally
- Frenotomy referral only for significant functional impairment after failed nonsurgical support
- No post frenotomy stretching exercises
- Express after feeds to protect supply _

If D-MER or nursing aversion:

- D-MER: sudden dysphoria with letdown lasting minutes, distinct from PPD; psychoeducation
- Screen for perinatal mood and anxiety disorders
- Support feeding goals, including partial breastfeeding _

If supplementation needed:

- Order of choice: own expressed milk, donor milk, then formula
- Per feed: 2 to 10 mL first 24 hr, 5 to 15 mL at 24 to 48 hr
- Per feed: 15 to 30 mL at 48 to 72 hr, 30 to 60 mL at 72 to 96 hr
- Express once per supplement, or 8 or more times/24 hr if not at breast

use: Use for thyroid disease before, during, and after pregnancy.
body:
#Thyroid disease in pregnancy
_w_d, _hypothyroid on levothyroxine / subclinical hypothyroidism / TPO Ab positive, euthyroid / Graves disease / gestational thyrotoxicosis, _at / above / below goal.
TSH _, free T4 or total T4 _, total T3 _, TPO Ab _, TRAb _. Current dose _.

- Prenatal vitamin with 150 mcg iodine daily
- Separate levothyroxine from prenatal vitamin, iron, and calcium by 4 hr
- No TSH reference range for pregnancy: use upper limit about 4.0
- Total T4 in pregnancy: normal range about 1.5x nonpregnant after 16 wk
- No radioiodine uptake or scan in pregnancy
- Tell pediatrician about thyroid disease, antithyroid drugs, or high TRAb

If on levothyroxine before pregnancy:

- Preconception goal TSH between lower limit of normal and 2.5
- INCR. levothyroxine by 2 extra doses per week at positive pregnancy test (about 20-30%), patient to call clinic
- Goal TSH in lower half of trimester range, or <2.5 if no trimester range
- TSH every 4 wk until midgestation, then at least once near 30 wk
- Levothyroxine only; no T3 or desiccated thyroid
- After delivery: DECR. to prepregnancy dose, TSH at about 6 wk postpartum

If new TSH elevation in pregnancy:

- TPO Ab
- START levothyroxine _ mcg PO daily if TPO Ab positive with TSH above pregnancy range, or TSH >10
- Consider levothyroxine if TPO Ab positive with TSH >2.5, or TPO Ab negative with TSH above range but <10
- Low free T4 with normal TSH: no routine treatment
- Started in pregnancy, 50 mcg or less: may stop after delivery, TSH in 6 wk

If TPO Ab positive, euthyroid:

- TSH at confirmation of pregnancy, then every 4 wk through midpregnancy
- Prior pregnancy loss: consider levothyroxine 25-50 mcg PO daily
- Postpartum thyroiditis risk 33-50%

If low TSH in first trimester:

- Free T4 or total T4, total T3, TRAb
- Gestational transient thyrotoxicosis or hyperemesis: supportive care, IV fluids for dehydration, admit if needed
- No antithyroid drugs for hCG-mediated thyrotoxicosis; T4 normalizes by 14-18 wk
- START propranolol 10-40 mg PO q6-8h if symptomatic, short course

If Graves disease:

- TRAb at confirmation or diagnosis; repeat at 18-22 wk if elevated; again at 30-34 wk if elevated or on drug
- Euthyroid on methimazole 5-10 mg/day or less: consider stopping, TSH and free T4 every 1-2 wk
- Needs drug in first trimester: STOP methimazole, START PTU 50-150 mg PO TID through 16 wk
- Methimazole 5 mg daily = PTU 100 mg BID
- After 16 wk: CONT PTU or switch to methimazole; neither clearly preferred
- Lowest dose keeping free T4 or total T4 at or just above upper limit of normal
- TSH and free T4 or total T4 every 4 wk
- No levothyroxine plus antithyroid drug combination
- TRAb >3x upper limit or uncontrolled in second half: MFM, US for fetal HR, growth, fluid, goiter
- Prior RAI or thyroidectomy: TRAb in early pregnancy

If postpartum:

- Postpartum thyroiditis: thyrotoxic at 2-6 mo, hypothyroid at 3-12 mo
- TSH if postpartum depression or low milk supply _
- Treat subclinical or overt hypothyroidism if breastfeeding
- Breastfeeding: methimazole up to 20 mg/day or PTU up to 450 mg/day, lowest effective dose
- Defer pregnancy 6 mo after radioactive iodine

#Intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy
Likely ICP given _palm and sole itch worse at night, no rash / new 3rd trimester itch, bile acids >10 / recurrent itch, prior ICP.
Total bile acids _, peak _, AST _, ALT _, bilirubin _. BP _, platelets _. Skin: excoriations only, no rash _.

DDx:
>ICP; most likely given _, delivery timing by peak bile acids
>Preeclampsia or HELLP; considered but unlikely given _, BP, CBC, CMP, urine protein-creatinine ratio
>Acute fatty liver of pregnancy; considered but unlikely given _, glucose, PT/INR
>Other liver disease (viral hepatitis, biliary obstruction, drug cholestasis); considered but unlikely given _, _

- Total bile acids (random is fine) and AST/ALT
- Repeat bile acids and AST/ALT if itch persists with normal results
- START ursodiol 300 mg PO BID, TID, or 500 mg PO BID (10-15 mg/kg/day)
- INCR. ursodiol up to 21 mg/kg/day if itch not relieved in 1-2 wk
- START hydroxyzine 25 mg PO TID or QID PRN itch, limited benefit
- Antenatal testing once or twice weekly from dx, or from GA when abnormal testing would prompt delivery _
- Repeat bile acids only to guide delivery timing in severe cases, not weekly
- Do not deliver <37 wk for itch alone without elevated bile acids
- Continuous EFM in labor
- Counseled: recurrence up to 90% in future pregnancies, higher later risk of liver and gallbladder disease

If peak bile acids <40:

- Plan delivery toward 39w0d, within 36w0d to 39w0d

If peak bile acids 40-99:

- Consider earlier delivery within 36w0d to 39w0d

If peak bile acids 100 or more:

- Offer delivery at 36w0d, or at dx if later, more frequent antenatal testing
- Consider 34-36 wk if refractory itch, prior ICP stillbirth <36 wk, or worsening liver function

- START betamethasone 12 mg IM q24h x 2 doses
- Not at 34w0d or later if pregestational diabetes

If itch persists 4-6 wk postpartum:

- Repeat bile acids and LFTs, hepatology referral if still abnormal

use: Use for a Category II or III intrapartum fetal heart rate tracing, with intrauterine resuscitation and escalation.
body:
#Category _II / III FHR tracing
Likely _cord compression given recurrent variable decels / uteroplacental insufficiency given recurrent late decels / tachysystole given >5 ctx in 10 min with decels.
Baseline _ bpm, variability _, accels _, decels _. Contractions _ in 10 min, oxytocin _ milliunits/min. SVE _, station _. Maternal BP _, HR _, temp _, SpO2 _.

DDx:
>Cord compression or uteroplacental insufficiency; most likely given _, intrauterine resuscitation
>Maternal hypotension after neuraxial analgesia; considered but unlikely given _, BP check
>Intraamniotic infection; considered but unlikely given _, fetal tachycardia, maternal temp
>Uterine rupture or abruption; considered but unlikely given _, bradycardia, bleeding, prior cesarean

- High-risk features _: absent variability, prolonged minimal variability, new tachycardia, recurrent or repeated prolonged decels
- Protective features _: moderate variability, accels
- Confirm fetal, not maternal, HR with maternal pulse oximetry, FSE if still unclear
- Lateral or other maternal position change
- IV fluid bolus _ mL
- HOLD oxytocin, or DECR. rate, while decels or tachysystole persist
- No routine maternal O2 unless maternal hypoxia
- Scalp or vibroacoustic stimulation if minimal or absent variability without decels
- SVE for progress and station
- Attending notified _, reassess tracing q _ min _ local
- FSE contraindicated with unknown presenting part, HIV, active HSV, previa or vasa previa, fetal bleeding disorder

If recurrent variable decels:

- Amnioinfusion via IUPC _ local

If hypotension after neuraxial analgesia:

- START vasopressor IV per anesthesia
- DECR. epidural basal rate if hypotension recurs

If tachysystole with FHR changes despite holding oxytocin:

- START terbutaline 0.25 mg SQ once
- Restart oxytocin only after FHR reassuring and tachysystole resolved

If fetal tachycardia:

- Evaluate for intraamniotic infection, hyperthyroidism, dehydration, DKA

If recurrent decels with pushing in second stage:

- Push with every other contraction, change position
- Evaluate for operative vaginal delivery

If Category III, or Category II not responding:

- Immediate intrauterine resuscitation, attending, anesthesia and pediatrics to bedside
- Expedited delivery, operative vaginal or cesarean, if not resolved
- Sinusoidal pattern >30 min: no resuscitation helps, proceed to expedited delivery
- Suspected uterine rupture with bradycardia: emergent operative delivery
- Tetanic contraction: STOP oxytocin, START terbutaline 0.25 mg SQ while preparing for delivery

body:
#Pyelonephritis in pregnancy
Likely pyelonephritis given _fever, flank pain, CVA tenderness, pyuria / fever, nausea, vomiting, positive urine cx / preterm contractions with fever and pyuria.
GA _. Tmax _, HR _, BP _, RR _, SpO2 _. WBC _, platelets _, Hgb _, creatinine _. UA _, urine cx _, prior cx _.

>Pyelonephritis; most likely given _, IV abx
>Nephrolithiasis; considered but unlikely given _, renal US if not improving
>Intraamniotic infection; considered but unlikely given _, uterine tenderness, fetal tachycardia
>Renal abscess; considered but unlikely given _, imaging if no response by 72 hr

- Admit
- UA, urine cx before abx, do not wait for results to treat
- CBC, CMP
- Blood cx only if septic, rarely change management
- IV fluid hydration, watch SpO2, RR and lung exam for pulmonary edema or ARDS
- START ceftriaxone 1 g IV q24h
- Tailor abx to urine cx susceptibilities
- FHT and toco per GA _, watch for preterm labor
- When afebrile and improving, switch to PO abx per susceptibilities, 14 days total
- No nitrofurantoin or fosfomycin for treatment, poor kidney levels
- Urine cx after the 14-day course
- START suppression: nitrofurantoin 100 mg PO qHS or cephalexin 250-500 mg PO qHS
- Suppression for rest of pregnancy and 4-6 wk postpartum, recurrence up to 25% before delivery
- Consider monthly urine cx until delivery
- OB f/u in _ wk

If beta-lactam allergy, high anaphylaxis risk:

- START aztreonam 1 g IV q8-12h, with ID input

If another IV regimen needed:

- START ampicillin 2 g IV q6h plus gentamicin 1.5 mg/kg IV q8h or 5 mg/kg IV q24h

If no improvement by 72 hr:

- Review susceptibilities, resistance is the commonest cause of failure
- Renal US for obstruction, stone, or abscess

If ESBL, MRSA, or other resistant organism:

- ID consult

If G6PD deficiency:

- STOP nitrofurantoin, use cephalexin for suppression

If sepsis, hypoxia, or rising creatinine:

- Escalate level of care, notify attending and OBHWS

use: Use for the nursery A&P of an opioid-exposed newborn assessed with Eat, Sleep, Console.
body:
#Neonatal opioid withdrawal syndrome
Likely NOWS given _buprenorphine or methadone exposure, poor feeding, tremors / maternal opioid use, excessive crying, poor sleep / opioid exposure with sneezing, loose stools, high tone.
Exposure _, last maternal dose or use _, other substances _. _ hr of life. Eat _, sleep _, console _. Weight _ g, _ % change. Stools _.

DDx:
>NOWS; most likely given _, function-based assessment after feeds
>Hypoglycemia; considered but unlikely given _, glucose _
>_; considered but unlikely given _, _

- Observe 72 hr or more if chronic opioid exposure; up to 7 days if buprenorphine, methadone, or long-acting opioid
- Infant testing: urine, meconium, or umbilical cord tissue _ local
- Rooming-in with parent through observation and treatment
- Assess after feeds, every 3-4 hr. Do not wake to assess _
- Eat: 1 oz or more per feed, or breastfeeds well. Sleep: 1 hr or more. Console: within 10 min
- Nonpharmacologic care first for all: skin-to-skin, swaddle and hold, feed on demand
- Low-stimulation room, clustered care, parent at bedside
- Any domain failed from NOWS: increase nonpharmacologic care first, then reassess
- Higher-calorie or smaller, more frequent feeds if poor feeding or slow weight gain
- Daily weight, voids and stools
- Social work, reporting per state law _ local
- At d/c: referral to early intervention, home visiting, Early Head Start _
- PCP f/u _ days after d/c

If still failing despite maximal nonpharmacologic care:

- START morphine 0.03-0.05 mg/kg PO per dose, PRN or q3-4h _ local
- INCR. morphine if still failing _ local
- Alternative: START methadone 0.05-0.1 mg/kg PO q6h _ local
- Adjunct clonidine or phenobarbital if severe _ local
- DECR. opioid once controlled, monitor 24 hr or more after the last dose

If breastfeeding:

- Encourage breastfeeding on methadone or sublingual buprenorphine, any dose. It lowers NOWS severity
- Avoid breastfeeding during nonprescribed opioid use. Recent use: pump to keep supply if future abstinence is supported
- Support breastfeeding if nonprescribed use stopped by the delivery hospitalization (ABM)
- Discourage breastfeeding if active use or relapse in the last 30 days (AAP)
- Monitor infant for sedation during maternal methadone titration

desc: Infant of a hepatitis B positive or unknown status mother
use: Use for the nursery plan of a newborn whose mother is HBsAg positive or has no HBsAg result at delivery.
body:
#Perinatal hepatitis B exposure
Maternal HBsAg _positive / unknown, result pending _.
Birth weight _ g, born _ at _. Maternal HBV DNA _, HBeAg _. HepB vaccine given _, HBIG given _.

- START HepB vaccine, single-antigen, IM within 12 hr of birth
- Breastfeeding OK from birth
- If transferred: communicate vaccine and HBIG status to the receiving facility
- Final series dose no earlier than age 24 wk (164 days)

If mother HBsAg, HBeAg, or HBV DNA positive, or known chronic HBV:

- START HBIG 0.5 mL IM within 12 hr of birth, separate limb from vaccine
- Series: birth, 1-2 mo, 6 mo with single-antigen vaccine _
- Testing at 9-12 mo, or 1-2 mo after the final dose if delayed: HBsAg and anti-HBs
- Do not test before 9 mo. Do not test anti-HBc
- HBsAg negative, anti-HBs 10 mIU/mL or more: protected, no further care
- HBsAg negative, anti-HBs <10: START 1 more HepB dose, retest 1-2 mo later
- Still <10: 2 more doses to finish a 2nd series, retest 1-2 mo after the last
- Or a full 2nd 3-dose series, then retest 1-2 mo later
- No more doses if still <10 after 2 full series
- Infant HBsAg positive: refer to peds hepatology or ID _

If status unknown and birth weight 2000 g or more:

- Maternal HBsAg as soon as possible
- Vaccine within 12 hr, no HBIG while result pending
- Mother positive: START HBIG 0.5 mL IM as soon as possible, no later than age 7 days
- Mother negative: finish the series on the routine schedule

If status unknown and birth weight <2000 g:

- START HBIG 0.5 mL IM within 12 hr if maternal status cannot be found within 12 hr

If birth weight <2000 g:

- Birth dose does not count. 3 more doses, 4 total, starting at age 1 mo

If maternal status can never be known, such as safe surrender:

- Finish the series on the HBsAg-positive schedule, anti-HBs and HBsAg at 9-12 mo

body:
#Early-onset sepsis risk, GA _ wk
Likely _low EOS risk given well appearing after maternal intrapartum fever / low EOS risk given well appearing, GBS positive, inadequate IAP / EOS given tachypnea, tachycardia, or temperature instability. Calculator risk _ per 1000 after exam.
Maternal Tmax _, ROM _ hr, GBS _positive / negative / unknown. Intrapartum abx _, _ hr before delivery. Exam _well appearing / equivocal / clinical illness. HR _, RR _, temp _.

DDx:
>Early-onset sepsis; most likely given _, blood cx _
>TTN or other respiratory distress; considered but unlikely given _, CXR _
>_; considered but unlikely given _, _

- Risk approach: categorical, calculator, or serial exams _ local
- Calculator for 35 wk or more: GA, maternal Tmax, ROM hr, GBS status, intrapartum abx type and timing, exam category
- Equivocal: HR >160, RR >60, temp 100.4 F or higher or <97.5 F, or grunting, flaring, retracting without O2
- Equivocal means 1 sign >4 hr, or 2 or more signs >2 hr, even if intermittent
- Clinical illness: NCPAP, HFNC, or ventilation outside delivery room, pressors, encephalopathy, seizure, 5 min Apgar <5, O2 >2 hr
- Risk 1 per 1000 or more: blood cx and enhanced observation
- Risk 3 per 1000 or more: blood cx and START empiric abx
- Vitals q4h if risk at birth >1 per 1000 _ local
- Blood cx 1 mL or more, before abx
- CBC, CRP, surface or gastric cx cannot diagnose EOS. No urine cx at <72 hr
- LP if critically ill, unless it would compromise the infant or delay abx. LP if blood cx positive
- STOP abx when blood cx sterile at 36-48 hr, unless site-specific infection
- Do not continue abx for abnormal labs alone in a well-appearing infant
- Reassess and notify MD for any new equivocal sign

If maternal chorioamnionitis and well appearing:

- Categorical approach: blood cx and START empiric abx
- Calculator approach: enter maternal Tmax and ROM. The chorio diagnosis is not an input
- Serial exam approach: structured exams q4-6h through 48 hr _

If GBS positive with inadequate IAP and well appearing:

- No other risk: observe in hospital 48 hr or more
- ROM >18 hr or GA <37 wk: lab testing _

If empiric abx:

- START ampicillin 50 mg/kg IV q8h
- START gentamicin 4 mg/kg IV q24h if GA 35 wk or more and age 7 days or less
- Gentamicin levels _ local
- Critically ill: consider adding broader-spectrum coverage until cx results
- Meningitis: ampicillin dose per ID _ local

If blood cx positive:

- LP if not done. Daily blood cx until sterile
- Narrow abx to organism. Duration by organism, CSF results, and clearance _
- ID consult if meningitis, site-specific, resistant, or atypical organism

use: Use for the nursery A&P of a newborn with scalp swelling after birth, to sort caput, cephalohematoma, and subgaleal hemorrhage.
body:
#Newborn scalp swelling, _caput succedaneum / cephalohematoma / possible subgaleal hemorrhage
Likely _caput given swelling at presenting part, crosses sutures / cephalohematoma given swelling over one bone / subgaleal hemorrhage given fluctuant, diffuse swelling after vacuum.
Delivery _spontaneous / vacuum / forceps, extraction time _, pulls _, cup detachments _. Swelling _, crosses sutures _, fluctuant _. HR _, RR _, cap refill _. Head circumference _ cm at _, now _. Hct _, platelets _, coags _. TcB _.

DDx:
>_; most likely given _, _
>Subgaleal hemorrhage; considered but unlikely given _, serial head circumference and Hct
>Skull fracture; considered but unlikely given _, CT if step-off deformity

- Caput: fluid at the presenting part, crosses sutures, not fluctuant, does not enlarge. No treatment, usually resolves in 12-18 hr
- Cephalohematoma: under the periosteum, limited to one bone. Appears in first few days, resolves over weeks
- Cephalohematoma: no treatment. Watch for anemia and hyperbilirubinemia
- Scalp hematoma or significant bruising raises hyperbilirubinemia risk. TcB or TSB plan _
- Small risk of linear skull fracture under a cephalohematoma. Rarely calcifies into a bony mass
- Vitamin K IM given _
- After vacuum or forceps: HR, RR, color, activity, head circumference at 1 hr
- No hats, or remove often, to watch head shape
- Head circumference up 1 cm may mean about 40 mL of blood in the subgaleal space
- Vacuum >20 min, >3 pulls, or >2 cup detachments: cord gas, CBC, closer monitoring
- Closer monitoring: vitals hourly x 2 hr, then q2h x 6 hr, longer if concern
- Step-off deformity: CT head, neurosurgery if depressed fracture

If subgaleal hemorrhage suspected:

- Diffuse fluctuant swelling crossing sutures, may shift. Ear displacement or eyelid swelling as it grows
- Urgent senior or NICU review, continuous HR, RR, SpO2
- CBC and coags on admission, repeat _. Type and screen. Blood gas q2-4h
- Shock signs: HR >160, RR >60, falling Hct, lactate >3, cap refill >3 sec, pallor, low BP
- Normal HR and BP can be falsely reassuring. Shock can come before the bleed looks large
- START NS _ mL/kg IV bolus and PRBC as needed, correct coagulopathy _ local
- Transfer to NICU _

body:

body:

>Congenital CMV; considered but unlikely given _, CMV PCR if amniocentesis done

- Detailed anatomy US if onset <32w0d
- Offer amniocentesis with CMA if anomaly or polyhydramnios, or isolated FGR <32w0d
- CMV PCR on amniotic fluid if amniocentesis; no routine toxoplasma, rubella, or HSV testing

- BP each visit, preeclampsia labs if BP rises, especially if onset <32w0d
- MFM consult _
- No LMWH, sildenafil, or activity restriction to treat FGR
- No aspirin for FGR alone
- Kick counts, continuous EFM in labor
- Peds aware: monitor glucose, temperature, and feeding

If EFW <3rd %ile or elevated UA PI with EDF present:

- Deliver at 37w0d, or at dx if later

- UA Doppler 2-3x/wk, NST twice weekly or admit
- Deliver at 33w0d-34w0d, or at dx if later, MFM consult
- Consider cesarean

If REDV:

- Admit, NST at least 1-2x/day
- Deliver at 30w0d-32w0d, or at dx if later, MFM consult
- Consider cesarean

If oligohydramnios, preeclampsia, or chronic HTN also present:

- Deliver at 34w0d-37w6d, NST twice weekly or admit

If delivery likely <34w0d, or 34w0d-36w6d within 7 days:

- START betamethasone 12 mg IM q24h x 2 doses if no prior course
- Not at 34w0d or later if pregestational diabetes

If delivering <32w0d:

- START magnesium sulfate for neuroprotection, dosing _ local

body:
#Suspected fetal macrosomia
Likely LGA fetus given _EFW >90th, no diabetes / EFW >90th with GDM or DM / EFW 4,000 g or more.
GA by _. EFW _ g (_th %ile), AC _th %ile. MVP _ cm. GDM screen _, A1c _. Prior macrosomic infant _, BMI _.

- Check MVP or AFI for polyhydramnios
- Counseled: US and exam estimates of fetal weight are imprecise near term
- Counseled: risk of labor dystocia, shoulder dystocia, and birth injury rises with birth weight

- IOL timing _

- Tight glucose control, review log every _ wk
- Deliver at 39w0d-39w6d if well controlled on meds
- Deliver at 39w0d-40w6d if GDM well controlled on diet
- Deliver at 36w0d-38w6d if pregestational DM with vascular disease, poor control, or prior stillbirth
- GDM poorly controlled: individualized, late preterm or early term _

body:
#Amniotic fluid abnormality, _oligohydramnios / polyhydramnios
Likely _isolated oligohydramnios given MVP <2 cm / oligohydramnios with EFW <10th / idiopathic polyhydramnios given MVP 8 cm or more.
MVP _ cm, AFI _ cm. EFW _th %ile, anatomy _. ROM testing _. GDM screen _, antibody screen _, RPR _. Meds _.

>Fetal anomaly or aneuploidy; considered but unlikely given _, detailed anatomy US
>Diabetes, alloimmunization, or congenital infection; considered but unlikely given _, OGTT, antibody screen

- Oligohydramnios: MVP <2 cm or AFI 5 cm or less
- Polyhydramnios: MVP 8 cm or more or AFI 24 cm or more
- Detailed anatomy US and EFW
- MFM consult _

- Sterile speculum exam and ROM testing
- STOP NSAIDs and ACEi, _
- UA Doppler if EFW <10th
- Offer amniocentesis with CMA if anomaly or aneuploidy suspected
- NST or BPP once or twice weekly from dx or viability
- Fluid and growth US every 2-4 wk, every 2 wk if FGR
- Deliver at 36w0d-37w6d if isolated, or at dx if later

- OGTT if not done, antibody screen, syphilis serology
- Fetal anemia and infection workup if hydrops, hepatosplenomegaly, or placentomegaly
- Genetic counseling and offer CMA if anomaly, early onset, or severe

- Amnioreduction only if severe with severe discomfort or dyspnea
- Repeat US if fluid rising or growth in question

- Deliver mild idiopathic at 39w0d-40w6d
- Check presentation at labor onset, malpresentation and dysfunctional labor more common
- Peds present at delivery, PPH readiness

- NST or BPP once or twice weekly from 32w0d-34w0d, or at dx if later

If MVP 16 cm or more or AFI 35 cm or more:

- Deliver at a tertiary center

body:
#Short cervix on TVUS
CL _ mm on TVUS at _w_d, _singleton / twins, _no prior / prior spontaneous preterm birth at _w.
Contractions _, bleeding _, LOF _. SVE or speculum _. Peanut allergy _.

- Base treatment only on TVUS CL
- Short cervix: CL 25 mm or less before 24w0d
- Do not prescribe 17-OHPC, including compounded

- Preterm labor precautions reviewed

- Or START progesterone 8% gel 90 mg vaginally daily until 36w6d

- Vaginal progesterone as above is an option

If no prior sPTB and CL 10-25 mm without dilation:

- No cerclage

If CL <15 mm:

- SVE or speculum exam for dilation, candidacy for exam-indicated cerclage

If no prior sPTB and CL <10 mm:

- Consider cerclage even without dilation

If prior sPTB <34w0d and CL <25 mm before 24w0d:

- Vaginal progesterone also an option

HSV NAAT _, type _. Type-specific IgG _. Last outbreak _. Partner HSV status _.

- Or START acyclovir 400 mg PO TID from 36w0d until delivery

- Cesarean if genital lesions or prodrome at labor onset
- No cesarean for nongenital lesions only (back, thigh, buttock)

- Peds aware of maternal HSV status at delivery

- Or START acyclovir 800 mg PO BID x 5 days

- Or START acyclovir 400 mg PO TID x 7-10 days

body:
#HIV in pregnancy
_Suppressed / not suppressed on ART at _w_d, VL _ copies/mL on _.
ART regimen _. CD4 _. Adherence _. HBV _, HCV _, RPR _.

- CONT current ART if suppressed and tolerated, do not interrupt
- Co-manage with HIV specialist _
- National Perinatal HIV/AIDS Clinical Consultation Center 888-448-8765 for clinician questions
- HIV VL at first visit, 2-4 wk after starting or changing ART, monthly until undetectable, then every 3 mo
- HIV VL at 34w0d-36w0d to plan delivery
- Screen for syphilis, HBV, HCV, TB, and HSV
- Infant feeding counseling started early, continued after birth
- Avoid fetal scalp electrode and operative vaginal delivery
- CONT oral ART on schedule in labor
- Avoid methylergonovine if on a protease inhibitor or cobicistat, use oxytocin, misoprostol, or carboprost for PPH
- Peds: infant ARV within 6 hr of birth, regimen by transmission risk _
- CONT ART postpartum, HIV specialist f/u in _ wk

If not on ART:

- START ART promptly with HIV specialist, regimen _

If VL >1,000 copies/mL or unknown near delivery:

- Scheduled cesarean at 38w0d
- START zidovudine 2 mg/kg IV over 1 hr, then 1 mg/kg/hr IV until delivery
- Begin zidovudine 3 hr before cesarean, or at admission if in labor
- If ROM or labor before cesarean, mode of delivery with consult _

If VL 1,000 copies/mL or less on ART:

- No cesarean for HIV alone, deliver at 39w0d or later
- IV zidovudine not required

If VL 50-999 copies/mL near delivery:

- Consider IV zidovudine as above, benefit uncertain

If planning to breastfeed:

- Breastfeeding risk <1% but not zero with sustained undetectable VL
- Formula or pasteurized donor milk removes postnatal risk
- Close maternal VL and infant f/u, feeding plan _

use: Use for a pregnant patient with reactive syphilis serology or confirmed syphilis.
body:
#Syphilis in pregnancy
_Primary / secondary / early latent / late latent or unknown duration syphilis at _w_d.
RPR 1:_ on _, treponemal test _. Prior RPR and treatment _. Neuro, eye, or ear sxs _. Penicillin allergy _. HIV _.

- Oklahoma law: syphilis test at first prenatal exam
- Rescreen all at 28 wk and at delivery (ACOG)
- Rescreen at 28 wk and delivery if high-prevalence area or at risk (CDC)
- Test after any fetal death at 20 wk or later
- HIV test at dx
- Neuro, eye, and ear exam, CSF and specialist eval if sxs
- Use benzathine penicillin G (Bicillin L-A), not Bicillin C-R
- Report to OSDH, partner services _
- Presumptive tx for partners exposed within 90 days of early syphilis, even if seronegative
- Partners exposed >90 days: test, treat if serology unavailable and f/u uncertain
- Counseled: Jarisch-Herxheimer fever, headache, myalgia within 24 hr, may cause contractions or decreased FM
- Quantitative RPR at delivery for comparison with infant

If primary, secondary, or early latent:

- START benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM once
- Second dose 2.4 million units IM 1 wk later can be given

If late latent or unknown duration:

- START benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly x 3 doses
- If gap >9 days between doses, repeat the full course

If neurosyphilis, ocular, or otic syphilis:

- START aqueous penicillin G 3-4 million units IV q4h, 18-24 million units/day, x 10-14 days

If penicillin allergy:

- No proven alternative in pregnancy, penicillin skin test or oral challenge
- Desensitize, then treat with penicillin G
- No doxycycline, azithromycin, erythromycin, or ceftriaxone in place of penicillin

If diagnosed at 20w0d or later:

- Fetal US for hydrops, thick placenta, or other signs, do not delay treatment
- MFM consult if US abnormal, may need a second dose

If treated at 24w0d or earlier:

- Repeat RPR no sooner than 8 wk after tx, then at delivery

If treated after 24w0d:

- Repeat RPR at delivery
- Fourfold titer rise sustained >2 wk means reinfection or failure, retreat _

If delivering:

- Peds: infant serum RPR (not cord blood), exam, placenta pathology
- Maternal tx adequate only if penicillin regimen started 30 days or more before delivery
- No discharge of mother or infant until maternal serology documented

use: Use for a pregnant patient with a positive hepatitis B surface antigen.
body:
#Chronic hepatitis B in pregnancy
HBsAg positive at _w_d, HBV DNA _ IU/mL, _not on / on antiviral therapy.
HBeAg _, ALT _. Cirrhosis eval _. HCV _, HIV _. Prior HBV care _.

- Confirm positive HBsAg with neutralizing test per lab
- HBV DNA, HBeAg, ALT now
- Cirrhosis eval by exam and/or liver US
- HBV DNA at 26-28 wk if not on treatment
- Refer to hepatology or ID _
- Report to perinatal hepatitis B prevention program _
- Test and vaccinate household and sex contacts if susceptible
- No cesarean for HBV alone
- Breastfeeding safe, including on tenofovir
- Peds: HBIG and HBV vaccine within 12 hr of birth, even if mother on antiviral
- Peds: vaccine doses at 1 and 6 mo, HBsAg and anti-HBs at 9-12 mo

If HBV DNA >200,000 IU/mL:

- START tenofovir disoproxil fumarate 300 mg PO daily at 28-32 wk through delivery
- Or START tenofovir alafenamide 25 mg PO daily (SMFM), TDF preferred for pregnancy safety data (AASLD)

If already on entecavir or another antiviral:

- Switch to TDF or TAF for pregnancy and postpartum

If tenofovir only for transmission and no other indication:

- STOP tenofovir at delivery, or CONT per hepatology
- HBV DNA and ALT every 1-3 mo for 6 mo after stopping
- Restart antiviral if ALT 5x ULN or more

desc: Pregnancy of unknown location, suspected ectopic
use: Use for a positive pregnancy test with no intrauterine or ectopic pregnancy on transvaginal US, including methotrexate and surgical planning.
body:
#Pregnancy of unknown location
Likely PUL given _bleeding, + hCG, no IUP on TVUS / one-sided pelvic pain, no IUP or mass on TVUS / hCG plateau or slow rise, no IUP.
Serial hCG _ >> _ in 48 hr (_%). TVUS: uterus _, adnexa _, free fluid _. BP _, HR _, Hgb _, Rh _.

DDx:
>Early viable IUP; most likely given _, repeat hCG and TVUS
>Failed IUP; considered but unlikely given _, hCG fall of 21% or more in 48 hr suggests it
>Ectopic pregnancy; considered but unlikely given _, serial hCG and TVUS until resolved

- Serial quantitative hCG q48h with TVUS until IUP seen or hCG undetectable
- Expected 48-hr hCG rise in viable IUP: 49% or more if initial <1500, 40% if 1500-3000, 33% if >3000
- Slower rise or any fall: failed IUP or ectopic
- Discriminatory level up to 3500 if pregnancy desired; most IUPs visible by 1500
- No IUP with hCG above discriminatory level: concern for failed IUP or ectopic
- CBC, blood type and Rh
- Ectopic precautions reviewed: heavy bleeding, severe or one-sided pain, shoulder pain, dizziness or fainting

If undesired pregnancy or viable IUP excluded:

- Uterine aspiration for chorionic villi; villi present, no further workup and no methotrexate
- No villi: treat as ectopic, or repeat hCG in 24 hr to confirm 50% or more fall

If ectopic, stable and unruptured, methotrexate candidate:

- CBC and CMP before dosing
- Methotrexate contraindications: renal insufficiency, moderate to severe anemia, leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, liver disease, alcohol use disorder, active PUD, breastfeeding
- START methotrexate 50 mg/m2 IM once on day 1 if hCG <3600, single-dose regimen
- START methotrexate 50 mg/m2 IM on day 1 and day 4 if hCG higher, especially >5000, two-dose regimen
- hCG on day 1, 4 and 7; a rise from day 1 to 4 is common
- Day 4 to 7 fall >15%: hCG weekly until undetectable
- START repeat methotrexate 50 mg/m2 IM, or surgery, if single-dose day 4 to 7 fall is 15% or less
- Surgery if hCG does not fall after 2 single doses
- START methotrexate 50 mg/m2 IM on day 7 if two-dose fall is 15% or less, again day 11 if needed
- Surgery if two-dose day 11 to 14 fall is still 15% or less
- HOLD folic acid, including prenatal vitamin, and NSAIDs during treatment
- Avoid opioids and alcohol, which mask rupture; avoid intercourse, vigorous exercise and sun
- Pain 2-3 days after dose is common; rupture risk persists until hCG undetectable
- Avoid pregnancy until 1 ovulatory cycle after hCG undetectable; some advise 3 mo
- hCG may take up to 8 wk to clear; no evidence methotrexate affects fertility

If asymptomatic with low, falling hCG and reliable f/u:

- Expectant management with hCG q48h; 88% resolve if initial hCG 200 or less
- Medical or surgical treatment if hCG fall is insufficient

If unstable, peritoneal signs, or suspected rupture:

- Emergent OB/GYN consult for laparoscopy, salpingostomy or salpingectomy
- Transfer _ local

If extrauterine cardiac activity, cul-de-sac fluid, hCG >5000, or mass >4 cm:

- Urgent OB/GYN referral for surgery
- Also refer if methotrexate contraindicated or failed, poor f/u access, or transfusion declined

If Rh negative and ectopic confirmed:

- START Rh immune globulin 50 mcg IM within 72 hr, or 300 mcg if 50 mcg not stocked (ACOG)
- HOLD Rh immune globulin if solely medical management (NICE)

If PUL resolves as failed IUP before 12 wk:

- Rh testing and Rh immune globulin not routine, may offer

desc: Breech presentation at term, ECV counseling
use: Use at 36 weeks or later when the fetus is breech, to document external cephalic version counseling and delivery planning.
body:
#Breech presentation
Breech at _w_d, _frank / complete / footling or incomplete on bedside US.
Placenta _, DVP _ cm, EFW _, prior uterine surgery _, Rh _.

- Offer ECV near term if no contraindication; check presentation from 36w0d
- ECV success about 58% overall, higher with multiparity
- After successful ECV, about 97% are cephalic at birth; reversion about 2%
- Serious complications about 0.24%, emergency cesarean from ECV about 0.35%
- Transient FHR changes 5-10%, usually resolve without intervention
- ECV contraindicated if previa, labor, classical uterine scar, major fetal anomaly, abnormal FHR, or other bar to vaginal birth
- ROM is a relative contraindication, cord prolapse risk
- One prior cesarean: ECV reasonable, success 50-100%, no uterine rupture in reported series
- ECV only where cesarean is readily available, L&D _ local
- NST or BPP before and after ECV
- START terbutaline 0.25 mg SQ once, 15-30 min before ECV
- Neuraxial analgesia with tocolysis is reasonable to raise success _
- Labor precautions: go to L&D right away with ROM or labor while breech
- Return weekly

If Rh negative and unsensitized:

- START Rh immune globulin 300 mcg IM within 72 hr after ECV, whether or not it succeeds

If ECV declined, failed, or contraindicated:

- Planned cesarean at 39w0d or later, bedside US for presentation that day
- Planned vaginal breech birth reasonable under hospital protocol with experienced clinician _
- Vaginal breech: perinatal or neonatal death or serious short-term morbidity may be higher than with planned cesarean

body:
#Chronic hypertension in pregnancy
_At / above / below goal on current regimen, home average _.
BP _. Baseline creatinine _, AST/ALT _, platelets _, UPCR _. EFW _.

- Goal BP <140/90; start or titrate meds at 140/90 or higher
- START labetalol 100 mg PO BID
- INCR. labetalol by 100 mg BID every 2-3 days to goal, max 2400 mg/day
- STOP ACEi, ARB, renin inhibitor, and mineralocorticoid receptor antagonist
- Baseline CBC, AST, ALT, creatinine, BUN, electrolytes, urine protein-creatinine ratio
- 24-hr urine protein if UPCR elevated
- ECG or echo if signs of decreased cardiac function
- START aspirin 81 mg PO daily from 12-28 wk until delivery
- Growth US in 3rd trimester
- Antenatal testing weekly from 32w0d if on meds
- Expectant management past 39w0d only after risk-benefit review, with surveillance
- Home BP log _
- Repeat CBC, CMP, UPCR if BP rises or new sxs, to assess superimposed preeclampsia
- f/u _ wk

If asthma, heart block, bradycardia, or decreased cardiac function:

- START nifedipine ER 30 mg PO daily instead of labetalol, if no tachycardia
- INCR. nifedipine ER every 7-14 days to goal, max 120 mg/day

If poorly controlled or with comorbidities:

- Antenatal testing from dx, frequency _

If BP 160/110 or higher, confirmed:

- L&D now, treat within 30-60 min with IV labetalol, IV hydralazine, or PO nifedipine

If not on meds:

- Deliver 38w0d to 39w6d

If controlled on meds:

use: Use for anemia found on prenatal CBC, with iron dosing, IV iron criteria and hemoglobinopathy screening.
body:
#Anemia in pregnancy
Likely iron deficiency anemia given _low Hgb, ferritin <30 at 1st visit / low Hgb and MCV at 24-28 wk / fatigue, dizziness, low Hgb.
Hgb _ at _w_d, MCV _, ferritin _. Hgb electrophoresis _.

DDx:
>Iron deficiency anemia; most likely given ferritin _, treat with iron
>Thalassemia trait; considered but unlikely given _, Hgb electrophoresis, genetic testing if alpha suspected
>Folate or B12 deficiency; considered but unlikely given MCV _, folate and B12 if macrocytic

- Anemia: Hgb <11 in 1st or 3rd trimester, Hgb <10.5 in 2nd trimester
- Ferritin <30 confirms iron deficiency
- CONT prenatal vitamin with 27 mg iron daily
- Ferritin with CBC at 1st visit and 24-28 wk if risk factors: prior iron deficiency, diabetes, smoking, IBD, vegetarian diet, bariatric surgery
- More risk factors: abnormal uterine bleeding history, underweight or obese, HIV, multiparity, pregnancy interval <6 mo
- START ferrous sulfate 325 mg (65 mg elemental iron) PO every other day
- Take iron on an empty stomach if tolerated, with vitamin C or orange juice
- Take iron 2 hr apart from milk, calcium, and antacids; not with tea, coffee, or high-fiber foods
- Iron-rich foods: fortified cereal, beans, lentils, tofu, beef, with a vitamin C food
- Stool softener PRN constipation; black stools expected
- Repeat CBC and ferritin in 2-4 wk on oral iron
- Adequate response: Hgb up 1 g/dL in 14 days, or ferritin normal in 3 wk
- Adequate response: CONT oral iron, repeat CBC at 24-28 wk or in 3rd trimester
- CONT iron after Hgb normalizes to rebuild stores _
- Hgb electrophoresis if not done, or if MCV <80 with normal ferritin
- Partner testing and genetic counseling if hemoglobinopathy carrier
- If treated this pregnancy: CBC and type and screen on L&D admission
- Screen for postpartum anemia before discharge or at the postpartum visit

If 1st trimester Hgb <9:

- Hgb electrophoresis
- Consider IV iron directly if risk factors for anemia

If 2nd or 3rd trimester Hgb 10-10.9:

- Oral iron every other day or IV iron, by clinical picture

If 2nd or 3rd trimester Hgb <10 or ferritin <30, or inadequate response to oral iron:

- START ferumoxytol 510 mg IV over 15 min x 2 doses, 3-8 days apart, preferred
- Alt: iron sucrose 500 mg IV x 2 doses, 24 hr or more apart
- Alt: LMW iron dextran 1000 mg IV once after 25 mg test dose; only if adherence or transport is a barrier
- Goal 1000-1500 mg total
- Repeat CBC and ferritin 4 wk after the last dose
- No 1st trimester safety data for IV iron

If MCV >100:

- B12 and folate

desc: Rh negative and red cell alloimmunization
use: Use at prenatal visits for an Rh negative patient or a positive red cell antibody screen.
body:
#Rh negative and red cell alloimmunization
_Rh negative, antibody screen negative / Rh negative with anti-D / non-D red cell antibody present.
Type _, antibody _, titer _ on _ (prior _). Partner type or antigen _. Prior affected pregnancy _. RhIG given _.

- ABO, Rh D type and antibody screen at first visit
- Repeat antibody screen at 28 wk before Rh immune globulin

If Rh negative and unsensitized:

- START Rh immune globulin 300 mcg IM at 28 wk
- HOLD antenatal dose if partner Rh D negative and paternity certain _
- START Rh immune globulin 300 mcg IM within 72 hr of delivery if newborn Rh positive
- Some benefit possible up to 28 days postpartum if 72 hr missed
- Cord blood type at delivery; rosette screen, Kleihauer-Betke if positive
- START extra Rh immune globulin 300 mcg IM per 30 mL fetal whole blood if large bleed, up to 5 doses in 24 hr
- START Rh immune globulin 300 mcg IM within 72 hr after ECV, abdominal trauma, amnio or CVS, bleeding after 20 wk, or 2nd or 3rd trimester fetal death
- START repeat 300 mcg IM if undelivered 12 wk after 28-wk dose (label), or wait for postpartum dose (ACOG)
- Weak D phenotype: RHD genotyping; weak D type 1, 2, or 3 does not need Rh immune globulin
- CONT Rh immune globulin prophylaxis if anti-D is passive from a recent dose

If sensitized, antibody screen positive:

- HOLD Rh immune globulin once sensitized to D, no benefit
- Antibody ID and titer; anti-D, Kell, c, C, E, e, Duffy and Kidd can cause HDFN; ABO does not
- Partner type and antigen status if paternity certain; antigen negative, no further testing
- Cell-free DNA fetal RHD if partner antigen positive or unknown _
- Titers every 2-4 wk after 20 wk while below critical titer
- Critical titer is lab-specific, usually 1:8 to 1:32
- MFM referral at critical titer
- MCA peak systolic velocity q1-2 wk once titer critical; >1.5 MoM suggests moderate to severe fetal anemia
- MCA >1.5 MoM: MFM for cordocentesis and intrauterine transfusion
- Deliver 37w0d to 38w6d if no intrauterine transfusion needed; timing _ if transfused

If anti-K (Kell):

- MFM referral at any titer; titer predicts fetal anemia poorly

If prior affected fetus or newborn:

- MFM referral; titers do not reflect risk, follow MCA Dopplers

use: Use when labor is slow or stalled, to document the stage, contraction adequacy, and the plan to continue labor or deliver.
body:
#Labor protraction or arrest, _first stage / second stage
Likely _prolonged latent phase given <6 cm, >16 hr / active phase arrest given ROM, no change 4 hr / second-stage arrest given no descent.
SVE _ cm, _ station, position _. Membranes _intact / ruptured at _. Ctx every _ min, MVU _, oxytocin _ milliunits/min for _ hr. Epidural _. Pushing since _. EFW _. FHT category _I / II / III.

DDx:
>Inadequate uterine activity; most likely given _, IUPC and oxytocin
>Malposition, OP or OT; considered but unlikely given _, manual rotation
>Cephalopelvic disproportion or LGA fetus; considered but unlikely given _, _

- Active phase starts at 6 cm; apply active phase arrest criteria only from 6 cm
- Protracted active phase: <1 cm change in 2 hr
- Slow but progressive active labor, change at least every 4 hr, reassuring status: not an indication for cesarean
- AROM if membranes intact
- IUPC if ROM with protracted active labor, or contractions not traced externally
- START oxytocin _low-dose, 2 milliunits/min, up by 2 q30 min / high-dose, 4 milliunits/min, up by 4 q30 min
- Upright positions, ambulation, continuous labor support
- IV fluids 250 mL/hr rather than 125 mL/hr if nulliparous and oral intake restricted _
- Neuraxial analgesia offered
- Continue labor vs cesarean discussed with patient, preferences _

If <6 cm:

- Prolonged latent phase is >16 hr; most enter active phase with expectant management, AROM, or oxytocin
- No cesarean for prolonged latent phase if maternal and fetal status reassuring

If induced and still latent:

- Failed induction only after 12-18 hr of oxytocin after ROM, longer individualized (ACOG)
- Failed induction after 24 hr of oxytocin, with AROM if feasible (faculty)

If 6 cm or more with ROM:

- Active phase arrest: no change despite 4 hr adequate ctx (MVU >200), or 6 hr oxytocin with inadequate ctx
- Cesarean for active phase arrest

If complete:

- Push at complete dilation, no delayed pushing; delay raises PPH, chorioamnionitis, and neonatal acidemia
- Prolonged second stage: >3 hr pushing if nulliparous, >2 hr if multiparous (ACOG)
- Second-stage arrest: 4 hr nulliparous, 3 hr multiparous with epidural; 3 hr and 2 hr without (faculty)
- Past these limits: individualize by descent, clinical factors, and patient preference
- Arrest can be called earlier if no descent or rotation despite adequate ctx, pushing, and time
- Manual rotation if OP or OT
- Assess for operative vaginal delivery before cesarean for second-stage arrest
- Second-stage cesarean: more endometritis and hysterotomy extensions, plan resources

Low-risk nulliparous at _w_d, no maternal or fetal indication for delivery, dated by _.

body:
#Abnormal placentation or prior uterine surgery
Likely _placenta previa given placenta covering os / placenta accreta spectrum given prior cesarean, US signs / vasa previa given vessels over os on Doppler.
GA _w_d by _. Placental edge _ mm from os. Prior uterine surgery _none / classical cesarean / myomectomy requiring cesarean / uterine rupture, op note _. Bleeding _. Hgb _, Rh _.

- MFM referral _
- No digital cervical exam until previa excluded; speculum exam is safe
- RhoGAM 300 mcg IM if Rh negative and bleeding
- Precautions: come to L&D for any bleeding, contractions or leaking fluid
- Do not delay an indicated late preterm delivery for steroids

If placenta previa or low-lying placenta:

- TVUS at 32 wk; repeat TVUS at 36 wk if still previa or low-lying
- Transfer care if previa persists past 32 wk _

- ROM at a viable GA: cesarean

- Review op note for extent and location of the myomectomy
- Deliver at 37w0d-38w6d; 36w0d-37w0d if extensive or complicated myomectomy

body:
#S/p _ at _w_d, PPD _

- Routine postpartum care

#Acute blood loss anemia

Postpartum Hgb _, pre-delivery _. Symptoms _.

- Ferrous sulfate 325 mg PO daily or every other day
- IV iron if Hgb under 7-8 or oral iron not tolerated
- Transfuse if Hgb under 7 with symptoms or ongoing bleeding
- Docusate 100 mg PO BID while on iron
- Recheck CBC if symptomatic or Hgb dropped more than 3 g/dL

#Gestational diabetes

- Stop insulin and glucose checks after delivery unless hyperglycemia persists
- 75 g 2-hour OGTT at 4-12 weeks postpartum

#Gestational hypertension

- BP q4h, treat if 150/100 or more
- Preeclampsia warning signs reviewed
- BP check within 7-10 days, within 72 h if severe

#GBS positive

- Infant observation per adequacy of intrapartum prophylaxis, at least 36 h if prophylaxis inadequate

#Postpartum endometritis
Likely endometritis given _fever, uterine tenderness, after cesarean / fever, foul lochia, soft tender uterus / fever 38 C or more, 2 days, no source.
Tmax _, HR _, WBC _. Fundal tenderness _, lochia _. UA _.

DDx:
>Endometritis; most likely given _, IV clindamycin plus gentamicin
>UTI, wound or perineal infection; considered but unlikely given _, UA, urine cx, wound exam

- START clindamycin 900 mg IV q8h plus gentamicin 5 mg/kg IV q24h
- CONT IV abx until afebrile 48 hr, then STOP, no oral abx needed
- START ampicillin 1 g IV q6h if no improvement by 48 hr or enterococcus suspected
- CT abdomen and pelvis if fever persists 48-72 hr, for abscess or septic pelvic thrombophlebitis

#Postpartum constipation
Last BM _, PPD _, Bristol type _. Laceration _ degree, opioids _, iron _, breastfeeding _.

- START polyethylene glycol 17 g PO daily, titrate to soft stool, compatible with breastfeeding
- Fluids, fiber, early walking

If 3rd or 4th degree laceration:

- START polyethylene glycol 17 g PO daily x _ wk, goal soft stool without straining
- Laxative, not a constipating regimen: earlier, less painful first BM with the same continence at 3 mo

If opioid prescribed at discharge:

- CONT polyethylene glycol 17 g PO daily, scheduled, while taking the opioid

Dispo: discharge home _ h after delivery.

Reactive criteria: 32 weeks or later, 2 accelerations of 15 bpm or more for 15 sec or more within 20 min; before 32 weeks, 10 bpm for 10 sec. Baseline variability minimal to moderate.

use: Use for suspected intraamniotic infection or intrapartum fever.
body:
#Intraamniotic infection, suspected

Maternal temp _ at _. Fetal tachycardia _, maternal WBC _, purulent fluid _. Fever 39.0 C or higher once, or 38.0-38.9 C with one additional clinical risk factor.

- Ampicillin 2 g IV q6h plus gentamicin 5 mg/kg IV q24h, or 2 mg/kg IV then 1.5 mg/kg IV q8h

- Acetaminophen 1 g PO q6h PRN fever
- Continue labor, no indication for immediate cesarean

- After cesarean: one more dose plus clindamycin 900 mg IV or metronidazole 500 mg IV once
- Notify pediatrics at delivery

Temp 38.0-38.9 C without other findings.

- Recheck temp in 30 min, treat as intraamniotic infection if persistent

use: Use in OB triage for preterm contractions.
body:
#Rule out preterm labor at _w_d

Contractions every _ min. Leakage of fluid _, bleeding _, discharge _, intercourse in 24 h _. FHT category _I / II / III, baseline _. Prior preterm birth _, prior cesarean _, steroids this pregnancy _.

- Sterile speculum exam before digital exam
- fFN collected before digital exam or lubricant if 24w0d-34w6d, cervix under 3 cm, no bleeding and no intercourse in 24 h
- ROM testing if indicated
- UA with culture, GC and chlamydia, vaginal profile, GBS culture
- SVE after speculum, repeat in 1-2 h for cervical change
- Transvaginal cervical length if under 34 weeks: under 20 mm high risk, over 30 mm preterm labor unlikely

Preterm labor diagnosed, cervical change, 2 cm or more, or positive fFN with short cervix:

- Consult OBHWS, admit
- Betamethasone 12 mg IM q24h x2 doses if 24w0d-33w6d
- START betamethasone 12 mg IM q24h x 2 doses if 34w0d-36w6d, singleton, delivery risk within 7 days, no prior course
- No late preterm betamethasone with pregestational diabetes or chorioamnionitis, and no tocolysis to complete it
- Late preterm betamethasone given: notify NICU, neonatal hypoglycemia risk
- Nifedipine 20 mg PO once then 10-20 mg PO q4-6h up to 48 h to allow steroids, if 24w0d-33w6d and no contraindication
- START indomethacin 50-100 mg PO once then 25 mg PO q4-6h, max 48 h, if under 32 weeks, instead of nifedipine
- Avoid indomethacin with asthma, bleeding disorder or significant renal disease; ductal constriction and oligohydramnios risk
- No tocolysis: fetal demise, lethal anomaly, nonreassuring FHT, severe preeclampsia or eclampsia, unstable bleeding, chorioamnionitis
- PPROM without infection: tocolysis only for steroids or transport
- START magnesium sulfate if under 32 weeks and delivery imminent, for neuroprotection
- Magnesium regimen _ local: 4 g IV over 15-30 min then 1 g/h, or 6 g IV load then 2 g/h
- GBS prophylaxis if GBS unknown or positive

Preterm labor ruled out, negative fFN or cervical length over 30 mm and no cervical change:

- Discharge with preterm labor precautions
- OB follow-up in 1 week

use: Use for intrapartum glucose management in gestational diabetes.
body:
#Gestational diabetes, _A1 / A2, intrapartum

Diagnosed by _ GTT. Intrapartum glucose goal 70 to 110.

- POC glucose q2h, q1h if on insulin
- Rotating fluid protocol: glucose 100 or higher, LR at 125 mL/hr; glucose under 100, D5LR at 125 mL/hr
- Glucose over 110: recheck in 30 minutes, if still over 110 start regular insulin IV infusion per protocol _ local

Insulin infusion rate, verify against local protocol _:

- Glucose 111 to 130: 1 unit/hour
- Glucose 131 to 150: 2 units/hour
- Glucose 151 to 170: 3 units/hour
- Glucose 171 to 190: 4 units/hour
- Glucose over 190: check ketones and notify physician

Postpartum:

- Stop insulin after delivery, check fasting and postprandial glucose _
- 75 g 2-hour OGTT at 4 to 12 weeks postpartum

use: Use for the plan for nausea and vomiting of pregnancy in clinic or triage.
body:
#Nausea and vomiting of pregnancy

PUQE _, _mild / moderate / severe. Weight _, ketones _, tolerating PO _. Heartburn or reflux _.

- Small frequent bland meals, high carbohydrate and low fat, avoid trigger smells and foods
- Salty foods in the morning and sour or tart liquids may be better tolerated
- Switch prenatal vitamin to folic acid 0.4 to 1 mg PO daily until nausea improves _
- Ginger 250 mg PO QID PRN
- P6 acupressure 2-3 min each wrist or acupressure wristband PRN
- Pyridoxine 10 to 25 mg PO q6 to 8h, add doxylamine 12.5 mg PO up to TID or combination doxylamine-pyridoxine _
- If persistent: ondansetron 4 mg PO q8h PRN or promethazine 12.5 to 25 mg PO q6h PRN _
- IV fluids, electrolytes, and thiamine if unable to tolerate PO or losing weight _
- Return for inability to keep fluids down for 24 hours, dizziness, or decreased urination

If heartburn or reflux component:

- Avoid lying down within 3 hr of eating, elevate head of bed
- START sodium alginate tablets or capsules (sodium alginate as the only active ingredient), _ mg PO after meals and at bedtime per label
- START calcium carbonate 500 mg (200 mg elemental Ca) chewable 2 tabs PO PRN, max 5 tabs/day (1 g elemental Ca)
- Separate calcium carbonate from iron or prenatal vitamin by at least 2 hr
- Avoid sodium bicarbonate (baking soda) or magnesium trisilicate as the antacid
- START famotidine 20 mg PO BID if persistent despite antacids
- START omeprazole 20 mg PO daily if persistent on famotidine, antacid PRN breakthrough

use: Use when counseling and prescribing medical management of early pregnancy loss.
body:
#Early pregnancy loss, _ weeks by _

Ultrasound _. Hemodynamically stable, Hgb _, Rh _positive / negative. Options of expectant, medical and uterine aspiration management discussed, patient chose medical management.

Reviewed risks including incomplete passage needing a repeat dose or uterine aspiration, heavy bleeding, rare need for transfusion, and infection.

- Mifepristone 200 mg PO once, if available, then misoprostol 24 hours later _
- Misoprostol 800 mcg vaginally once, 4 tablets placed together, first dose on _
- Repeat misoprostol 800 mcg vaginally if no response to the first dose, no sooner than 3 hours and usually within 7 days
- Ibuprofen 400 mg PO 1 hour before misoprostol, then q4-6h PRN cramping, and acetaminophen 1000 mg PO q8h PRN, max 3 g/day
- Ondansetron 4 mg PO q8h PRN nausea _
- Rh immune globulin if Rh negative and 12 weeks or more; under 12 weeks not routine, shared decision _
- Follow-up ultrasound or hCG in 7-14 days _
- Backup for uterine aspiration: Dr. _

Go to the ER for soaking more than 2 maxi pads an hour for 2 hours in a row, fever, pain not controlled by medicine, foul-smelling discharge, or dizziness or fainting.

Questions answered.

body:
Endotracheal intubation procedure note

Indication: _
Procedure operator: _
Attending physician: _

Consent: _

During the informed consent discussion regarding the procedure or treatment, I explained the following to the patient or designee:

- Nature of the procedure or treatment and who will perform it
- Necessity for the procedure and the possible benefits
- Risks and complications, most common and serious
- Alternative treatments and the risks, benefits, and side effects of each, including no treatment
- Likelihood of the patient achieving his or her goals without this procedure or treatment
- Problems that might occur during recuperation

body:
Delirium prevention orders

- CAM screen every shift
- Awake with lights and TV on during the day, lights off 2200 to 0600
- Glasses and hearing aids on and working
- Reorient often, family at bedside encouraged
- Cluster overnight care, no vitals, labs, or baths 2300 to 0600 unless needed for safety
- Up to chair for meals, out of bed and walking as able, PT and OT consult
- Remove unneeded lines, restraints, and Foley, bladder scan every 8 hours if not voiding, straight cath for retention
- Avoid anticholinergics, benzodiazepines, and sedative hypnotics, no scheduled opioids unless needed for pain
- Acetaminophen 650 mg PO every 6 hours scheduled for pain _
- Melatonin 3 mg PO nightly as the only sleep aid
- Bowel regimen, hydration, glucose control
- Delirium precautions sign on door

use: Use as a nursing communication order for oxygen titration in COPD.
body:
Nursing communication: oxygen goals for COPD

- SpO2 goal 88 to 92 percent, awake and asleep
- Brief dips to 88 percent during sleep are expected, do not increase oxygen for them
- Increase oxygen only for SpO2 under 88 percent for 5 minutes or longer, or repeated drops under 88 percent despite current oxygen
- Wean oxygen if SpO2 stays above 92 percent, to limit CO2 retention
- Page the physician before increasing oxygen flow
- Page for new confusion, drowsiness, or increased work of breathing

#Precipitated opioid withdrawal

Buprenorphine _ mg given at _. COWS before _ and now _.

- Additional buprenorphine: buprenorphine-naloxone 8 mg SL now, repeat 8 mg SL in 1 hour if COWS still rising _
- Symptom adjuncts as needed:

- Hydroxyzine 25 to 50 mg PO every 6 hours as needed for anxiety
- Ibuprofen 600 mg PO every 6 hours as needed for aches
- Reassess COWS every 1 hour until improving
- ED if unable to keep fluids down or symptoms uncontrolled
- Restart plan: _
