use: Use for frailty or prefrailty in an older adult.
body:
#Frailty
_Prefrail / frail, _ on current plan.
Clinical Frailty Scale _ of 9. FRAIL scale _ of 5. SPPB _ of 12, gait speed _ m/s, grip _ kg, 5x chair stand _ sec.
Weight change _ in past yr, MNA-SF _ of 14, TUG _ sec, falls _.

- FRAIL scale: fatigue, resistance, ambulation, illnesses, loss of weight >5% in past yr. Score 1-2 prefrail, 3-5 frail.
- Clinical Frailty Scale 1-3 not frail, 4-9 increasing frailty
- Low function: gait speed 0.8 m/s or less, SPPB 8 or less, 5x chair stand >15 sec
- Low grip: <27 kg men, <16 kg women
- Exercise: multicomponent program led by progressive resistance training, plus balance and walking _
- Resistance 2-3 days/wk, nonconsecutive: 6-10 exercises, progress from 1-2 to 2-3 sets of 8-12 reps at hard effort
- Power when able: fast lift, slow lower, e.g. fast sit-to-stand
- Balance and functional training 3 or more days/wk. Walking 5-10 min, build to 150 min/wk as able.
- Vivifrail home program by SPPB: A 0-3, B 4-6, C 7-9, D 10-12, plus version if fall risk. Level _
- PT referral: progressive strength, power, balance, gait training, home program _
- Protein 1.0-1.2 g/kg/day, 1.2-1.5 g/kg/day with acute or chronic illness, unless eGFR <30 and not on dialysis
- Protein 25-30 g per meal. Energy about 30 kcal/kg/day. No weight-loss diet unless clear benefit.
- Medication review and deprescribing with Beers or STOPP criteria _
- Fatigue causes: PHQ-9, CBC, TSH, B12, orthostatic BP, sleep apnea screen _
- Treatable causes of weight loss _
- Vision, hearing, continence, cognition with Mini-Cog _
- Vitamin D not for frailty itself
- No hormone therapy or drug therapy for frailty itself
- Fall risk review and prevention plan _
- Social support, caregiver, and home services _
- Goals of care, advance directive, and health care agent _
- Recheck SPPB, gait speed, grip, and weight in 12 wk, then every _ mo

If age 75 or older or at risk of vitamin D deficiency:

- START vitamin D3 800-1000 IU PO daily, no level needed

If weight loss, MNA-SF 11 or less, or undernutrition:

- START oral nutritional supplement PO between meals, 400 kcal and 30 g protein/day or more, for 1 mo or longer
- Dietitian referral, weight and intake monthly _

If fall in past yr or gait or balance problem:

- Otago home program via PT, 3 times/wk plus walking 2 or more times/wk _

If severe frailty:

- Geriatrics referral _

use: Use for a pre-travel visit for international travel.
body:
#Travel medicine visit
Travel to _ x _ wk, departing _.
Itinerary urban or rural _, activities _, lodging _. Pregnancy _, immune compromise _, chronic disease _.

- Destination-specific vaccine and malaria needs reviewed _
- Routine vaccines up to date. MMR 2 doses at least 2 wk before departure if no immunity.
- Hepatitis A vaccine 1 dose before travel to endemic areas, age 6 mo or older. Restart 2-dose series at 12 mo if given earlier.
- Typhoid: oral Ty21a 1 capsule every other day x 4 doses, finish at least 1 wk before travel, age 6 yr or older
- Typhoid alternative: Vi polysaccharide 0.5 mL IM at least 2 wk before travel, age 2 yr or older
- Yellow fever: certified center, age 9 mo or older, at least 10 days before travel _
- Yellow fever contraindicated with immune compromise, thymus disorder, age <6 mo. Use caution if age 60 or older, pregnant, breastfeeding.
- Rabies pre-exposure: 2 doses IM on days 0 and 7 for remote travel, animal work, long stays, or children _
- Japanese encephalitis: 2 doses IM on days 0 and 28, day 7 allowed age 18-65, finish 1 wk before travel _
- Travelers' diarrhea: no routine abx ppx, oral rehydration for children
- START loperamide 4 mg PO once, then 2 mg after each loose stool, max 16 mg/day, PRN mild diarrhea
- START azithromycin 1,000 mg PO once, or 500 mg PO daily x 3 days, PRN severe or bloody diarrhea
- No loperamide alone with bloody diarrhea or fever
- Flights >4 hr: walk, calf exercises, aisle seat
- Travel health and medical evacuation insurance, Medicare does not cover care abroad

- START doxycycline 2.2 mg/kg PO daily, max 100 mg, if age 8 yr or older

- START mefloquine 250 mg PO weekly, at least 2 wk before through 4 wk after, not with psychiatric illness or seizures

- START chloroquine 8.3 mg/kg salt PO weekly in children, max 500 mg salt

- START azithromycin 10 mg/kg PO daily x 3 days, max _ mg/dose, in children PRN severe diarrhea

If infant 6-11 mo:

- Early MMR dose before international travel, then routine doses

If departing <2 wk and age >40, immune compromise, or liver disease:

- Hepatitis A immune globulin 0.1 mL/kg with vaccine _

If high VTE risk:

- Below-knee compression stockings 15-30 mmHg during travel _

use: Use for suspected tick-borne illness in Oklahoma, such as ehrlichiosis, Rocky Mountain spotted fever, or tularemia.
body:
#Tick-borne illness
Likely _ehrlichiosis given fever, headache, low WBC and plt / RMSF given fever, rash on wrists, forearms, ankles / tularemia given fever, skin ulcer, swollen regional nodes. Tick exposure on _.
Rash _, ulcer or eschar _, lymphadenopathy _. WBC _, plt _, Na _, AST/ALT _.

DDx:
>Ehrlichiosis; most likely given _, treating empirically
>Rocky Mountain spotted fever; considered but unlikely given _, treating empirically
>Tularemia; considered but unlikely given no ulcer or regional lymphadenopathy _, _
>Lyme disease; considered but unlikely given no bite in a high-incidence state, _

- START doxycycline 100 mg PO BID now; do not wait for test results
- CONT doxycycline until at least 3 days after fever resolves with clinical improvement, minimum 5-7 days
- CBC with diff and CMP: leukopenia, thrombocytopenia, hyponatremia, or high transaminases support the dx
- Normal labs early in illness do not exclude it
- Ehrlichia PCR on whole blood _
- Rickettsia and Ehrlichia IgG IFA now and repeat in 2-4 wk; fourfold rise confirms
- Fever should resolve in 24-48 hr on doxycycline; if not, reconsider dx
- No antibiotic ppx after a tick bite to prevent ehrlichiosis or RMSF
- Lyme ppx only if bite in a high-incidence state, blacklegged tick attached 36 hr or more, within 72 hr of removal
- START doxycycline 200 mg PO once if Lyme ppx criteria met; child <45 kg 4.4 mg/kg PO once, max 200 mg
- Tick removal: fine-tipped tweezers close to skin, steady upward pull, no twisting; clean site with alcohol or soap
- Return for confusion, bleeding, dyspnea, or no improvement in 48 hr; f/u in _ days

If child <45 kg:

- START doxycycline 2.2 mg/kg PO BID, max 100 mg per dose, any age

If organ dysfunction, severe thrombocytopenia, or mental status change:

- Admit

If tularemia, adult:

- START ciprofloxacin 750 mg PO BID x 10 days
- START doxycycline 200 mg PO once, then 100 mg PO BID x 14-21 days, as tularemia alternative
- No doxycycline monotherapy if tularemia is severe or treatment delayed >2 wk

If tularemia, child:

- START ciprofloxacin 15 mg/kg PO q12h, max 750 mg per dose, x 10 days

use: Use for a positive TB skin test or IGRA once active TB is excluded.
body:
#Latent TB infection
Likely latent TB infection given _+ IGRA on screening, no sxs, normal CXR / + TST, born in high TB country, no sxs / + test after close TB contact, no TB disease.
TST _ mm or IGRA _, CXR _, symptoms _. Risk factors _.

>Latent TB infection; most likely given positive test, normal CXR, and no symptoms
>Active TB disease; considered but unlikely given _, CXR and symptom review to exclude

- CXR and symptom review before treatment: fever, cough, chest pain, weight loss, night sweats, hemoptysis, fatigue
- Rifamycin interactions: warfarin, methadone, hormonal contraceptives, some ART; advise backup barrier contraception
- HOLD regimen if transaminases >3x ULN with symptoms or >5x ULN without symptoms
- Monthly visit for adherence, TB symptoms, and side effects
- Rifamycins turn urine and other body fluids orange and can stain soft contact lenses
- Give patient written record of test, CXR, regimen, and completion date
- Regimen, one of:

If 3HP:

- START 3HP, age 12 or older: isoniazid 15 mg/kg PO weekly, max 900 mg, plus rifapentine weekly x 12 doses
- Round isoniazid up to the nearest 50 or 100 mg
- START 3HP age 2-11: isoniazid 25 mg/kg PO weekly, max 900 mg, plus rifapentine weekly x 12 doses
- Rifapentine by weight: 10-14 kg 300 mg, 14.1-25 kg 450 mg, 25.1-32 kg 600 mg, 32.1-49.9 kg 750 mg, 50 kg or more 900 mg
- No 3HP if pregnant, planning pregnancy, or age <2 yr

If 4R:

- START 4R: rifampin 10 mg/kg PO daily x 4 mo, child 15-20 mg/kg, max 600 mg

If 3HR:

- START 3HR: isoniazid 5 mg/kg PO daily, max 300 mg, plus rifampin 10 mg/kg PO daily, max 600 mg, x 3 mo
- START 3HR in child: isoniazid 10-20 mg/kg PO daily, max 300 mg, plus rifampin 15-20 mg/kg PO daily, max 600 mg, x 3 mo

If neuropathy risk:

- START pyridoxine 25-50 mg PO daily with daily isoniazid, or 50 mg PO weekly with 3HP
- Neuropathy risk: pregnancy, breastfeeding, HIV, diabetes, alcohol use, malnutrition, CKD, older age

If hepatotoxicity risk:

- Baseline AST, ALT, bilirubin if liver disease, regular alcohol or injection drug use, HIV, pregnancy, or within 3 mo postpartum
- Repeat LFTs monthly if baseline abnormal or liver disease risk, and any time hepatitis symptoms occur

If symptoms or abnormal CXR:

- Sputum x 3, 8-24 hr apart, for AFB smear, cx, and NAAT; hold LTBI treatment

body:
#Conjunctivitis
Likely _viral / bacterial / allergic conjunctivitis given _watery discharge w/ cold or flu sxs / thick purulent discharge, lids matted shut / bilateral intense itching, other allergy sxs.
Discharge _, itching _, _unilateral / bilateral, contact lens use _. Visual acuity _, photophobia _, pupils _.

>_viral / bacterial / allergic conjunctivitis; most likely given _, _
>Bacterial keratitis; considered but unlikely given _, urgent ophthalmology if contact lens wearer
>Gonococcal or chlamydial conjunctivitis; considered but unlikely given _, cx if severe purulent discharge
>Herpes simplex conjunctivitis; considered but unlikely given no vesicular lid lesions _, _

- Cx and gonorrhea and chlamydia testing if severe purulent discharge; systemic treatment if positive
- Urgent ophthalmology: vision loss, moderate or severe pain, photophobia, corneal involvement, severe purulent discharge
- Also refer: neonate, prior HSV eye disease, recurrent episodes, or no improvement in 1 wk

- START erythromycin 0.5% ointment 1/2-inch ribbon in affected eye QID x 1 wk, as alternative

- START ketotifen 0.025% 1 drop in each eye q8-12h, as allergic alternative

- START ciprofloxacin 0.3% or ofloxacin 0.3% 1-2 drops in affected eye QID x 1 wk
- Prompt ophthalmology evaluation for contact lens wearers given keratitis risk

body:
#Head lice
Likely head lice given _live lice seen on scalp w/ scalp itching / live lice seen on scalp w/ excoriations behind ears, nape / live lice seen on scalp on louse comb, no itch yet.

- Do not use the same product more than 2-3 times if it is not working

- START malathion 0.5% lotion, rinse after 8-12 hr, repeat in 7-9 days if live lice

- START mebendazole 100 mg PO once, repeat in 2 wk, if available from a compounding pharmacy

- Albendazole safety <6 yr is not certain; mebendazole <2 yr, weigh risks and benefits _

- Pregnancy: treat only if infection is compromising pregnancy, and defer until third trimester

body:
#Vulvovaginal candidiasis
Likely _uncomplicated / complicated VVC given _vulvar itching, thick curdy discharge, yeast or pseudohyphae on KOH / vulvar soreness, external dysuria, normal pH / recurrent itching, + yeast cx or PCR.

>VVC; most likely given _, pH <4.5 and yeast on KOH prep
>Bacterial vaginosis or trichomonas; considered but unlikely given _, pH and wet mount _
>_; considered but unlikely given _, _

- START fluconazole 150 mg PO once
- Vaginal culture or PCR if complicated, recurrent, or persistent symptoms
- No treatment for asymptomatic colonization; partner treatment not needed
- Creams and suppositories may weaken latex condoms and diaphragms
- Return if symptoms persist or recur within 2 mo

If topical preferred:

- START clotrimazole 1% cream 5 g intravaginally daily x 7-14 days, or miconazole 2% cream 5 g intravaginally daily x 7 days, as alternatives

- START fluconazole 150 mg PO every 72 hr x 3 doses, days 1, 4, and 7
- START fluconazole 150 mg PO weekly x 6 mo for maintenance

- Nonfluconazole azole x 7-14 days; boric acid 600 mg vaginal capsule daily x 3 wk if recurs

use: Use for the A&P of an abnormal cervical cancer screening result, by result category.
body:
#Abnormal cervical cancer screening
Cytology _NILM / ASC-US / LSIL / ASC-H / HSIL / AGC, HPV _negative / positive, genotype _.
Age _, negative HPV-based screen within 5 yr _, pregnant _, immunosuppressed _.

- Result and next step discussed with patient, follow-up date _

If ASC-US or LSIL:

- ASC-US, HPV negative: repeat HPV-based testing in 3 yr
- ASC-US HPV positive, or LSIL: colposcopy
- ASC-US HPV positive or LSIL after a negative HPV-based screen within about 5 yr: repeat HPV-based testing in 1 yr
- LSIL, HPV negative, unknown prior history: repeat HPV-based testing in 1 yr

If NILM, HPV positive:

- NILM, HPV positive, not 16 or 18: repeat HPV-based testing in 1 yr, colposcopy if still abnormal

If HPV 16 or 18 positive:

- HPV 16 or 18 positive, any cytology including NILM: colposcopy

If HSIL:

- Colposcopy, or expedited excision without biopsy
- Expedited excision preferred if 25 or older, not pregnant, and HPV 16 positive

If ASC-H:

- Colposcopy regardless of HPV result

If AGC:

- Colposcopy with endocervical sampling regardless of HPV result
- Add endometrial sampling if 35 or older, or younger with AUB, chronic anovulation, or obesity

If age <25:

- Age <25 with LSIL, ASC-US HPV positive, or ASC-US without HPV: repeat cytology at 1 and 2 yr
- Colposcopy if ASC-H, HSIL, AGC, or low-grade result persists at 2 yr

If pregnant:

- Pregnancy: same thresholds; no ECC or endometrial biopsy; postpartum colposcopy no earlier than 4 wk

If self-collected HPV positive:

- Colposcopy if 16 or 18, otherwise clinician-collected cytology

If after colposcopy or treatment:

- After colposcopy with less than CIN 2 for a low-grade result: repeat HPV-based testing in 1 yr
- After treatment of CIN 2 or worse: HPV-based testing at 6 mo, then yearly until 3 negative
- Then HPV-based testing every 3 yr for at least 25 yr after treatment

use: Use for the A&P of urinary incontinence in adults, including older and cognitively impaired patients.
body:
#Urinary incontinence
Likely _stress / urge / mixed / overflow / functional incontinence given _leakage w/ cough or exertion, + cough stress test / sudden urgency w/ leakage, frequency, nocturia / both exertional and urgency leakage.
UA _, PVR _, 3-day bladder diary _, cough stress test _, prolapse on exam _.

DDx:
>_; most likely given _, _
>UTI; considered but unlikely given _, UA _
>Overflow from retention or obstruction; considered but unlikely given _, PVR _
>Transient cause such as medications, constipation, delirium, or atrophic vaginitis; considered but unlikely given _, _

- UA for all; renal function if obstruction suspected
- 3-day bladder diary, cough stress test, PVR by bladder scan
- Reviewed medications, constipation, mobility, and glycemic control as reversible causes _
- Fluids about 50-70 oz/day in smaller amounts, less in the evening
- Limit caffeine and carbonated drinks, weight loss if overweight, stop smoking, treat constipation
- Pelvic floor muscle training: 3 sets of 8-10 contractions held 6-8 sec, 3-4x/wk, for at least 15-20 wk
- Urology or urogyn if pain, hematuria, significant prolapse, prior pelvic surgery or radiation, fistula, elevated PVR, or refractory

If unable to contract pelvic floor muscles:

- Pelvic floor PT with biofeedback _

If urge:

- Bladder training for urge: urge suppression, lengthen voiding interval by 30-60 min until every 3-4 hr
- START mirabegron 25 mg PO daily
- INCR. mirabegron to 50 mg PO daily after 4-8 wk PRN, monitor BP
- START vibegron 75 mg PO daily as alternative
- Beta-3 agonist preferred over antimuscarinics in older adults given dementia risk
- START solifenacin 5 mg PO daily only if beta-3 agonist fails, counseled on cognitive risk _

If stress incontinence:

- Pessary trial _

If vaginal atrophy:

- START estradiol vaginal cream 0.5-2 g intravaginally twice weekly _

If cognitive impairment:

- Prompted or scheduled voiding every 2-3 hr

If overflow:

- Stop retention-causing meds, intermittent catheterization if irreversible

use: Use for the A&P of acute or chronic bacterial prostatitis or chronic pelvic pain syndrome in men.
body:
#Prostatitis
Likely _chronic pelvic pain syndrome / acute bacterial prostatitis / chronic bacterial prostatitis given _chronic pelvic pain w/ voiding sxs, negative cx / fever, dysuria, suprapubic pain, tender boggy prostate / recurrent UTI w/ same organism, perineal pain.
Temp _, prostate exam _, UA _, urine cx _, PVR _.

DDx:
>Acute bacterial prostatitis; most likely given _, tender boggy prostate _
>Chronic pelvic pain syndrome; considered but unlikely given _, pelvic pain 3 of past 6 mo with negative cultures
>STI urethritis or epididymitis; considered but unlikely given _, GC/CT NAAT _
>Prostatic abscess; considered but unlikely given _, imaging if febrile >36 hr on abx

- Midstream urine cx before abx; no prostate massage in acute prostatitis
- CBC, BMP; blood cx if temp >101.1 F or immunocompromised
- PSA not indicated during infection, may stay elevated 1-2 mo
- Admit if septic, unable to take PO, urinary retention, failed outpatient tx, or recent prostate biopsy
- TRUS or CT pelvis if fever >36 hr on abx or not improving, for abscess
- Repeat urine cx 1 wk after abx
- Urology referral if refractory, retention, or hematuria

If acute bacterial:

- START ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO BID, or levofloxacin 500-750 mg PO daily
- START TMP-SMX 160/800 mg PO BID as alternative if susceptible
- Treat 2 wk; extend to 4 wk if severe or still symptomatic

If sexually active and under 35, or STI risk:

- START ceftriaxone 500 mg IM once plus doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x 10 days

If inpatient:

- START ceftriaxone 1-2 g IV q24h or ciprofloxacin 400 mg IV q12h per local antibiogram
- START ertapenem 1 g IV q24h if recent prostate biopsy or ESBL risk

If chronic bacterial:

- 2-glass test if unclear, fluoroquinolone x 4 wk or TMP-SMX x 6 wk

If CPPS:

- No repeated abx courses if urine cx and STI tests negative
- START tamsulosin 0.4 mg PO daily if voiding symptoms
- START naproxen sodium 550 mg PO q12h PRN as part of multimodal pain plan
- START tadalafil 5 mg PO daily as option, not with nitrates
- CPPS options: pelvic floor PT if pelvic floor tenderness, acupuncture, CBT, neuropathic agent _

use: Use for the A&P of H. pylori infection: testing, treatment, and test of cure.
body:
#H. pylori infection
H. pylori _positive / persistent after treatment by _stool antigen / urea breath test / biopsy, _.
Indication for testing _. Prior H. pylori treatment _, penicillin allergy _.

- Test and treat: current or past PUD, MALT lymphoma, dyspepsia age <60, long-term NSAID or aspirin, unexplained IDA, ITP
- Also test: atrophic gastritis or intestinal metaplasia, first-degree relative with gastric cancer, adult household members of positive patients
- Avoid clarithromycin triple therapy unless susceptibility testing shows sensitivity
- Test of cure for all: urea breath test or stool antigen 4 wk or more after abx
- HOLD PPI 2 wk before test of cure; H2 blocker or antacid OK
- No serology for diagnosis or test of cure

- START tetracycline 500 mg PO QID x 14 days; do not substitute doxycycline
- START metronidazole 500 mg PO TID or QID x 14 days
- No alcohol on metronidazole and for 3 days after the last dose

- START vonoprazan 20 mg PO BID plus amoxicillin 1,000 mg PO TID x 14 days
- START rifabutin triple capsules (omeprazole 10 mg, amoxicillin 250 mg, rifabutin 12.5 mg) 4 capsules PO TID x 14 days

If persistent infection after bismuth quadruple therapy:

- Rifabutin triple if no penicillin allergy; susceptibility testing or GI referral _

use: Use for the A&P of vitamin D deficiency: testing, repletion, and maintenance.
body:
#Vitamin D deficiency
Vitamin D deficiency, _new / on repletion / on maintenance, _.
25-OH vitamin D _ ng/mL on _. Indication for testing _. Calcium _, creatinine _.

- Deficiency <12 ng/mL; 12 to <20 inadequate; 20 or more adequate for most
- Test only with an indication: osteoporosis, malabsorption (celiac, IBD, bariatric surgery), CKD, liver disease, anticonvulsants, glucocorticoids _
- No routine testing in healthy adults, including those with dark skin or obesity
- Empiric vitamin D without testing: age 75 or older, pregnancy, high-risk prediabetes _
- Usual upper limit 4,000 IU/day for long-term use; excess causes hypercalcemia
- Vitamin D foods: fatty fish (salmon, tuna, mackerel), egg yolks, UV-exposed mushrooms, fortified milk, cereal, orange juice and yogurt
- Sun: skin makes vitamin D in direct sun, less with dark skin, shade or clouds; no more than a few minutes unprotected for skin cancer risk
- Immune system: vitamin D supports immune function, but supplements have not been shown to prevent colds or other respiratory infections

If new or on repletion:

- START vitamin D3 6,000 IU PO daily x 8 wk, or 50,000 IU PO weekly x 8 wk _
- Recheck 25-OH vitamin D after the 8 wk course _; if still low, review adherence and malabsorption

If age 50 or older:

- Prefer daily dosing over intermittent high doses

If on maintenance:

- CONT vitamin D3 1,500-2,000 IU PO daily after repletion

use: Use for the A&P of croup in a child.
body:
#Croup
Likely croup given _barky cough, inspiratory stridor and hoarseness after URI / abrupt barky cough worse at night, low-grade fever / barky cough, stridor only when agitated.
SpO2 _, stridor at rest _, retractions _, PO intake _.
Westley score _, _mild 0-2 / moderate 3-7 / severe 8-11 / impending respiratory failure 12 or more.

DDx:
>Viral croup; most likely given barky cough after URI symptoms _, treating
>Bacterial tracheitis; considered but unlikely given nontoxic appearance _, reassess if poor response to epinephrine
>Epiglottitis; considered but unlikely given barky cough, no drooling or toxic appearance _
>Foreign body aspiration; considered but unlikely given no choking episode _

- START dexamethasone 0.6 mg/kg PO once, max 16 mg, for all severities including mild
- d/c home if no stridor at rest after 2 hr observation, SpO2 90% or higher, tolerating PO
- Admit if stridor at rest recurs after observation and needs a 2nd racemic epinephrine dose, SpO2 <90%, or poor PO intake
- Oxygen and ED or PICU transfer if severe distress, cyanosis, lethargy, or fatigue with decreasing stridor
- Keep child calm on caregiver's lap, minimize exams and procedures
- No routine labs or imaging; neck and chest x-ray if poor response, high fever, or no infectious symptoms
- Humidified air and mist not recommended, no benefit
- Return for stridor at rest, retractions, drooling, cyanosis, or lethargy
- f/u if symptoms last beyond 1 wk _

If low-dose alternative:

- START dexamethasone 0.15 mg/kg PO once instead _, equally effective in trials

If stridor at rest or moderate to severe:

- START racemic epinephrine 2.25% 0.05 mL/kg nebulized, max 0.5 mL
- Repeat racemic epinephrine after 20 min if no improvement; reconsider diagnosis if a 3rd dose is needed
- Observe at least 2 hr after racemic epinephrine, effect wanes after 1-2 hr

If atypical age or course:

- Consider alternative diagnosis and ENT if age <6 mo or >6 yr, recurrent croup, positional stridor, or prior prolonged intubation

use: Use for the A&P of suspected or confirmed influenza in clinic, including antiviral, prophylaxis and return-to-school decisions.
body:
#Influenza
Likely influenza given _abrupt fever, myalgias, headache, dry cough / viral sxs and + rapid molecular flu test / no fever, confusion, poor appetite in older adult.
Onset _ days ago. Rapid molecular flu test _, COVID-19 test _. Temp _, SpO2 _, RR _. High-risk factors _, pregnant _.

DDx:
>Influenza; most likely given abrupt fever, cough, and myalgias during flu season, _
>COVID-19; considered but unlikely given _, tested with flu
>Bacterial pneumonia or coinfection; considered but unlikely given _, CXR if hypoxia, focal exam, or worsening after improvement

- Rapid molecular flu test if the result changes management; preferred over rapid antigen test. Do not delay antivirals for results
- Treat regardless of symptom duration if hospitalized, severe or progressive illness, or high risk
- High risk: age 65 or older, <2 yr, pregnant or within 2 wk postpartum, nursing home or long-term care resident, BMI 40 or higher
- High risk also: asthma, chronic lung, heart, kidney, liver, blood, metabolic or neurologic disease, diabetes, prior stroke, immunosuppression, American Indian or Alaska Native, age <19 on long-term aspirin
- Counseled on modest benefit: oseltamivir shortens symptoms by about 17 hr in adults and 29 hr in healthy children
- No reduction in hospitalization shown in adults; no symptom benefit shown in children with asthma
- Harms: nausea in 1 of 28 adults, vomiting in 1 of 22 adults and 1 of 19 children treated
- Oseltamivir: take with food if nausea; report confusion or abnormal behavior, especially in children
- Evaluate for bacterial coinfection if worse after initial improvement or not improving after 3-5 days of antiviral; abx only if suspected
- ED or admit for dyspnea, chest pain or pressure, confusion, seizure, no urine output, severe weakness, or dehydration
- Return to work or school when fever-free 24 hr without antipyretics and symptoms improving, then 5 days of added precautions such as masking
- Annual influenza vaccine for everyone 6 mo or older; age 65 or older: high-dose, recombinant or adjuvanted preferred
- F/u in _ days if not improving

If not high risk:

- May treat if onset within 48 hr, clinical judgment _
- Low risk: shared decision to treat _yes / no, _

If adult or child >40 kg:

- START oseltamivir 75 mg PO BID x 5 days; pregnancy: preferred agent, same dose

If renal impairment:

- DECR. oseltamivir to 30 mg PO BID x 5 days if CrCl 31-60, or 30 mg PO daily x 5 days if CrCl 11-30

If ESRD on HD:

- START oseltamivir 30 mg PO after each hemodialysis, max 5 days; not recommended in ESRD without dialysis

If child age 1 yr or older:

- START oseltamivir PO BID x 5 days by weight
- Oseltamivir weight bands: 15 kg or less 30 mg, 15.1-23 kg 45 mg, 23.1-40 kg 60 mg, >40 kg 75 mg

If term infant <1 yr:

- START oseltamivir 3 mg/kg PO BID x 5 days

If preterm:

- START oseltamivir by postmenstrual age: <38 wk 1 mg/kg, 38-40 wk 1.5 mg/kg, >40 wk 3 mg/kg, PO BID x 5 days

If baloxavir instead:

- START baloxavir 40 mg PO once if 20-79 kg, 80 mg if 80 kg or more; age 5 yr or older, within 48 hr of onset
- No baloxavir if pregnant, breastfeeding or severely immunosuppressed; do not take with antacids, calcium, iron, magnesium or zinc

If zanamivir instead:

- START zanamivir 10 mg (2 inhalations) BID x 5 days, age 7 yr or older; avoid in asthma, COPD, or milk protein allergy

If exposed household contact:

- Household ppx within 48 hr of exposure if contact is very high risk, such as severely immunocompromised
- Also ppx for unvaccinated household contacts of a very high-risk person, plus vaccine
- Early treatment if symptoms develop is an alternative to ppx; no ppx if >48 hr since exposure

If oseltamivir ppx:

- START oseltamivir 75 mg PO daily x 7 days after last exposure for ppx; child 1 yr or older weight-based dose PO daily; age 3-11 mo 3 mg/kg PO daily
- DECR. ppx oseltamivir to 30 mg PO daily if CrCl 31-60, or 30 mg PO every other day if CrCl 11-30

If baloxavir ppx, age 5 yr or older:

- START baloxavir single dose as above for ppx

If zanamivir ppx, age 5 yr or older:

- START zanamivir 10 mg inhaled daily x 7 days for ppx instead

use: Use for the A&P of suspected measles, including isolation, reporting, testing and post-exposure care of contacts.
body:
#Measles, suspected
Likely measles given _fever, cough, coryza, conjunctivitis, then rash / maculopapular rash head to trunk, Koplik spots / fever and rash in unvaccinated traveler.
Temp _ (38.3 C or higher), generalized maculopapular rash day _, cough _, coryza _, conjunctivitis _, Koplik spots _. MMR doses _. Travel or exposure _.

DDx:
>Measles; most likely given fever, rash, and cough, coryza or conjunctivitis, testing and isolating now
>Other viral exanthem; considered but unlikely given _, measles PCR and IgM to distinguish
>_; considered but unlikely given _, _

- Clinical case definition: generalized maculopapular rash 3 days or more, temp 38.3 C or higher, and cough, coryza or conjunctivitis
- Mask patient and room immediately in an airborne infection isolation room; if none, private room with door closed. Keep out of the waiting room
- Staff entering wear an N95 regardless of immunity; leave room empty up to 2 hr after the patient leaves
- Notify health department immediately on suspicion, by phone, before results: OSDH epidemiologist on call 405-426-8710, 24/7, _ local
- Throat or NP swab for measles rRT-PCR plus serum measles IgM now; urine PCR acceptable if no swab. Ship via health department
- Repeat serum IgM 3-10 days after symptom onset if early IgM negative and PCR negative or not done
- Isolate at home through 4 days after rash onset, rash day 0; for the whole illness if severely immunocompromised
- Complications: otitis media, pneumonia, croup, diarrhea; encephalitis about 1 per 1,000; death 1-3 per 1,000 children; SSPE years later
- Higher risk of complications: age <5, adults >20, pregnancy, immunocompromised
- ED if dyspnea, chest pain, dehydration, persistent fever or headache, or confusion; call ahead before arrival
- Contacts: list everyone in the building during the visit and up to 2 hr after, with health department
- MMR at least 6 mo after IG PEP if otherwise eligible
- Exposed nonimmune contacts: exclude from school, child care and health care work day 5 through day 21 after exposure, day 28 if IG given

If child:

- START vitamin A PO daily x 2 days: age <6 mo 50,000 IU, 6-11 mo 100,000 IU, 12 mo or older 200,000 IU

If nonimmune contact, not pregnant or severely immunocompromised:

- PEP: MMR within 72 hr of first exposure for nonimmune contacts 6 mo or older

If infant <12 mo or child <30 kg who cannot get MMR:

- PEP: IGIM 0.5 mL/kg IM, max 15 mL, within 6 days

If pregnant without evidence of immunity or severely immunocompromised:

- PEP: IGIV 400 mg/kg IV within 6 days

Likely pertussis given _paroxysmal cough, whoop, posttussive vomiting / URI sxs, low-grade fever, then worsening cough / apnea or cyanosis in infant, minimal cough.

- Culture on the same swab if within first 2 wk of cough; serology if cough 2-8 wk

desc: Urinary tract infection in a child
use: Use for suspected or confirmed UTI in a child 8 days to 5 years old in clinic, including older children with urinary symptoms.
body:
#Urinary tract infection, _febrile / afebrile
Likely _febrile UTI given fever without source, + UA, infant / afebrile cystitis given dysuria, frequency, urgency, + LE / pyelonephritis given fever, flank pain, CVA tenderness.
Age _ mo, Tmax _, appearance _. UA WBC _ /hpf, LE _, nitrite _. Urine cx by _cath / SPA / clean catch _, CFU/mL _. Stooling _.

DDx:
>Febrile UTI or pyelonephritis; most likely given _, urine cx _
>Afebrile cystitis; considered but unlikely given _, _
>Bowel and bladder dysfunction or constipation; considered but unlikely given _, _
>Urethritis, including STI; considered but unlikely given _, _

- Test urine within 72 hr of onset if fever without source at 2-24 mo, or urinary symptoms at 2-5 yr
- Evaluate sooner if known GU anomaly, prior febrile UTI, or flank pain
- UTI confirmed if pyuria plus single uropathogen: cath 10,000 or more CFU/mL, clean catch 100,000 or more CFU/mL
- Confirming pyuria at 2 mo-5 yr: 5 or more WBC/hpf or LE 1+ or higher
- STOP abx if cx negative, contaminated, or below threshold, unless clinical picture suggests otherwise _
- Choose empiric abx by local resistance _, then narrow to susceptibilities
- Cephalexin preferred if local susceptibility >80-85%; else cefixime, TMP-SMX, or ceftriaxone by local resistance
- Duration: afebrile cystitis age 2 yr or older x 3-5 days. Febrile UTI, low risk, x 5-7 days
- Duration 7-14 days if age <2 mo, urinary tract anomaly, bacteremia, or slow response
- PO abx if >28 days and tolerating PO. Admit if toxic, dehydrated, unable to take PO, or failed outpatient abx
- Recheck response in 48 hr _. Reassess if fever persists >48 hr on abx
- Renal and bladder US after first febrile UTI if <5 yr, for structural anomalies, not to detect VUR. Need not be done acutely
- VCUG if US abnormal, second febrile UTI at <2 yr, or second febrile UTI at 2 yr or older without another explanation
- VCUG optional after first febrile UTI if <1 mo, non-E. coli organism, circumcised male, atypical course, or unreliable f/u
- No routine abx ppx for low-risk VUR: grade I-II and no bowel and bladder dysfunction
- Ppx is an option for grade III or high-risk VUR, shared decision with family _
- Screen for and treat constipation and bowel and bladder dysfunction. Refer if no response to standard management
- Refer to peds urology or nephrology if VUR or urinary tract anomaly found

If age <2 mo:

- Age <2 mo with fever: follow the febrile infant pathway for age. Age 8-28 days: admit, START parenteral abx, switch to PO after improvement
- Likely UTI if 5 or more WBC/hpf or trace LE or higher

If age >2 mo:

- START empiric abx after cx sent if 10 or more WBC/hpf or LE 2+ or higher

If not toilet trained:

- Cath or SPA urine for cx. Bag urine for screening only, never for cx

If toilet trained:

- Midstream clean catch for UA and cx

If local susceptibility >80-85%:

- START cephalexin 50-100 mg/kg/day PO divided QID if 2-24 mo, 25-50 mg/kg/day divided BID to QID if older. Max 500 mg/dose

If alternative by local resistance:

- START cefixime 8 mg/kg PO daily, max 400 mg/dose, if 2 mo or older
- START amoxicillin-clavulanate 20-40 mg/kg/day of amoxicillin PO divided TID, max _ mg
- START TMP-SMX 6-12 mg/kg/day of TMP PO divided BID if 2-24 mo, 8 mg/kg/day divided BID if older. Max 160 mg TMP/dose

If afebrile cystitis:

- START cefdinir 14 mg/kg/day PO divided BID, max 600 mg/day, or nitrofurantoin 5-7 mg/kg/day PO divided QID, max 100 mg/dose. Afebrile cystitis only

If parenteral abx needed:

- Parenteral if bacteremia or critically ill. One parenteral dose first if family cannot fill PO abx promptly
- START ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg IV or IM q24h, max 2 g/dose. Switch to PO when improved

use: Use for prevention and treatment of constipation caused by opioids.
body:
#Opioid-induced constipation
Likely opioid-induced constipation given _hard stools after starting an opioid / straining on a stable opioid / worse after an opioid dose increase.
Opioid _ at _ MME/day x _. SBMs _ per wk, Bristol type _. Laxatives tried: _ x _ wk.

DDx:
>Opioid-induced constipation; most likely given _, _
>Bowel obstruction; considered but unlikely given passing flatus, no vomiting or distension _, imaging before PAMORA if suspected
>Chronic idiopathic constipation; considered but unlikely given onset with opioid _, _

- Rome IV: new or worse constipation when starting, changing, or increasing an opioid, plus 2 or more functional constipation criteria
- START polyethylene glycol 17 g PO daily or senna 8.6-17.2 mg PO nightly with any opioid start, scheduled not PRN
- Docusate adds no benefit to senna; use an osmotic or stimulant laxative, not docusate alone
- No fiber supplements for opioid-induced constipation
- Fluids, prompt toileting, physical activity
- INCR. to both classes before calling it refractory: polyethylene glycol 17 g PO daily plus senna 8.6-17.2 mg PO nightly _
- Enemas for rescue only _
- DECR. opioid dose or rotate to a less constipating opioid if possible _
- Return for severe abdominal pain, vomiting, distension, or no flatus
- F/u in _ wk

If refractory to 2 laxative classes on a regular schedule:

- START naldemedine 0.2 mg PO daily, with or without food; no renal adjustment, avoid in severe hepatic impairment
- START naloxegol 25 mg PO qAM, 1 hr before or 2 hr after first meal; 12.5 mg if not tolerated
- STOP maintenance laxatives when starting naloxegol or methylnaltrexone, resume PRN if response poor after 3 days
- Naloxegol contraindicated with strong CYP3A4 inhibitors; 12.5 mg with moderate inhibitors such as diltiazem or verapamil
- PAMORAs contraindicated with known or suspected GI obstruction
- STOP PAMORA if opioid is stopped

If naldemedine and naloxegol not suitable:

- START methylnaltrexone 450 mg PO qAM, 30 min before first meal, or 12 mg SQ daily

If CrCl <60:

- START naloxegol 12.5 mg PO qAM, INCR. to 25 mg if tolerated and symptoms persist
- START methylnaltrexone 150 mg PO qAM or 6 mg SQ daily

If advanced illness on opioids:

- START methylnaltrexone SQ every other day PRN, max 1 dose/24 hr: 8 mg if 38 to <62 kg, 12 mg if 62-114 kg
- Methylnaltrexone 0.15 mg/kg SQ if <38 kg or >114 kg; half dose if CrCl <60

If PAMORA not suitable:

- START lubiprostone 24 mcg PO BID with food and water; benefit not established with methadone
- DECR. lubiprostone to 16 mcg PO BID if Child-Pugh B, 8 mcg PO BID if Child-Pugh C

use: Use for constipation, straining, or infrequent stools in an infant under 12 months.
body:
#Infant constipation
Likely _infant dyschezia given straining, then soft stool / functional constipation given hard painful stools / normal breastfed pattern given soft infrequent stools.
Age _ wk, _breastfed / formula fed / mixed. Stools _ per wk, consistency _, blood _. Meconium by 48 hr _. Weight gain _. Abdomen _, anus _, spine _, tone _.

DDx:
>_; most likely given _, _
>Hirschsprung disease; considered but unlikely given meconium within 48 hr, normal growth _, rectal suction biopsy if suspected
>Hypothyroidism or cystic fibrosis; considered but unlikely given normal growth _, TSH or sweat chloride if suspected
>Cow milk protein allergy; considered but unlikely given _, elimination trial if intractable

- Red flags absent: meconium >48 hr, onset <1 mo, failure to thrive, distension, bilious vomiting, fever, ill appearance _
- Red flags absent: explosive stools, narrow ribbon stools, tight anus or empty rectum, weak suck or low tone, spine findings _
- Counsel: breastfed >1 mo, soft painless stools every 4-7 days can be normal
- Counsel: formula-fed infants pass fewer and firmer stools than breastfed infants
- Infant dyschezia criteria: <9 mo, straining and crying 10 min or more before soft stool, otherwise healthy
- No oral mineral oil, stimulant laxatives, or phosphate enemas in infants
- Peds GI referral if red flags, or if <6 mo and needing rectal stimulation to stool _
- Weight check and f/u in _ wk

If dyschezia:

- Reassure, resolves without treatment; no laxatives
- No rectal stimulation with thermometer, cotton swab, or finger

If hard stools and over 1 mo:

- 100% pear or apple juice 1 oz per month of age per day, max 4 oz/day; prune juice after 3 mo
- Hold knees to chest and gently press the lower belly for a few minutes

If under 6 mo and juice not enough:

- START lactulose 10 g/15 mL 0.5-1 mL/kg/day PO in 1-2 doses (350-700 mg/kg/day), max 30 mL/day _
- START glycerin infant suppository 1/2 to 1 PR once PRN, occasional use only _
- START polyethylene glycol 0.4 g/kg/day PO daily if lactulose fails, max 17 g/day; limited data <6 mo _

If 6-12 mo:

- Pureed prunes, pears, peaches, plums, peas, or beans BID
- START polyethylene glycol 0.4-0.8 g/kg/day PO daily, max 17 g/day, titrate to soft daily stool _
- START lactulose 10 g/15 mL 1-3 mL/kg/day PO divided BID, max 30 mL/day, if PEG not tolerated _

If impacted:

- Cleanout before maintenance therapy _

If intractable and cow milk protein allergy suspected:

- Cow milk protein-free trial x 2-4 wk _

use: Use for encopresis from functional constipation in a child age 4 or older.
body:
#Retentive fecal incontinence (encopresis)
Likely retentive fecal incontinence given _daily soiling, large rectal fecal mass / withholding, painful stools, soiling / relapse after laxatives stopped early.
Age _ yr. Accidents _ per wk, day or night _. Toilet BMs _ per wk, Bristol type _. Withholding _. Fecal mass on exam _. Spine and neuro exam _. Prior cleanouts and meds _.

DDx:
>Retentive fecal incontinence 2/2 functional constipation; most likely given _, _
>Functional nonretentive fecal incontinence; considered but unlikely given _, no fecal mass, normal stool frequency; transit study via GI if unclear
>Spinal cord abnormality; considered but unlikely given normal spine and lower extremity neuro exam, MRI spine if abnormal
>Hirschsprung disease; considered but unlikely given meconium within 48 hr, normal growth _, _

- Explained: soiling is overflow around retained stool, not willful; withholding cycle reviewed
- No blame, shame, or punishment for accidents
- Cleanout first if fecal mass on exam or impaction by history _
- START polyethylene glycol 0.4-0.8 g/kg/day PO daily, max 17 g/day, titrate to soft daily stool
- Scheduled toilet sits after meals x _ min, feet on a footstool
- Sticker or reward chart for each sit, even without a BM
- Stool and accident diary _
- CONT maintenance at least 2 mo, and symptom-free 1 mo or more, before a slow wean
- Many children need 6-12 mo of maintenance
- Relapse common, about 50%; restart maintenance at the first sign _
- Behavioral health referral if normal stooling not restored within 3 mo, or emotional or behavior concerns _
- Peds GI referral if red flags, or no response to max doses of 2 laxative classes x 3 mo _
- F/u in _ wk

- START bisacodyl PO daily instead of senna: 3-10 yr 5 mg, 10-11 yr 5-10 mg, 12 yr or older 5-15 mg _

If intractable and cow milk protein allergy suspected:

- Cow milk-free diet trial x 2-4 wk _

use: Use for the A&P of a skin tear or skin flap in fragile, aged skin, often after a fall.
body:
#Skin tear
Likely skin tear, type _1 given flap covers wound bed / 2 given partial flap loss / 3 given total flap loss.
Location _, size _ cm, flap viability _, bleeding or hematoma _, surrounding skin _.
Anticoagulant or antiplatelet _, steroids _, last tetanus _.

DDx:
>Skin tear; most likely given shear or bump on fragile skin, depth not past subcutaneous layer
>Laceration; considered but unlikely given _, repair as laceration if it extends through subcutaneous tissue
>Ruptured traumatic blister; considered but unlikely given _, _

- Control bleeding with pressure and elevation, up to 10 min
- Cleanse with normal saline, gently remove clots, hematoma, and debris; pat dry, do not scrub
- Realign viable flap with a moist cotton swab or gloved finger, without stretching the skin
- No sutures, staples, or adhesive closure strips in fragile skin
- Dressing: silicone dressing preferred, or silicone mesh, lipidocolloid, or petrolatum gauze with a secondary cover
- Avoid film, hydrocolloid, iodine dressings, plain gauze, and strong adhesive tape
- Mark an arrow on the dressing showing removal direction, with the flap, and date the next change
- Leave dressing on up to 5-7 days if no saturation, leak, or bleeding _
- Review anticoagulants, antiplatelets, steroids, and polypharmacy _
- Fall risk: TUG, orthostatic BP, medication review _
- Moisturize limbs BID; twice-daily moisturizer cuts skin tear incidence about 50%
- Protect skin: long sleeves, shin guards, padding on bedrails and wheelchair, safe transfers, short nails
- Red flags: spreading redness, warmth, pus, or increasing pain; dusky or nonviable flap; reaccumulating hematoma
- Wound care referral if not progressing at 2 wk or not healed at 4 wk
- Wound check in _ days

If gaping edges and <24 hr since injury:

- Tissue adhesive to approximate edges _

If nonviable flap:

- Debride carefully, keep any viable flap in place

If moderate exudate:

- Nonadhesive foam dressing, change every 2-7 days by exudate

If lower leg:

- Consider light compression, 10 mmHg, removed daily to check skin

If tetanus not up to date:

- Td or Tdap if last dose 10 yr or more ago, or 5 yr or more if dirty wound
- Tetanus vaccine now if series incomplete or unknown
- TIG 250 units IM only if dirty wound and series incomplete or unknown

body:
#Soft tissue hematoma of _shin / thigh / arm
Likely soft tissue hematoma given _fall or bump, then swelling and bruising / tender swelling, overlying ecchymosis / spontaneous swelling on anticoagulant.
Anticoagulant _apixaban / rivaroxaban / warfarin / aspirin or clopidogrel / none, last dose _.
Size _ cm, tense _, overlying skin _intact / thin and fragile / dusky or blistered, compartments soft _, distal NV intact _.
Hgb _, INR _.

>Expanding hematoma or active bleeding; considered but unlikely given stable size and Hgb _, ED if expanding

- Limit activity, elevate above heart, ice 10-20 min at a time for the first 48 hr
- Compression wrap _; loosen for pain, numbness, or a cold, pale limb

- Restart as soon as medically safe if held

body:
#Tendinopathy, _lateral elbow / medial elbow / de Quervain / patellar / Achilles / gluteal / biceps / _
Likely tendinopathy given _insidious onset after increased activity / focal tendon tenderness / pain w/ resisted tendon loading.
_ side, duration _ wk, tender at _, pain w/ resisted _, strength _, recent fluoroquinolone _.
POCUS: _not done / normal tendon / thickened, hypoechoic tendon / neovascularity on Doppler / partial-thickness tear / full-thickness tear _

DDx:
>Tendinopathy; most likely given _, _
>Tendon tear or rupture; considered but unlikely given strength _, imaging if new weakness or sudden pop
>_; considered but unlikely given _, _

- Relative rest, not complete rest: cut back painful loading, keep other activity
- Pain during exercise up to 5/10 is OK if back to baseline by next morning
- Progressive tendon loading exercise, home program or PT _
- Ice up to 20 min at a time PRN pain
- START diclofenac 1% gel topical QID x 7 to 14 days: 2 g for upper extremity, 4 g for lower extremity
- Diclofenac gel max 8 g/day per upper extremity joint, 16 g/day per lower extremity joint, 32 g/day total
- Corticosteroid injection gives short-term relief only, no long-term benefit; repeated injections risk rupture
- Fluoroquinolone tendon risk higher if >60, on corticosteroids, or transplant recipient
- Statins: no established link to tendon rupture _
- Imaging only if not improving at _ wk or red flags: x-ray first, then ultrasound or MRI
- POCUS in clinic if dx unclear or tear suspected
- Full resolution may take >6 mo
- Sports medicine or orthopedic referral if little improvement after 3 to 6 mo
- F/u in _ wk

If topical NSAID not enough:

- START naproxen 500 mg PO BID with food x 7 to 14 days

If tendon pain on a fluoroquinolone:

- STOP fluoroquinolone, switch to a non-fluoroquinolone abx

If lateral elbow:

- Wrist extensor strengthening with eccentric emphasis, PT _
- Counterforce brace centered over the back of the forearm for pain, does not reduce strength
- Avoid corticosteroid injection: lower 1-yr recovery (83% vs 96%) and more recurrence (54% vs 12%) than placebo injection
- 80 to 95% improve without surgery; surgical referral if no response after 6 to 12 mo

If medial elbow:

- Rest, ice, stretching, then forearm flexor and extensor resistive exercise as pain settles
- Surgery only after 9 to 12 mo of failed conservative care

If de Quervain:

- Thumb spica splint, especially at night; avoid side-to-side wrist motion
- Corticosteroid injection plus splint more effective than splint alone _
- Hand surgery referral if severe or not improving after 6 wk _

If patellar:

- Heavy slow resistance or eccentric decline squat training x 12 wk, PT _
- Isometric quad holds 45 sec x 5 for short-term pain relief
- Patellar strap _
- No corticosteroid injection into the patellar tendon: short-term benefit only, worse at 6 mo than exercise, rupture risk

If Achilles:

- In-shoe heel lifts; better than eccentric exercise at 12 wk for midportion pain
- No corticosteroid injection into the Achilles tendon, rupture risk
- Improvement may take several months; surgical referral if no improvement after 6 mo

If midportion Achilles:

- Eccentric heel drops off a step, 3 sets of 15 BID x 12 wk

If insertional Achilles:

- Concentric loading, no heel drops below step level

If gluteal:

- Load management education plus progressive hip abductor strengthening, PT _
- Avoid tendon compression: no leg crossing, low chairs, hanging on one hip, or lying on painful side
- Education plus exercise beat corticosteroid injection for global improvement at 8 and 52 wk

If biceps:

- Rest from painful activity, ice, PT stretching and strengthening _
- Corticosteroid injection may relieve pain _
- Popeye deformity suggests complete rupture, orthopedic referral

body:
#Low libido
Likely _testosterone deficiency given low libido, ED, two low AM levels / depression given low mood, anhedonia, positive PHQ-9 / medication effect given SSRI, opioid, or finasteride start.
Duration _, distress _, ED _. AM total testosterone _ and _ ng/dL, LH _, prolactin _, PHQ-9 _.

- PHQ-9 _, treat depression if present

- TSH <0.1 on repeat over 3-6 mo is persistent and rules out transient thyroiditis

- Treat if age 65 or older, cardiac risk factors or heart disease, osteoporosis, postmenopausal off estrogen or bisphosphonate, or hyperthyroid symptoms
- Consider treatment if age <65 without these risks _

- Consider treatment if age 65 or older, cardiac disease, osteoporosis, or hyperthyroid symptoms
- Age <65 without symptoms, cardiac disease, or osteoporosis: observe, no etiology workup needed

#Thyroiditis, _subacute / painless / postpartum / drug-induced
Likely _subacute thyroiditis given painful tender thyroid, high ESR / painless thyroiditis given no neck pain / postpartum thyroiditis given onset 2-6 mo postpartum.

>Acute suppurative thyroiditis; considered but unlikely given _, US or CT, abx and drainage
>Exogenous thyroid hormone; considered but unlikely given _, low uptake, high T4:T3 ratio

- Suspected acute suppurative thyroiditis: US or CT, abx and drainage

- Thyrotoxic phase 3-6 wk; hypothyroid phase in about 30%, up to 6 mo

- No response to full-dose NSAID in several days, or moderate to severe pain: START prednisone 40 mg PO daily x 1-2 wk

- Persistent hypothyroidism 5-15%, recurrence 1-4%

- Recurs in about 70% of later pregnancies

- Decide on continuing the drug with the prescribing specialist _

body:
#Thyroid nodule
_ cm _ lobe nodule, US pattern _TR_ / _ suspicion, FNA _not done / Bethesda _.
TSH _, prior US _, growth _, neck radiation _, family history _.

- Growth: 20% in 2 dimensions with at least 2 mm, or 50% volume increase
- No levothyroxine suppression for benign nodules
- Endocrinology or ENT referral for Bethesda III to VI _
- F/u in _ mo

If no FNA yet:

- FNA if high or intermediate suspicion 1 cm or more, low 1.5 cm or more, very low 2 cm or more or observe
- No FNA for pure cysts
- TR3: FNA 2.5 cm or more, follow 1.5 cm or more
- TR4: FNA 1.5 cm or more, follow 1 cm or more
- TR5: FNA 1 cm or more, follow 0.5 cm or more
- TR1 or TR2: no FNA, no follow-up

If below FNA size, surveillance:

- High suspicion: US in 6-12 mo
- Low to intermediate suspicion: US in 12-24 mo
- Very low suspicion >1 cm or pure cyst: US, if repeated, at 24 mo or later
- Very low suspicion 1 cm or less, or pure cyst: no follow-up
- TR5 yearly up to 5 yr; TR4 at 1, 2, 3, 5 yr; TR3 at 1, 3, 5 yr
- Stop at 5 yr if size stable

If Bethesda I, nondiagnostic, ROM 13%:

- Repeat US-guided FNA
- Repeatedly nondiagnostic: observe closely, or surgery if high suspicion US, growth, or risk factors

If Bethesda II, benign, ROM 4%:

- No further immediate workup
- High suspicion US: repeat US and FNA within 12 mo
- Low to intermediate suspicion: US in 12-24 mo; repeat FNA if growth or new suspicious features
- Very low suspicion: US, if repeated, at 24 mo or later
- Second benign FNA: stop surveillance of this nodule
- Surgery if growing and >4 cm, compressive symptoms, or clinical concern

If Bethesda III, AUS, ROM 22%:

- Repeat FNA or molecular testing, then surveillance or diagnostic lobectomy

If Bethesda IV, follicular neoplasm, ROM 30%:

- Molecular testing or diagnostic lobectomy

If Bethesda V, suspicious for malignancy, ROM 74%:

- Surgery: lobectomy or near-total thyroidectomy; molecular testing optional
- Neck US for lymph nodes before surgery

If Bethesda VI, malignant, ROM 97%:

- Surgery: lobectomy or near-total thyroidectomy
- Neck US for lymph nodes before surgery
- Active surveillance option for papillary microcarcinoma <1 cm without spread

If pregnant:

- FNA if TSH not suppressed; no radionuclide scan
- Indeterminate cytology: surgery can usually wait until after delivery

Likely OME given _effusion without bulging TM weeks after AOM / retracted, immobile TM after a cold / muffled hearing, effusion, no otalgia or fever.
_Unilateral / bilateral, effusion since _. Pneumatic otoscopy _. Tympanogram type _. At risk _.

DDx:
>OME; most likely given effusion without bulging TM or acute symptoms, watchful waiting
>AOM; considered but unlikely given no bulging TM, otalgia, or fever, treat if these develop

- Watchful waiting x 3 mo from effusion onset, or from dx if onset unknown, if not at risk
- No abx, steroids, antihistamines, or decongestants for OME
- Autoinflation is an option during watchful waiting _
- Hearing test if OME 3 mo or longer, or anytime in an at-risk child
- Bilateral OME with hearing loss: counsel on speech and language effects and listening strategies
- Recheck q3-6 mo until effusion resolves, significant hearing loss, or TM structural changes
- ENT for tubes if OME 3 mo or longer with documented hearing difficulty
- ENT for tubes may be offered if OME 3 mo or longer causes balance, school, behavior, or ear discomfort problems
- No tubes for a single OME episode <3 mo
- f/u _ mo

If at risk for speech, language, or learning problems:

- At risk: permanent hearing loss, speech or language delay, autism or developmental delay, Down syndrome, craniofacial syndromes, cleft palate, blindness or uncorrectable vision loss
- Hearing test at dx, do not wait 3 mo
- ENT for tubes if OME unlikely to resolve: type B tympanogram or effusion 3 mo or longer

If adult:

- ENT referral if effusion persists >6 wk, to evaluate for ET obstruction

use: Use for acute drainage through a tympanostomy tube in a child.
body:
#Tympanostomy tube otorrhea
Likely acute tube otorrhea given _drainage after a cold / painless drainage, no fever / purulent drainage, tube visible.
_ ear, tubes placed _, drainage x _ days. Tube patent _. Postauricular findings _.

DDx:
>Acute tube otorrhea; most likely given _, topical drops
>Cholesteatoma, foreign body, or tumor; considered but unlikely given first episode, ENT if persistent or recurrent

- START ciprofloxacin 0.3%-dexamethasone 0.1% otic, 4 drops in affected ear BID x 7 days, if 6 mo or older
- START ofloxacin 0.3% otic, 5 drops in affected ear BID x 10 days, if 1 to 12 yr, as an alternative
- Quinolone drops only, no aminoglycoside drops through a tube
- No oral abx for uncomplicated tube otorrhea
- Drop technique: warm bottle in hand 1-2 min, ear up, pump tragus 4-5x, hold position 1-5 min
- No routine prophylactic water precautions, earplugs, or swim restriction
- Cx drainage if not improved after 1 wk of drops
- ENT if drainage persists after a full course, or 2 or more episodes in 6 mo
- Ear checks until the tube extrudes _
- Handout given

use: Use for suspected acute mastoiditis in a child, usually at admission.
body:
#Acute mastoiditis
Likely acute mastoiditis given _AOM with postauricular swelling, auricle pushed forward / fever, mastoid erythema and tenderness / postauricular fluctuance with otorrhea, irritability.
_ side. Postauricular erythema _, swelling _, fluctuance _, auricle protrusion _. Tmax _. Facial nerve _. CT _.

DDx:
>Acute mastoiditis; most likely given _, IV abx and ENT
>Subperiosteal or intracranial abscess; considered but unlikely given _, CT with contrast
>Mastoid effusion on CT only; considered but unlikely given postauricular findings, effusion alone is not mastoiditis

- Admit, ENT consult for possible surgery
- CT temporal bone with IV contrast if abscess or intracranial extension suspected
- MRI or MR venogram if intracranial or venous sinus complication suspected _
- START ampicillin-sulbactam 50 mg/kg/dose of ampicillin IV q6h, max 2 g/dose, if no intracranial extension
- Cx from myringotomy or drainage, narrow abx to results
- Myringotomy with or without tube, abscess drainage, or mastoidectomy per ENT
- ID consult if abscess, bone destruction, intracranial extension, or no improvement after 48-72 hr
- Neurosurgery consult if intracranial spread or neuro findings
- Watch for facial palsy, meningitis, labyrinthitis, neck abscess, venous sinus thrombosis
- Switch to amoxicillin-clavulanate 90 mg/kg/day of amoxicillin PO divided BID, max 2 g/dose, when improving
- Total abx 14 days if no intracranial extension and adequate source control

If intracranial extension:

- START ceftriaxone 50 mg/kg/dose IV q12h, max 2 g/dose
- START vancomycin 15 mg/kg/dose IV q6h, max 750 mg/dose, if 50 kg or less and <18 yr
- START vancomycin 15 mg/kg/dose IV q8h, max 1 g/dose, if >50 kg or 18 yr or older
- Vancomycin levels and dosing per pharmacy _
- Longer course, duration per ID _

If severe penicillin allergy:

- START levofloxacin 10 mg/kg/dose IV or PO BID, max 375 mg/dose, if 6 mo to <5 yr
- START levofloxacin 10 mg/kg/dose IV or PO daily, max 750 mg/dose, if 5 yr or older

use: Use for a traumatic or AOM-related tympanic membrane perforation.
body:
#Tympanic membrane perforation
Likely TM perforation given _cotton swab injury, sudden pain, bloody otorrhea / slap, blast, or diving injury, sudden hearing loss / AOM with new purulent otorrhea.
_ ear, perforation size _ of TM. Weber lateralizes to _. Vertigo _. Facial weakness _.

>Inner ear injury; considered but unlikely given no vertigo, Weber to affected ear, urgent ENT if present
>Retained foreign body; considered but unlikely given _, ENT if present

- Keep ear dry: petroleum jelly cotton ball for showers, silicone plug for bathing or swimming
- No irrigation or syringing for cerumen
- No aminoglycoside or other ototoxic drops
- Most small perforations heal within 1 mo
- If AOM, treat AOM with oral abx
- Audiogram 3 mo after injury to confirm healing

- Urgent ENT: severe hearing loss, Weber to unaffected ear, vertigo, facial weakness, retained foreign body

- START ofloxacin 0.3% otic, 10 drops in affected ear BID x 14 days, if 12 yr or older
- START ofloxacin 0.3% otic, 5 drops in affected ear BID x 10 days, if 1 to 12 yr
- ENT if otorrhea persists after 2 wk of topical abx

use: Use for the A&P of cerumen impaction, separate from the removal procedure note.
body:
#Cerumen impaction
Likely cerumen impaction given _muffled hearing, fullness, wax hides TM / wax hides TM in hearing aid user / wax hides TM, nonverbal patient.
_Left / right / bilateral. TM visible _. Symptoms _. TM perforation, tubes, or prior ear surgery _.

DDx:
>Cerumen impaction; most likely given _, removal
>_; considered but unlikely given _, reassess if symptoms persist after wax removed

- Treat if symptomatic or wax blocks a needed exam, asymptomatic wax may be observed
- START carbamide peroxide 6.5% otic, 5 to 10 drops in affected ear BID up to 4 days, if >12 yr
- Water or saline drops are as effective, no cerumenolytic proven superior
- Irrigation with body-temperature water, or manual removal under direct view _
- If irrigation fails, instill water, wait 15 min, then repeat
- Recheck canal and symptoms after the first attempt, consider another dx if symptoms persist
- No cotton swabs or objects in the canal, no ear candling
- Home bulb syringe irrigation is an option for selected adults, no home jet irrigators
- ENT if repeated attempts fail, or pain or vertigo during removal

If TM perforation, tubes, prior ear surgery, or abnormal canal:

- No irrigation or cerumenolytic drops, manual removal or ENT

If diabetes or immunocompromised:

- Higher otitis externa risk after irrigation, consider manual removal _

If anticoagulant, antiplatelet, or bleeding disorder:

- Avoid traumatic irrigation or removal, refer if needed

If hearing aid user:

- Canal check q3-6 mo

use: Use for suspected sudden sensorineural hearing loss in an adult, an urgent problem.
body:
#Sudden sensorineural hearing loss
Likely SSNHL given _one-sided loss over <72 hr, normal TM / one-sided loss with dizziness or vertigo / Weber to good ear, normal otoscopy.
Onset _, _left / right. Weber lateralizes to _, Rinne _. Otoscopy _. Neuro exam _.

DDx:
>Idiopathic SSNHL; most likely given _, steroids and urgent audiometry
>Conductive loss from cerumen or effusion; considered but unlikely given normal otoscopy, Weber to good ear
>Retrocochlear lesion; considered but unlikely given _, MRI or ABR

- Emergency: urgent ENT referral, audiometry as soon as possible and within 14 days of onset
- Same-day tuning fork: Weber to good ear and Rinne air louder than bone suggest sensorineural loss
- Check for bilateral or recurrent loss and focal neuro findings, these need more workup
- No routine head CT or labs
- MRI of head and IACs with and without contrast, or ABR, for retrocochlear lesion
- START prednisone 1 mg/kg PO daily as a single dose, max 60 mg, x 7-14 days, best within 2 wk of onset
- DECR. prednisone over a similar 7-14 days after the full-dose course
- START methylprednisolone 48 mg PO daily or dexamethasone 10 mg PO daily as alternatives, same timing
- Hyperbaric oxygen with steroids is an option within 2 wk, or as salvage within 1 mo _
- Intratympanic steroid by ENT if incomplete recovery 2-6 wk after onset
- No antivirals, thrombolytics, vasodilators, or vasoactive agents
- Repeat audiometry at end of treatment and within 6 mo after
- Audiologic rehab and hearing aids if residual loss or tinnitus

body:
#Eustachian tube dysfunction
Likely ETD given _ear fullness, popping after a cold / muffled hearing, allergies, retracted TM / ear pressure with flying or diving.
_Left / right / bilateral, x _ wk. TM _. Tympanogram _. Nasal exam _.

DDx:
>Obstructive ETD; most likely given _, _
>Patulous ET; considered but unlikely given no autophony or hearing own breathing, TM not moving with breathing
>OME; considered but unlikely given _, tympanometry

- Treat allergic rhinitis, rhinosinusitis, or reflux if present
- Nasal steroids show no clear benefit for ETD alone
- START fluticasone 50 mcg/spray, 2 sprays each nostril daily, if allergic rhinitis, 12 yr or older
- Autoinflation by nasal balloon or gentle Valsalva, minimal benefit in adults
- Flying: swallow, yawn, or chew gum on descent, avoid flying with URI or active allergies
- Diving: descend and ascend slowly, no diving while congested
- ENT referral if symptoms 3 mo or longer affect quality of life, balloon dilation for selected adults
- f/u _ wk

If adult flying with prior ear pain:

- START pseudoephedrine 120 mg PO once 30 min before departure, if no contraindication

If child flying:

- Nurse, bottle, or sips during descent, pseudoephedrine not effective in children

If adult with effusion >6 wk:

- ENT referral to evaluate for ET obstruction

use: Use for new or chronic tinnitus.
body:
#Tinnitus
Likely primary tinnitus given _bilateral ringing with age-related hearing loss / ringing after loud noise exposure / constant nonpulsatile ringing, normal ear exam.
_Unilateral / bilateral, _pulsatile / nonpulsatile, x _ mo. Bothersome _. Hearing change _. Otoscopy _. Neuro exam _.

DDx:
>Primary tinnitus with hearing loss; most likely given _, audiogram
>Vestibular schwannoma; considered but unlikely given symmetric symptoms, MRI if unilateral or asymmetric
>Vascular cause; considered but unlikely given nonpulsatile, CTA if pulsatile
>Cerumen or ototoxic medication; considered but unlikely given _, _

- Audiogram within 4 wk if chronic, unilateral, or with hearing change
- Urgent audiometry if sudden hearing loss
- Prompt workup for focal neuro signs, vertigo, ear pain or drainage, or papilledema
- No imaging if bilateral, nonpulsatile, symmetric hearing, and normal exam
- MRI of head and IACs with and without contrast if unilateral or asymmetric
- CTA head and neck, or noncontrast temporal bone CT, if pulsatile
- No routine TSH, B12, or glucose testing
- Review ototoxic meds: aminoglycosides, loop diuretics, high-dose aspirin, NSAIDs, quinine, platinum chemo
- CBT referral for chronic bothersome tinnitus
- Sound therapy, and hearing aid evaluation if hearing loss
- No routine benzodiazepines, anticonvulsants, or antidepressants for tinnitus itself
- No supplements such as ginkgo, none proven
- Treat comorbid depression, anxiety, or insomnia, screen for suicidal ideation
- Hearing protection from loud noise
- Nonbothersome tinnitus: education only

body:

Likely ear foreign body given _bead or toy in child's canal / live insect in canal, ear pain / suspected button battery, pain.
_ ear. Object _, time since _. TM _. Canal injury _.

>Retained foreign body; most likely given _, removal
>TM perforation; considered but unlikely given _, recheck TM after removal

- Live insect: kill first with mineral oil or lidocaine if TM intact, then remove
- Removal under direct view with forceps or hook, suction for smooth round objects

- First attempt is the best chance in a young child, ENT if it fails
- Emergent ENT: button battery, penetrating object, expandable object, severe pain
- Expedited ENT: object or dead insect not removed in clinic
- Recheck canal and TM after removal
- START ofloxacin 0.3% otic daily x 7 days if canal or TM trauma: 5 drops if <13 yr, 10 drops if 13 or older
- Keep ear dry and ENT referral if TM perforation suspected

use: Use for probable, confirmed, or severe sarcopenia in an older adult.
body:
#Sarcopenia
Likely sarcopenia given _feeling weak, trouble rising from a chair / slow walking and falls / weight loss with muscle wasting.
SARC-F _ of 10. Grip _ kg, 5x chair stand _ sec. ASMI _ kg/m2 by _. Gait speed _ m/s, SPPB _ of 12.

DDx:
>Sarcopenia, _probable / confirmed / severe; most likely given _, _
>Depression; considered but unlikely given _, PHQ-9 _
>Stroke, balance disorder, or peripheral vascular disease; considered but unlikely given _, exam _

- Find: SARC-F 4 or more, or falls, weakness, slow gait, trouble rising from a chair, weight loss
- Probable sarcopenia: grip <27 kg men, <16 kg women, or 5x chair stand >15 sec
- Confirmed: low muscle mass by DXA or BIA, ASMI <7.0 kg/m2 men, <5.5 kg/m2 women
- Severe: plus gait speed 0.8 m/s or less, SPPB 8 or less, or TUG 20 sec or more
- Probable sarcopenia is enough to start exercise and protein while muscle mass testing is pending
- Secondary causes: inactivity, malnutrition, inflammatory disease, malignancy, organ failure _
- Progressive resistance training 2-3 days/wk, nonconsecutive, 2-3 sets of 8-12 reps at hard effort, plus balance _
- PT referral for supervised progressive resistance and power training _
- Protein 1.0-1.2 g/kg/day, 25-30 g per meal, unless eGFR <30 and not on dialysis
- Protein supplement if dietary protein below goal _
- START creatine monohydrate 3-5 g PO daily with resistance training if desired, small strength gain _
- HMB not recommended, no added benefit with resistance training
- No approved drug therapy for sarcopenia
- Recheck grip, chair stand, gait speed in _ mo

If Asian ancestry:

- Cutoffs: grip <28 kg men, <18 kg women, 5x chair stand 12 sec or more, gait speed <1.0 m/s, SPPB 9 or less

#Malnutrition in an older adult
Likely malnutrition given _weight loss >5% in 6 mo / intake half or less for >1 wk / low BMI with muscle loss.
Weight _ lb, loss _% over _ mo, BMI _. MNA-SF _ of 14. Intake _, dentition _, swallowing _, mood _.

>_; most likely given _, _
>Depression or dementia; considered but unlikely given _, PHQ-9 and Mini-Cog _
>Medication effect; considered but unlikely given _, medication review _
>Malignancy or other chronic disease; considered but unlikely given _, weight loss workup _

- MNA-SF: 12-14 normal, 8-11 at risk, 0-7 malnourished
- Diagnosis needs 1 or more phenotypic plus 1 or more etiologic criterion
- Phenotypic: weight loss >5% in 6 mo or >10% beyond 6 mo, BMI <22 if over 70, or low muscle mass
- Etiologic: intake 50% or less of needs >1 wk, any reduction >2 wk, malabsorption, or inflammation
- Severe: weight loss >10% in 6 mo or >20% beyond 6 mo, or BMI <20 if over 70
- Causes: dementia, dentition, depression, diarrhea, disease, drugs, dysfunction, dysgeusia, dysphagia _
- Energy about 30 kcal/kg/day. Protein 1.0 g/kg/day or more, 1.2-1.5 g/kg/day with acute or chronic illness.
- Liberalize dietary restrictions. Fortified foods, snacks, finger foods, shared meals _
- Home-delivered meals, food access, feeding help _
- START oral nutritional supplement PO between meals, not in place of meals, 400 kcal and 30 g protein/day or more
- Supplement for 1 mo or longer; check weight, intake, and adherence monthly
- Dietitian referral, 2 or more sessions _
- Oral care, dental exam, denture fit _
- Resistance and balance exercise alongside nutrition support _
- No routine appetite stimulants. Megestrol: avoid, minimal weight effect, more thrombosis and possibly death.

- SLP swallow evaluation, texture-modified diet if needed _

- Refeeding risk: K, Mg, phos before feeding and during advance _
- START thiamine 100 mg PO daily before feeding, x 5-7 days
- Advance intake slowly _

use: Use for the A&P of suspected or confirmed classic or incomplete Kawasaki disease in a child.
body:
#Kawasaki disease, _classic / incomplete
Likely Kawasaki disease given _fever 5 days, rash, red eyes, cracked lips / infant, long fever, irritability only / long fever, neck node, no abx response.
Fever day _. Lips and mouth _, conjunctivae _, rash _, hands and feet _, cervical node _ cm.
CRP _, ESR _, WBC _, Hgb _, plt _, albumin _, ALT _, UA WBC _. Echo LAD z _, RCA z _.

DDx:
>Kawasaki disease; most likely given _, IVIG and echo
>Other febrile exanthem; considered but unlikely given no exudative conjunctivitis or pharyngitis, vesicles, or generalized nodes _
>_; considered but unlikely given _, _

- Classic: fever 5 days or more plus 4 or more of 5 principal features. Day 1 is the first day of fever
- Features: oral changes, nonexudative bulbar conjunctival injection, rash, hand and foot erythema or edema or periungual peeling, cervical node 1.5 cm or more
- Dx at 4 days of fever allowed if 4 or more features, especially red, swollen hands and feet
- Another dx more likely if exudative conjunctivitis or pharyngitis, oral ulcers, vesicular rash, generalized nodes, or splenomegaly
- Incomplete: evaluate if fever 5 days or more with 2-3 features, or infant with 7 days or more of unexplained fever
- Labs: CBC with diff, CRP, ESR, CMP with albumin and ALT, UA, urine cx
- Supplemental labs: anemia for age, plt 450,000 or more after day 7, albumin 3.0 g/dL or less, elevated ALT
- Supplemental labs also: WBC 15,000 or more, urine 10 WBC/hpf or more with negative urine cx
- Echo positive: LAD or RCA z-score 2.5 or more, aneurysm, or 3 or more suggestive features
- Echo at dx, do not delay IVIG for it. Repeat at 1-2 wk and 4-6 wk after treatment
- Admit for IVIG, peds cardiology consult _ local
- START IVIG 2 g/kg IV once over 10-12 hr, max 100 g, within 10 days of fever onset
- START aspirin _30-50 / 80-100 mg/kg/day PO divided q6h until afebrile 48-72 hr
- DECR. aspirin to 3-5 mg/kg PO daily until no coronary change at 6-8 wk from onset
- Avoid ibuprofen while on aspirin, it blocks the antiplatelet effect
- Do not use ESR to judge IVIG response, IVIG raises ESR
- Defer MMR and varicella vaccines 11 mo after IVIG
- Inactivated influenza vaccine for child 6 mo or older and household, before d/c in flu season
- d/c when afebrile 36 hr after IVIG and hydrated without IV fluids _ local
- f/u PCP in 2-3 days, peds cardiology 2 wk and 6 wk after onset

If incomplete KD with CRP 3.0 mg/dL or more or ESR 40 or more:

- Treat if 3 or more supplemental labs positive or echo positive

If incomplete KD with CRP <3.0 mg/dL and ESR <40:

- Reassess daily while febrile, echo if typical peeling develops

If fever day 10 or later:

- IVIG if persistent fever, or coronary abnormality with CRP >3.0 mg/dL or raised ESR
- No IVIG if afebrile, no marked inflammation, and normal echo

If fever 36 hr or more after IVIG ends:

- START 2nd IVIG 2 g/kg IV once, max 100 g, and consult rheumatology
- Alternatives: infliximab or tapering steroid course with cardiology and rheumatology _

If high risk, age 6 mo or younger, z-score 2.5 or more, or shock:

- START methylprednisolone 1 mg/kg IV BID, max 60 mg/day, while febrile, with IVIG _ local
- Then prednisolone 1 mg/kg PO BID; taper once CRP normal _ local

If influenza or varicella while on aspirin:

- Reye syndrome risk: switch to an alternative antiplatelet for at least 2 wk with cardiology _

use: Use for the A&P of suspected intussusception in an infant or young child.
body:
#Intussusception
Likely intussusception given _colicky pain, knees drawn up, well between / vomiting, intermittent crying spells / lethargy or pallor, +/- bloody stool.
Age _, sx duration _ hr. Vomiting _, bloody stool _, mass _, peritoneal signs _. HR _, BP _. US _.

DDx:
>Intussusception; most likely given _, US _
>Pathologic lead point, e.g. Meckel diverticulum, polyp, or lymphoma; considered but unlikely given age _, _
>Perforation or peritonitis; considered but unlikely given _, KUB for free air _
>_; considered but unlikely given _, _

- Peak 6 mo-3 yr, 70% before age 2. Classic triad in only about 20%
- Currant jelly stool is a late finding, do not wait for it
- US is test of choice: sensitivity about 98%, target or pseudokidney sign
- POCUS by a trained clinician: sensitivity about 100%, specificity 94-95%
- Abdominal x-ray only for free air or obstruction, if ill appearing
- IV access, NPO, 20 mL/kg IV fluid bolus before enema
- Peds surgery aware before enema _ local
- Air or contrast enema under fluoro or US. Success about 83% air vs 70% liquid
- Enema perforation risk about 0.4%. Up to 3 attempts is standard
- Delayed repeat enema after partial reduction if stable, about 50% success
- Post-reduction: _ED observation 2 hr or more, d/c if well (APSA) / admit overnight for occult perforation (Merck)
- d/c if normal vitals, pain free, tolerating PO, active, no frank blood in stool
- Recurrence 8-15%, most within the first 1-3 days. Recurrence is still treated by enema
- Lead point workup if age >5 yr or multiple recurrences
- Return for recurrent pain episodes, vomiting, bloody stool, or lethargy

If free air, peritonitis, shock, or unstable:

- No enema. Emergent peds surgery consult

If enema fails or lead point found:

- Admit, peds surgery for operative reduction

use: Use for the A&P of a pulled elbow (nursemaid's elbow) in a young child.
body:
#Radial head subluxation, _right / left
Likely radial head subluxation given _pulled by hand, won't use arm / arm held still after a pull / no use of arm, no swelling.
Age _, mechanism _. Swelling _, bruising _, deformity _, tenderness outside radial head _. Distal pulses and cap refill _.

DDx:
>Radial head subluxation; most likely given _, reducing today
>Elbow or forearm fracture; considered but unlikely given no deformity, swelling, or bruising _, x-ray if present
>_; considered but unlikely given _, _

- Neurovascular exam before reduction: distal pulses, cap refill
- X-ray first, no reduction, if deformity, swelling, bruising, or tenderness outside the radial head _
- X-ray also if fall or direct blow, atypical mechanism, or unclear history _
- No reduction if neurovascular compromise or signs of infection
- Position: child on caregiver's lap, elbow at 90 degrees, thumb over radial head, other hand at wrist
- Hyperpronation first: rapidly hyperpronate the forearm. First-attempt failure 9% vs 26% with supination-flexion
- Click or pop may be felt. Brief crying expected, no analgesia needed
- Observe up to 30 min with a toy or snack; nearly all use the arm by then
- No sling or immobilization after successful reduction
- Recurrence is common, more often in young children
- Prevention: lift under the arms, never pull or swing by the hands or arms

If first attempt fails:

- Repeat hyperpronation, or supination-flexion: rapid supination then full elbow flexion in one motion

If not using arm 30 min after reduction:

- 2nd attempt, x-ray of the elbow, or d/c with recheck next day _

use: Use for the A&P of Osgood-Schlatter disease in an active older child or adolescent.
body:
#Osgood-Schlatter disease, _right / left / bilateral
Likely Osgood-Schlatter disease given _tibial tubercle pain with running, jumping / tender, swollen tibial tubercle in growth spurt / knee pain kneeling, young athlete.
Tibial tubercle tenderness _, swelling _, pain with resisted knee extension _. Quad and hamstring tightness _.

DDx:
>Osgood-Schlatter disease; most likely given _, clinical dx
>Fracture, tumor, or infection; considered but unlikely given _, x-ray if severe or atypical
>_; considered but unlikely given _, _

- Clinical dx. No x-ray unless severe or atypical presentation _
- Activity as tolerated is safe and causes no long-term damage
- Goal: a dull ache that does not limit sport and settles soon after
- Pain during sport means stop that session; mild soreness afterward is OK
- Brief rest from aggravating sport only if limping or pain at rest
- Ice 15-20 min after activity, never directly on skin. No ice or NSAID before sport
- Quad and hamstring stretches: hold 30 sec x 3 per leg, 1-2x/day after exercise, no bouncing
- Strengthening: static quad holds 10 x 30 sec and double-leg bridges daily x 4 wk
- Then progress isometric holds >> squats >> lunges through wk 12
- Cross-train with swimming or cycling, less tendon load
- Patellar tendon strap below the kneecap optional
- START ibuprofen 10 mg/kg PO q6-8h PRN, max 40 mg/kg/day. Eases pain, does not shorten course
- No corticosteroid injection: skin atrophy and tendon rupture risk
- Return to sport when full painless motion and can jog, sprint, and hop without pain
- Usually settles after the growth spurt; tubercle bump may persist
- f/u in _ wk

If persistent after growth plate closure:

- Ortho referral, ossicle excision rarely needed
