use: Use for the A&P of iron deficiency with or without anemia in an infant, child or teen, from screening through treatment.
body:
#Iron deficiency, _with anemia / without anemia
Likely iron deficiency given _toddler drinking over 24 oz milk daily / breastfed infant with few iron-rich foods / teen with heavy menstrual bleeding.
Age _, wt _ kg. Hgb _, MCV _, ferritin _, CRP _. Milk intake _ oz/day. Lead _.

DDx:
>Iron deficiency; most likely given _, iron trial
>Lead exposure; considered but unlikely given _, blood lead _
>_; considered but unlikely given _, reevaluate if no Hgb response

- Screen with CBC plus ferritin; Hgb alone only if both not possible
- Screen at 9-12 mo if mostly breastfed, 15-18 mo if formula fed, after switch to milk
- Rescreen every well visit to age 4 if ongoing risk, such as excess milk
- Iron deficiency: ferritin 20 ng/mL or less in young children. Ferritin rises with inflammation, CRP _
- Anemia severity: mild Hgb 9 or more, moderate 7 to <9, severe <7 g/dL
- START ferrous sulfate 3 mg/kg elemental iron PO once daily
- Give with water or juice, not milk. Separate from calcium supplements
- Liquid iron stains teeth: mix with water or juice, brush after dose
- Milk: none before 12 mo. 16 oz/day at 12-24 mo, 16-24 oz/day at 2-5 yr, never >24 oz/day
- Iron-rich foods: beans, lentils, tofu, beef, fortified cereal, with a vitamin C food
- Store iron out of reach: overdose is a leading cause of fatal poisoning under age 6
- Recheck CBC in 1 mo: mild should normalize, moderate or severe Hgb up 2 g/dL or more
- CONT same dose at least 3 mo, ferritin at 3 mo
- CONT 3 more mo if ferritin <20 ng/mL at 3 mo
- Still anemic at 3 mo or recurrence within 2 yr: confirm dx, check adherence, find cause

If adolescent:

- Screen CBC plus ferritin 1 yr or more after menarche, by age 14. Yearly if heavy menses
- Iron deficiency: ferritin 30 ng/mL or less in teens and menstruating patients
- START ferrous sulfate 65 mg elemental iron PO once daily

If severe anemia, stable, reliable family:

- Oral iron, recheck CBC in 7-10 days

If clinically unstable:

- Admit, transfuse slowly in small aliquots

If oral iron fails or absorption impaired:

- IV iron, peds hematology referral

use: Use for the A&P of a simple febrile seizure in a child 6 to 60 months old.
body:
#Simple febrile seizure
Likely simple febrile seizure given _brief generalized seizure, first day of fever / seizure before other illness signs / seizure with URI, AOM, or roseola.
Age _ mo, Tmax _. Seizure _ min, generalized _, single in 24 hr _. Postictal _, neuro exam _, meningeal signs _.
Immunizations _, prior abx _, fever source _.

DDx:
>Simple febrile seizure; most likely given _, treating fever source
>Meningitis or encephalitis; considered but unlikely given no meningeal signs _, LP if signs
>Complex febrile seizure; considered but unlikely given <15 min, generalized, single _
>_; considered but unlikely given _, _

- Simple: age 6-60 mo, temp 38.0 C or higher, generalized, <15 min, once in 24 hr
- Simple also requires no CNS infection and no prior neurologic problem
- No routine EEG, neuroimaging, CBC, or electrolytes for the seizure itself
- Evaluate and treat the fever source _
- LP if meningeal signs: neck stiffness, Kernig, Brudzinski
- Admission usually not needed. Consider if young, abnormal exam, or unreliable f/u
- Recurrence about 1 in 3. Risk factors: age <18 mo, fever <1 hr before seizure, first-degree relative, temp <40 C
- 2-yr recurrence by number of risk factors: 0 is 14%, 1 is 24%, 2 is 32%, 3 is 63%, 4 is 75%
- Epilepsy risk after simple febrile seizure _2.4% (AAFP) / 2-6% (Merck), slightly above general population
- Antipyretics for comfort only, they do not prevent recurrence
- No continuous or intermittent anticonvulsant ppx
- Seizure >5 min unlikely to stop on its own: benzodiazepine
- Home first aid taught: on side, nothing in mouth, time it
- Return or 911 for seizure 5 min or more, repeat seizure, stiff neck, hard to wake, or breathing trouble

If age 6-12 mo with Hib or pneumococcal vaccines missing or unknown:

- LP is an option

If pretreated with abx:

- LP is an option, abx may mask meningitis

If LP done:

- Blood cx and serum glucose with LP

If home rescue med for prolonged seizures, age 2-5 yr:

- START diazepam rectal gel 0.5 mg/kg PR once PRN seizure 5 min or more, round up to unit dose, max 20 mg

use: Use for the A&P of dehydration in a child with gastroenteritis, including oral rehydration, ondansetron and IV criteria.
body:
#Dehydration, _minimal / mild / moderate to severe
Likely dehydration 2/2 viral gastroenteritis given _vomiting, diarrhea, fewer wet diapers / thirsty, sticky mouth, fewer tears / sunken eyes, dry mouth, no tears.
Wt _ kg, baseline _. Clinical dehydration score _: appearance _, eyes _, mucous membranes _, tears _. Cap refill _, HR _, urine output _.

DDx:
>Viral gastroenteritis; most likely given _, ORS
>Bacterial enteritis; considered but unlikely given no blood or mucus _, stool studies if present
>Surgical abdomen or other serious dx; considered but unlikely given _, _

- Score appearance, eyes, mucous membranes, tears 0-2 each: 0 none, 1-4 mild, 5-8 moderate to severe
- Best single signs: prolonged cap refill, abnormal skin turgor, abnormal breathing pattern
- No routine labs in mild illness
- Stool studies only if blood or mucus, sepsis, immunocompromise, travel, outbreak, or diarrhea >7 days
- Low-osmolarity ORS. Start 5 mL every 1-5 min, increase as tolerated
- Replace ongoing losses: ORS 10 mL/kg per watery stool, 2 mL/kg per emesis
- CONT breastfeeding and usual formula, undiluted. Lactose-free formula not needed
- Age-appropriate diet once rehydrated, no BRAT restriction, no fasting
- Avoid soda, juice, and full-strength sports drinks
- No antidiarrheals; loperamide not for children
- No promethazine or metoclopramide
- Probiotics: _not recommended (AGA) / LGG or S. boulardii x 5-7 days, weak evidence (ESPGHAN)
- Return for no urine in 8 hr, bloody or green vomit, blood in stool, lethargy, or unable to keep ORS down
- f/u in _ days

If mild dehydration:

- ORS 50 mL/kg over 4 hr at home, about 1 mL/kg every 5 min
- Half-strength apple juice, then preferred fluids, is an option

If moderate dehydration:

- ORS 100 mL/kg over 4 hr in clinic or ED
- Consider lytes. Bicarb <13 predicts outpatient failure

If vomiting, age 6 mo or older:

- START ondansetron ODT once: 8-15 kg 2 mg, 15-30 kg 4 mg, >30 kg 8 mg
- Repeat dose once if vomited within 15 min
- Avoid ondansetron in congenital long QT; check lytes if severe

If ORS fails or persistent vomiting:

- NG rehydration with ORS, fewer failures than IV

If severe, shock, or failed ORS and NG:

- NS or LR 20 mL/kg IV over 10-15 min, repeat up to 60 mL/kg in first hr
- 10 mL/kg boluses if frail or malnourished. No hypotonic fluid for boluses
- Lytes, creatinine, glucose
- Admit if IV rehydration fails, social concerns, or suspected serious alternative dx

use: Use for the A&P of an acute limp in a child.
body:
#Limp, _right / left
Likely _transient synovitis given age 4-10, afebrile, well appearing / toddler's fracture given toddler, acute limp, tibial tenderness / SCFE given obese adolescent, knee or thigh pain, limited IR.
Age _, T _, weight-bearing _. Hip ROM and internal rotation _, point tenderness _. WBC _, ESR _, CRP _. X-ray _, hip US _.

DDx:
>_; most likely given _, _
>Septic arthritis or osteomyelitis; considered but unlikely given _, Kocher criteria _
>SCFE or Legg-Calve-Perthes; considered but unlikely given _, x-ray _
>Leukemia, tumor, or nonaccidental trauma; considered but unlikely given _, _

- Hip disease can present as knee or thigh pain; examine the hip in every limp
- Common by age: 1-3 yr toddler's fracture, septic hip, DDH. 4-10 yr transient synovitis, Perthes. 11-16 yr SCFE, overuse
- X-ray AP and lateral of the painful area. Hip: AP pelvis and frog-leg lateral, both hips
- Toddler: AP and lateral tibia; spiral fracture may not show on AP alone
- Red flags: fever, pain that wakes child, constitutional sxs, mass, refusal to bear weight
- Night pain or mass: CBC with diff, alk phos, calcium, lytes, x-ray, MRI _
- Morning-predominant limp: JIA, rheumatology referral _
- Multiple or suspicious fractures: NAT evaluation _ local
- Lyme titers if endemic area exposure _
- Growing pains only if bilateral, only at night, and absent by day
- Return for fever, worse limp, refusal to walk, or night pain

If fever, non-weight-bearing, or ill appearing:

- CBC with diff, ESR, CRP, hip US for effusion
- Kocher criteria: hx of fever, non-weight-bearing, ESR 40 mm/hr or more, WBC >12,000
- Septic arthritis probability with 1, 2, 3, 4 criteria: 3%, 40%, 93%, 99.6%
- Temp >38.5 C and CRP >2.0 mg/dL add predictive value
- Normal US does not exclude septic arthritis; an effusion does not prove it
- Urgent ortho for aspiration if 2 or more criteria or high suspicion; do not wait for MRI
- Synovial fluid cell count, Gram stain, cx. WBC >50,000 presumes infection
- MRI for suspected osteomyelitis, diskitis, or abscess

If transient synovitis:

- START ibuprofen 10 mg/kg PO TID x 5 days, max 40 mg/kg/day
- Recheck in 2-3 days, usually resolves within 1 wk

If SCFE suspected:

- Non-weight-bearing now: crutches or wheelchair
- Stable, walking: AP and frog-leg lateral both hips. Unstable: AP and cross-table lateral, no frog-leg
- Urgent ortho referral same day, no forceful manipulation
- Endocrine workup if age <8 or >15, underweight, or short stature _

If toddler's fracture:

- Removable boot up to 3 wk, no cast needed
- Negative x-ray but suspicion persists: repeat x-ray in 1-2 wk

If Perthes suspected:

- MRI if x-ray normal. Ortho referral
- Exclude hypothyroidism and sickle cell disease _

body:
#Uterine fibroids
Likely uterine fibroids given _heavy menstrual bleeding, enlarged irregular uterus / pelvic pressure, urinary frequency, constipation / incidental fibroids on pelvic imaging.
Uterus _ wk size. Hgb _, ferritin _, pregnancy test _. US: _ fibroids, largest _ cm, submucosal _.

DDx:
>Uterine fibroids; most likely given _, pelvic US _
>Endometrial polyp; considered but unlikely given _, saline infusion sonography if intermenstrual bleeding
>Uterine sarcoma or endometrial cancer; considered but unlikely given _, MRI if rapid growth
>Pregnancy; considered but unlikely given _, pregnancy test _

- Transvaginal and transabdominal pelvic US with Doppler _
- CBC, ferritin _
- Expectant management if no bothersome sxs; sxs usually decrease after menopause
- Return for severe bleeding, lightheadedness, or syncope

If heavy menstrual bleeding:

- START levonorgestrel 52 mg IUD; expulsion more common with fibroids
- START combined oral contraceptive 1 tab PO daily _
- START tranexamic acid 1,300 mg PO TID for up to 5 days during menses
- No tranexamic acid with combined hormonal contraception or thrombosis history or risk
- DECR. tranexamic acid to 1,300 mg PO BID if Cr >1.4 to 2.8
- START naproxen 500 mg PO BID during menses for pain, small effect on bleeding

If first-line therapy fails or is declined:

- START relugolix 40 mg, estradiol 1 mg, norethindrone acetate 0.5 mg 1 tab PO daily
- Start within 7 days of menses onset; limit use to 24 mo for bone loss
- START elagolix 300 mg, estradiol 1 mg, norethindrone acetate 0.5 mg PO qAM plus elagolix 300 mg PO qPM, as alternative
- DXA at baseline and periodically; BP checks on therapy
- Nonhormonal contraception during and for 1 wk after stopping
- Contraindicated: thrombosis history or risk, smoker over 35, uncontrolled HTN, osteoporosis, liver disease, hormone-sensitive cancer, undiagnosed AUB

If preop or bridge to menopause:

- START leuprolide 3.75 mg IM monthly; max 6 mo alone, 12 mo with add-back
- Raises preop Hgb and shrinks uterus; fibroids regrow 6-9 mo after stopping

If iron deficient:

- START ferrous sulfate 325 mg PO daily or every other day

If procedure needed:

- Gyn referral if bothersome sxs despite medical therapy, bulk sxs, infertility or recurrent pregnancy loss with submucosal fibroid, or rapid growth
- Options: hysterectomy, myomectomy if uterus or fertility to be kept, uterine artery embolization, radiofrequency ablation _
- Postmenopausal bleeding: endometrial evaluation for cancer, with or without fibroids
- f/u _ mo

use: Use for the A&P of acute or recurrent nosebleed.
body:
#Epistaxis
Likely anterior epistaxis given _unilateral septal bleed, dry air or nose blowing / recurrent bleeds, child picks nose / bleed on anticoagulant or antiplatelet.
Side _, duration _, recurrent _. BP _, Hgb _. Anticoagulant or antiplatelet _, bleeding disorder hx _, intranasal drug use _. Site on anterior rhinoscopy _.

DDx:
>Anterior epistaxis; most likely given _, site on anterior septum _
>Posterior epistaxis; considered but unlikely given no blood down throat despite anterior pressure _
>Bleeding disorder or HHT; considered but unlikely given _, CBC, PT, PTT if severe or recurrent
>Nasal tumor or foreign body; considered but unlikely given _, endoscopy if recurrent unilateral

- ED if airway concern, hypovolemia, or unstable
- Firm pressure to soft lower third of nose x 10-15 min without release, sitting up, leaning forward
- START oxymetazoline 0.05% 2-3 sprays in bleeding nostril, or soaked pledget, with pressure
- Anterior rhinoscopy after clot removal to find the site
- Cautery only with relative hemostasis: topical anesthetic, silver nitrate around then on the site, never blind
- No routine labs; CBC, PT, PTT if signs of bleeding disorder with severe or recurrent bleeding
- CONT anticoagulant or antiplatelet during first-line care; reverse or hold only if life-threatening bleeding _
- Recheck BP _; HTN rarely the sole cause
- Prevention: saline gel or petroleum jelly inside nose TID, saline spray, humidifier, no picking
- Oxymetazoline no more than 3 days
- f/u _

If bleeding site not seen despite pressure:

- Anterior packing; resorbable if anticoagulant, antiplatelet, or suspected bleeding disorder
- Nonresorbable packing stays 48 hr, removal _; abx not routinely needed

If suspected posterior bleed:

- ED and ENT if blood down throat despite anterior pressure, or failed anterior packing
- Posterior packing: admit
- ENT for arterial ligation or embolization if not controlled by packing or cautery

If recurrent:

- ENT for nasal endoscopy if recurrent despite packing or cautery, or recurrent unilateral
- Look for nasal and oral telangiectasias for HHT if recurrent bilateral bleeds or family hx
- CT if foreign body, tumor, or sinusitis suspected

If child:

- Nose picking is the most common cause; keep nails short, petroleum jelly inside nose
- Oxymetazoline: OTC label age 6 or older; clinician discretion age 2-5; never <2

#Hypernatremia
Likely 2/2 _poor water intake given dementia, no water access / GI losses given vomiting or diarrhea / diabetes insipidus given polyuria, dilute urine.

>Iatrogenic sodium load; considered but unlikely given _, review hypertonic saline, bicarbonate, tube feeds

- Free water deficit (L) = TBW x wt (kg) x (Na/140 - 1)
- TBW 0.6 men or children, 0.5 women or men >65, 0.45 women >65
- Goal Na 145; give deficit over 24 hr (AAFP) / 48 hr if chronic (Merck), within the rate limit below
- Adults: lower Na up to 12 mEq/L per 24 hr
- Do not raise Na again if correction exceeds 12 mEq/L per 24 hr
- START free water _ mL PO or per tube q_ hr, preferred route
- START D5W _ mL/hr IV if enteral water not possible
- Avoid NS unless hypovolemic, it can worsen hypernatremia
- Glucose q_ hr on D5W, glucosuria risk especially with diabetes
- BMP q_ hr during correction, watch K and bicarbonate
- Strict I/O, track urine free water losses with urine Na and K _
- HOLD loop diuretics, lithium, hypertonic fluids if able _
- Seizures or coma: ICU evaluation

If acute onset <24 hr:

- Correct over 24 hr, up to 1 mEq/L/hr

If infant or child:

- Lower Na <0.5 mEq/L/hr, <12 mEq/L per 24 hr

If hypovolemic:

- START NS _ for volume, replace free water separately

If hypervolemic:

- START D5W for free water deficit
- START furosemide _ mg IV

If urine osm <300 with Na >145:

- Suspect DI; review lithium, amphotericin, foscarnet, demeclocycline

use: Use for documenting RBC, platelet, plasma, or cryo transfusion decisions and reactions.
body:
#Blood product transfusion
_Transfusion indicated / not indicated given Hgb _, bleeding _.
Hgb _ from _, plt _, INR _, PTT _, fibrinogen _. Type and screen _.

- Transfusion consent _
- RBC: transfuse 1 unit at a time if not bleeding, reassess sxs and Hgb after each unit
- Each unit raises Hgb about 1 g/dL
- Hemodynamically stable adult: transfuse for Hgb <7

If cardiac surgery:

- Transfuse for Hgb <7.5

If orthopedic surgery or preexisting cardiovascular disease:

- Transfuse for Hgb <8

If ACS with anemia, not actively bleeding:

- Transfuse to keep Hgb 10 or higher (ACC/AHA), or for Hgb <8 (AABB)

If critically ill child, stable, no cyanotic heart disease or hemoglobinopathy:

- Transfuse for Hgb <7

If high risk for fluid overload, such as HF or severe CKD:

- Transfuse slowly, START furosemide _ mg IV with transfusion _

If considering platelets:

- Plt <10,000 if hypoproliferative or consumptive, not bleeding
- Plt <10,000 before CVC at a compressible site
- Plt <20,000 before LP or low-risk IR procedure
- Plt <50,000 before major nonneuraxial surgery or high-risk IR procedure
- Plt <50,000 with active bleeding
- No platelets for nonoperative ICH with plt >100,000, even on antiplatelets

If considering plasma or cryo:

- No plasma for INR <1.8 before a procedure
- Plasma 10-15 mL/kg for bleeding with PT or PTT >1.5x normal
- Warfarin reversal: 4-factor PCC, plasma only if PCC unavailable
- Cryo 15-20 units for major bleeding with fibrinogen 150 mg/dL or less

If transfusion reaction suspected:

- STOP transfusion, keep IV open with NS, recheck patient and unit ID
- Notify blood bank, send unit and patient samples
- Do not restart that unit or other issued units
- Hemolysis labs: DAT, urine Hgb, LDH, bilirubin, haptoglobin
- Fever rise 1 C or more: START acetaminophen _ mg PO, evaluate as possible hemolysis
- Urticaria or itching only: START diphenhydramine 50 mg PO or IV, may resume transfusion
- Generalized urticaria or mild bronchospasm: START hydrocortisone 100-200 mg IV too
- Anaphylaxis: START epinephrine 0.5 mg IM, NS IV, hold further transfusion
- TACO: START furosemide 20-40 mg IV, treat as HF
- TRALI: supportive care, avoid diuretics, report to blood bank
- Acute hemolysis: NS to UOP 100 mL/hr, START furosemide 40-80 mg IV, early nephrology
- Prior febrile reactions: acetaminophen premed, leukoreduced products
- IgA deficiency with anaphylaxis: washed products

use: Use for outpatient warfarin follow-up and INR-based dose adjustment.
body:
#Warfarin anticoagulation
_In / above / below goal INR on current regimen, _.
Indication _, goal INR _. INR _ today, prior _. Weekly dose _ mg. Bleeding _, missed doses _, new meds _.

- CONT warfarin _ mg PO daily, weekly total _ mg
- Goal INR 2-3: AF, VTE, bileaflet mechanical aortic valve without risk factors
- Goal INR 2.5-3.5: mechanical mitral valve, or mechanical aortic valve with risk factors
- Goal INR 1.5-2: On-X aortic valve after 3 mo, no risk factors, with aspirin 75-100 mg daily
- One INR off by 0.5 or less, previously stable: CONT dose, recheck in 1-2 wk
- Recheck in 1 wk after a 10-20% change or starting or stopping an interacting drug
- Recheck in 1-2 wk after a 5-10% change
- Stable dose: q4 wk if <6 mo, q6-8 wk if 6 mo or more, up to 12 wk (CHEST)
- Interacting drugs that raise INR: amiodarone, azoles, TMP-SMX, metronidazole, fluoroquinolones, macrolides
- Interacting drugs that lower INR: rifampin, carbamazepine, barbiturates, nafcillin
- Avoid NSAIDs and antiplatelets unless clearly indicated
- Diet: consistent vitamin K intake week to week, no routine vitamin K supplements
- Missed dose: take same day, do not double the next day
- Review indication, duration, and DOAC candidacy at least yearly

If out of range, goal 2-3, no bleeding, per clinic nomogram _ local:

- INCR. weekly dose 10-20% plus 1 extra dose if INR <1.5, recheck 1 wk
- INCR. weekly dose 5-10% if INR 1.5-1.9, recheck 1-2 wk
- DECR. weekly dose 5-10% if INR 3.1-4, recheck 1-2 wk
- HOLD 1 dose, DECR. weekly dose 10% if INR 4.1-5, recheck 1 wk
- HOLD 1-2 doses, DECR. weekly dose 10-20% if INR 5.1-9, recheck within 1 wk
- No routine vitamin K if INR 4.5-10

If out of range, goal 2.5-3.5, no bleeding:

- INCR. weekly dose 10-20% plus 1 extra dose if INR <1.9
- INCR. weekly dose 5-10% if INR 1.9-2.4
- DECR. weekly dose 5-10% if INR 3.6-4.5
- HOLD 1 dose, DECR. weekly dose 10% if INR 4.6-5

If INR >10, no bleeding:

- HOLD warfarin, START vitamin K 2.5-5 mg PO once, recheck INR in 1-2 days
- Resume at 10-20% lower weekly dose when INR in range

If minor bleeding:

- HOLD warfarin, INR today, same-day evaluation _

If major bleeding:

- STOP warfarin, ED now
- START 4-factor PCC IV by INR and weight, plus vitamin K 5-10 mg slow IV

- Moderate: Vmax 3-3.9 m/s or mean gradient 20-39 mmHg, TTE every 1-2 yr
- Severe: Vmax 4 m/s or more or mean gradient 40 mmHg or more, TTE every 6-12 mo

- AVR reasonable if low surgical risk with Vmax 5 m/s or more, BNP >3x normal, or Vmax rise 0.3 m/s/yr or more

Ca _ (ULN _), PTH _, 25-OH vit D _, Cr _, eGFR or CrCl _. 24-hr urine Ca _. DXA T-score spine _, hip _, distal 1/3 radius _. Stones _.

- Urine Ca/Cr clearance ratio <0.01: consider familial hypocalciuric hypercalcemia, genetic testing _

- Thiazides and lithium can raise Ca and PTH and skew urine Ca; review need _

use: Use for the A&P of known primary or secondary adrenal insufficiency on replacement.
body:
#Adrenal insufficiency
_Primary / secondary adrenal insufficiency, _adequately / under / over-replaced on current regimen, _.
Weight _, orthostatic BP _, Na _, K _, glucose _. Crises or ED visits since last visit _.

- CONT hydrocortisone _ mg PO on waking and _ mg PO early afternoon, total 15-25 mg/day
- Titrate by weight, postural BP, energy, and signs of excess; no ACTH or cortisol levels to guide dose
- Sick-day rules: double hydrocortisone if temp >38 C (100.4 F), triple if >39 C (102.2 F), until well, usually 2-3 days
- Extra electrolyte-containing fluids during illness
- Unable to take PO, vomiting, or trauma: hydrocortisone 100 mg IM or SQ, then ED
- Rx emergency kit: hydrocortisone sodium succinate 100 mg vial with syringe and needle; teach patient and family to inject
- Medical alert ID and steroid emergency card
- Minor to moderate procedure: hydrocortisone 25-75 mg/24 hr x 1-2 days
- Major surgery or trauma: hydrocortisone 100 mg IV, then 200 mg/24 hr infusion or 50 mg IV/IM q6h
- Phenytoin, carbamazepine, St John's wort speed cortisol clearance; avoid licorice and grapefruit juice
- Endocrinology review at least yearly _
- Adrenal crisis signs (vomiting, severe weakness, hypotension, confusion): hydrocortisone 100 mg IM/IV now, then ED

If poor adherence to multiple daily doses:

- START prednisolone 3-5 mg PO daily in place of hydrocortisone

If primary adrenal insufficiency:

- CONT fludrocortisone _ mg PO every morning, usual 0.05-0.2 mg/day; no salt restriction
- Monitor salt craving, orthostasis, edema, K; renin near upper normal suggests adequate dose
- Periodic screening for autoimmune thyroid disease, diabetes, celiac disease, B12 deficiency _

If hypertension on fludrocortisone:

- DECR. fludrocortisone and review glucocorticoid dose
- START ARB or ACEi if HTN persists; avoid diuretics; spironolactone and eplerenone contraindicated

If pregnant:

- Review each trimester; hydrocortisone preferred, no dexamethasone
- INCR. hydrocortisone as needed in 3rd trimester, often 20-40% from wk 24
- Active labor: hydrocortisone 100 mg IV, then 200 mg/24 hr

If child:

- Hydrocortisone about 8 mg/m2/day PO in 3 to 4 divided doses, managed with pediatric endocrinology
- F/u in _ mo

body:
#Hyperprolactinemia
Likely _prolactinoma given oligo-amenorrhea, galactorrhea, prolactin >250 / medication related given antipsychotic or other dopamine blocker / macroprolactinemia given high prolactin without symptoms.
Prolactin _ (ULN _), hCG _, TSH _, Cr _, LFTs _. Meds _. Pituitary MRI _, visual fields _.

DDx:
>Prolactinoma; most likely given _, pituitary MRI with gadolinium
>Medication related; considered but unlikely given _, review dopamine blockers, antidepressants, estrogen
>Primary hypothyroidism or CKD; considered but unlikely given _, TSH and Cr
>Macroprolactinemia; considered but unlikely given _, macroprolactin by PEG precipitation

- One prolactin drawn without venipuncture stress is usually enough; repeat fasting on another day if borderline
- hCG, TSH, CMP; exclude pregnancy, breastfeeding, hypothyroidism, kidney or liver failure
- Review meds: antipsychotics and other dopamine blockers, antidepressants, estrogen-containing contraceptives
- Macroprolactin by PEG precipitation if asymptomatic
- Pituitary MRI with gadolinium once secondary causes excluded
- Tumor >3 cm with only modest prolactin: ask lab for 1:100 dilution to exclude hook effect
- Visual field testing if macroadenoma near the optic chiasm
- Endocrinology referral for prolactinoma _
- Urgent eval for new visual loss or severe headache with a known macroadenoma

If symptomatic prolactinoma or macroadenoma:

- Baseline echocardiogram before cabergoline
- START cabergoline 0.25 mg PO twice weekly
- INCR. cabergoline by 0.25 mg twice weekly no sooner than q4 wk to normal prolactin, max 1 mg twice weekly
- Recheck prolactin _ wk after each dose change
- Repeat echo q5 yr if dose 2 mg/wk or less, yearly if endocrinology goes higher for resistance
- Counsel on rare compulsive behaviors or psychosis on dopamine agonists
- Taper trial after 2 yr or more if prolactin normal and tumor clearly smaller, with endocrinology

If asymptomatic microprolactinoma:

- Treatment not required; monitor prolactin and MRI with endocrinology _

If antipsychotic related:

- Dopamine agonist not routine; may worsen psychosis
- Discuss with psychiatry: dose reduction, switch to lower-prolactin agent, or adjunctive aripiprazole

If pregnant or planning pregnancy:

- Macroadenoma: normalize prolactin and shrink tumor before conception
- STOP cabergoline once pregnancy confirmed
- MRI in pregnancy only for signs of tumor growth, without gadolinium
- No dopamine agonist while breastfeeding
- F/u in _ wk

use: Use for the A&P of known MGUS, with risk-based follow-up.
body:
#MGUS
_Low / intermediate / high-risk MGUS, M-protein _stable / rising, _.
M-protein _ g/dL, isotype _, FLC ratio _. Hgb _, Ca _, Cr _, bone sxs _.

- MGUS: M-protein <3 g/dL, marrow clonal plasma cells <10%, no CRAB features
- Risk factors: M-protein 1.5 g/dL or more, non-IgG isotype, FLC ratio <0.26 or >1.65
- 20-yr progression risk to myeloma: 5% with no risk factors, 21% with 1, 37% with 2, 58% with 3
- No treatment for MGUS itself
- SPEP, CBC, Ca, Cr at each f/u
- DXA _; higher fracture risk
- Hematology referral and repeat labs sooner for CRAB: high Ca, kidney injury, anemia, bone lesions
- Reassess for new peripheral neuropathy _

If low risk (IgG, M-protein <1.5 g/dL, normal FLC ratio):

- Repeat SPEP in 6 mo, then q2-3 yr if stable (IMWG)
- Or clinical exam with SPEP and UPEP q6-12 mo (Merck)
- Bone marrow and skeletal imaging not needed unless CRAB features

If intermediate or high risk:

- Hematology for CRAB testing and bone marrow biopsy with cytogenetics, flow cytometry, FISH
- If negative: SPEP and CBC at 6 mo, then yearly for life

If IgM MGUS:

- CT abdomen to exclude retroperitoneal lymph nodes
- Hematology for any abnormality, to exclude Waldenstrom macroglobulinemia

If light-chain MGUS:

- CBC, Cr, serum FLC, 24-hr UPEP at f/u _
- F/u in _ mo

use: Use for the A&P of known HFE hemochromatosis, including phlebotomy, liver evaluation, and family screening.
body:
#Hereditary hemochromatosis
_C282Y homozygous / C282Y/H63D hemochromatosis, _induction / maintenance phlebotomy, _.
Ferritin _ (goal _), TSAT _, Hgb _, ALT _, AST _, platelets _. Fibrosis stage _.

- Treat C282Y homozygotes with ferritin >300 ng/mL men or >200 ng/mL women and TSAT 45% or more
- Normal ferritin at dx: no phlebotomy, serial ferritin and LFTs _
- Phlebotomy 500 mL weekly; smaller volume or longer interval if not tolerated
- Hgb before each phlebotomy, keep 11 g/dL or higher
- Ferritin monthly during induction to goal 50-100 ng/mL
- Maintenance: ferritin near 50 ng/mL, phlebotomy usually 3-4x/yr
- Avoid iron and vitamin C supplements; dietary iron restriction not needed
- Limit alcohol; intake >60 g/day raises cirrhosis risk about 9-fold
- Chelation only if phlebotomy not tolerated or refractory; PPI not a primary treatment
- Phlebotomy may improve LFTs, cardiac function, fatigue; not diabetes, arthropathy, or hypogonadism
- Screen first-degree relatives: TSAT, ferritin, HFE genotype; for children, test the other parent first

If ferritin >1000, high ALT or AST, or low platelets:

- Hepatology for fibrosis staging, liver biopsy or MRI _

If cirrhosis:

- HCC surveillance: liver US with or without AFP q6 mo, continue after iron depletion
- Liver transplant evaluation if decompensated cirrhosis or HCC

If fibrosis stage 3 or less:

- No routine HCC surveillance

If C282Y/H63D or H63D homozygous:

- Low overload risk from genotype alone; treat MASLD, diabetes, alcohol use first
- Liver biopsy or MRI liver iron if ferritin >1000; phlebotomy if liver iron high
- F/u in _ mo

use: Use for the A&P of restless legs syndrome, including iron repletion, gabapentinoids, and augmentation.
body:
#Restless legs syndrome
Likely RLS given _urge to move legs at rest, eased by walking / evening leg discomfort disrupting sleep / sxs in pregnancy, ESRD, low iron.
Sxs _ days/wk, distress _. Ferritin _, TSAT _, Hgb _, eGFR _. Meds _.

DDx:
>Restless legs syndrome; most likely given urge to move at rest, worse in evening, relieved by movement
>Leg cramps or positional discomfort; considered but unlikely given _, _
>Venous stasis, leg edema, myalgia, or arthritis; considered but unlikely given _, exam _

- Clinically significant if sxs 2x/wk or more with at least moderate distress
- Morning iron, TIBC, TSAT, ferritin; no iron pills or iron-rich foods for 24 hr before
- Stop or reduce aggravators: alcohol, caffeine, sedating antihistamines, serotonergic antidepressants, dopamine antagonists
- Evaluate and treat OSA _
- Mentally engaging activities when sitting
- No iron therapy if TSAT >45%
- Avoid dopamine agonists and levodopa as standard therapy given augmentation risk; never cabergoline

If ferritin 75 or less or TSAT <20%:

- START ferrous sulfate 325 mg (65 mg elemental iron) PO once daily in the evening, with 200 mg vitamin C or orange juice
- Take iron 2 hr apart from calcium, tea, coffee and 4 hr apart from levothyroxine
- Repeat iron panel in 3 mo, iron held 2 days before; goal ferritin >100

If IV iron is needed:

- IV iron if ferritin 75-100, or ferritin 100 or less with oral iron failed or not tolerated
- START ferric carboxymaltose 1000 mg IV once
- Iron panel and symptom check 6-8 wk after infusion

If persistent sxs despite iron:

- START gabapentin 300 mg PO daily, 100 mg if age >65; INCR. to usual 900-2400 mg/day
- START pregabalin 75 mg PO daily, 50 mg if age >65; INCR. to usual 150-450 mg/day
- START gabapentin enacarbil 600 mg PO daily with food about 5 PM; 300 mg if CrCl 30-59

If augmentation on a dopamine agonist:

- Augmentation: sxs start earlier, spread to arms, or grow more intense
- Correct iron and remove aggravating meds first
- START gabapentinoid, then DECR. dopamine agonist slowly; abrupt stop causes severe rebound
- Keep dose at or below pramipexole 0.75 mg/day, ropinirole 4 mg/day, rotigotine 3 mg/day
- Sleep medicine referral if severe or refractory

If refractory, with sleep medicine:

- START oxycodone ER 5-10 mg/day PO, usual 10-40 mg/day
- START methadone 2.5 mg/day PO, usual 5-30 mg/day

If ESRD:

- START gabapentin _, renally dosed
- START iron sucrose IV _ if ferritin <200 and TSAT <20%
- START vitamin C _ PO daily

If pregnant:

- Check ferritin and TSAT; pregnancy-safe drug _
- F/u in _ wk

body:
#Multiple sclerosis
_Relapsing / progressive MS on _, _stable / new sxs since last visit, _.
Last relapse _, last MRI _, gait _. Fatigue _, bladder _, spasticity _, PHQ-9 _. DMT labs _.

- CONT _ disease-modifying therapy, with neurology
- Relapse: new or worse focal deficit >24 hr, after 30 days stable, without fever or infection
- New sxs: CBC, UA with cx to exclude pseudorelapse from infection, fever, or heat
- Vaccines: influenza yearly; no live vaccines on DMTs; delay vaccines during a relapse
- Vaccinate 4-6 wk before starting immunotherapy (AAN); live 4 wk and non-live 2 wk before B-cell therapy (label)
- PHQ-9; depression is common in MS
- Exercise 150 min/wk; progressive resistance 2-3x/wk, 1-3 sets of 8-15 reps, 5-10 exercises
- Balance training 3-6x/wk for 20-60 min; PT or OT referral
- START cholecalciferol _ IU PO daily, 600-4000 IU/day to 25-OH D 20-50 ng/mL; benefit on progression unclear
- Ocrelizumab or ofatumumab: HBV screen, immunoglobulins, LFTs before start; immunoglobulins during therapy
- Natalizumab: anti-JCV antibody periodically; PML risk higher if JCV+, >2 yr on drug, or prior immunosuppressants
- Fingolimod: eye exam at baseline and 3-4 mo, VZV antibody before start, CBC and LFTs; no live vaccines until 2 mo after stopping
- Siponimod: CYP2C9 genotype, ECG, eye exam, CBC, LFTs before start
- Dimethyl fumarate: CBC with lymphocytes before, at 6 mo, then q6-12 mo; hold if lymphocytes <0.5 for >6 mo
- Teriflunomide: ALT monthly x 6 mo, BP, TB screen; pregnancy test and effective contraception
- HOLD natalizumab and urgent MRI if progressive one-sided weakness, vision change, or confusion over days to wk

If relapse with functional deficit:

- START methylprednisolone 1000 mg IV or PO daily x 3 days, no oral taper
- START prednisone 1250 mg PO daily x _ days if oral methylprednisolone not available
- Neurology contact within _ days
- Mild relapse without functional deficit: steroids not needed

body:
#Interstitial lung disease
Likely ILD given _exertional dyspnea, dry cough, bibasilar velcro crackles / clubbing with progressive dyspnea / dyspnea or cough with RA, SSc, or myositis.
HRCT pattern _. FVC _ % pred, DLCO _ % pred. SpO2 rest _ and exertion _, 6MWD _. Exposures _, serologies _.

DDx:
>Idiopathic pulmonary fibrosis; most likely given _, UIP pattern on HRCT, no exposure or CTD
>CTD-associated ILD; considered but unlikely given _, ANA, RF, anti-CCP, myositis panel
>Hypersensitivity pneumonitis; considered but unlikely given _, birds, down feathers, mold, hot tub
>Drug, radiation, or occupational ILD; considered but unlikely given _, amiodarone, methotrexate, nitrofurantoin, asbestos, silica

- HRCT chest without contrast, thin sections 1.5 mm or less, inspiratory and expiratory images, prone optional
- PFTs: spirometry, lung volumes, DLCO
- SpO2 at rest and with exertion, 6-min walk test
- CRP, ESR, ANA by IFA, RF, anti-CCP, myositis panel; SSA and Scl-70 _
- Exposure hx: home, work, hobby, drug, radiation
- Pulmonology or ILD center referral; multidisciplinary discussion if dx uncertain or biopsy considered
- Priority referral if rapid progression, young age at onset, or transplant candidate
- No corticosteroid monotherapy, and no prednisone with azathioprine and NAC, in IPF
- Pneumococcal: PCV20 or PCV21 if age 50 or older, or PCV15 then PPSV23 1 yr later
- RSV vaccine once if age 50-74 with ILD, or age 75 or older; COVID-19 and influenza vaccines _
- Pulmonary rehab referral
- Long-term O2 15 hr/day or more if resting PaO2 55 or lower or SpO2 88% or lower
- Ambulatory O2 if exertional SpO2 88% or lower
- Smoking cessation _
- GERD: treat for sxs only, not to improve IPF outcomes
- Monitor for pulmonary HTN, sleep-disordered breathing, COPD, lung cancer; echo unreliable, RHC confirms PH
- Spirometry and DLCO q3-6 mo
- Progression in 1 yr, 2 of 3: worse sxs, FVC drop 5% or more predicted or DLCO drop 10% or more, worse imaging
- ED for acute worsening dyspnea over <1 mo; evaluate for exacerbation, PE, pneumothorax, infection

If IPF or progressive pulmonary fibrosis, started by pulmonology:

- START nintedanib 150 mg PO BID with food, 100 mg BID if Child-Pugh A
- Nintedanib: LFTs before start, regularly for first 3 mo, then periodically; loperamide and fluids for diarrhea
- START pirfenidone 267 mg PO TID x 7 days, then 534 mg TID x 7 days, then 801 mg TID, IPF only
- Pirfenidone: LFTs monthly x 6 mo, then q3 mo; SPF 50 or higher and protective clothing
- START nerandomilast 18 mg PO BID, alternative for IPF or progressive pulmonary fibrosis

If hypersensitivity pneumonitis:

- Identify and remove the exposure _; nonfibrotic HP has good prognosis with avoidance

If RA, systemic sclerosis, or myositis:

- Rheumatology co-management; PFTs q3-6 mo in the first yr for SSc and myositis
- F/u in _ mo

body:
#Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis
Likely adolescent idiopathic scoliosis given _asymmetry on school screening / uneven shoulders or waist noticed at home / rib hump on forward bend test.
Scoliometer _ degrees, Cobb angle _ degrees, Risser grade _, menarche _, neuro exam _.

DDx:
>Adolescent idiopathic scoliosis; most likely given age 10 or older, painless curve, normal neuro exam _
>Congenital or neuromuscular scoliosis; considered but unlikely given normal neuro exam, no cafe au lait spots or midline hairy patch
>Spinal tumor, infection, or inflammation; considered but unlikely given no significant pain, MRI if red flags

- Adams forward bend test, scoliometer at the rib or lumbar prominence
- Full-spine x-ray for Cobb angle and Risser grade if scoliometer 7 degrees or more
- X-ray cutoff 5 degrees or more if BMI 85th percentile or higher
- X-ray also for an obvious curve, or asymmetry with family hx of scoliosis
- Cobb angle 10 degrees or more confirms scoliosis
- Higher progression risk: age <12 yr, female, family hx, Risser grade 0-1
- Red flags: left thoracic curve, significant pain, neuro deficits, cafe au lait spots, midline hairy patch; MRI and refer
- Not caused by posture or backpacks; sports and activity as usual
- Refer if curve increases on follow-up x-ray
- Handout given _

If Cobb 10-19 degrees:

- Observe, x-ray every 6 mo while growing; PT referral optional _

If Cobb 20-29 degrees:

- X-ray every 6 mo with Risser grade
- Refer to peds ortho for bracing and PT, especially Risser 0-1

If Cobb 30-39 degrees:

- Refer for bracing and/or scoliosis-specific PT; bracing for 25-45 degrees while still growing (AAOS)

If Cobb 40 degrees or more:

- Refer to spine surgery (AAFP); fusion usually considered for curves >45-50 degrees (AAOS)

If braced:

- Brace 18 hr/day or as prescribed; more hours work better
- Brace off for sports
- Check skin under brace daily

- F/u in _ mo

body:
#Obsessive-compulsive disorder
Likely OCD given _contamination fears with washing / harm fears with repeated checking / need for symmetry with ordering.
Y-BOCS _, time on obsessions or compulsions _ hr/day, insight _, PHQ-9 _, GAD-7 _, tics _.

DDx:
>OCD; most likely given _, more than 1 hr/day or marked distress
>Depression or other anxiety disorder; considered but unlikely given PHQ-9 _, GAD-7 _, often comorbid
>_; considered but unlikely given _, _

- Y-BOCS today and at each f/u to track severity
- Screen for suicidal thoughts _
- Refer for CBT with exposure and response prevention (ERP), usually 13-20 weekly sessions
- ERP booster sessions after response to lower relapse risk
- START sertraline 50 mg PO daily
- INCR. sertraline over 4-6 wk to 200 mg PO daily or max tolerated dose
- Adequate trial: 8-12 wk, with 4-6 wk at max tolerated dose
- Monitor for suicidal thoughts in the first 1-2 mo, especially age 24 or younger

- CONT SSRI at least 1-2 yr after response, then taper over several months
- Resume prior dose if symptoms return during taper

- START fluvoxamine 50 mg PO daily; target 200 mg, max 300 mg daily
- START escitalopram 10 mg PO daily; target 20 mg, max 40 mg daily
- START paroxetine 20 mg PO daily; target 40-60 mg, max 60 mg daily
- START citalopram 20 mg PO daily; max 40 mg, 20 mg if age >60 or hepatic impairment

- Refer to psychiatry: severe Y-BOCS, unclear diagnosis, or no response to 2 SSRI trials
- Augmentation via psychiatry after about 3 mo at max SSRI dose: atypical antipsychotic, or clomipramine
- F/u in _ wk during titration, handout given _

HIV Ag/Ab _, creatinine _, hepatitis B serology _, pregnancy test _, PrEP or injectable ARV in past 6 mo _.

- Start ASAP, no later than 72 hr
- Not indicated if exposure carries no substantial HIV risk

use: Use for the A&P of suspected mpox (monkeypox), including testing, isolation, antiviral access and vaccination of contacts.
body:
#Suspected mpox
Likely mpox given _umbilicated anogenital or oral lesions / rectal pain, bloody stools, or proctitis / fever, lymphadenopathy, then pustular rash.
Exposure _ days ago, lesions _ at _, HIV _, CD4 _, travel _.

DDx:
>Mpox; most likely given _, PCR pending
>Syphilis; considered but unlikely given _, RPR _
>Herpes simplex; considered but unlikely given _, HSV PCR _

- Notify state or county health department today for testing and reporting _
- Lesion swabs for mpox PCR: 2 swabs per lesion from 2-3 lesions; results in 2-4 days
- HIV test if status unknown; syphilis, GC/CT NAAT by site, HSV PCR of ulcers
- Pain control; most recover without antivirals
- Isolate at home until rash resolved, often 2-4 wk
- Cover lesions with clothing; medical mask in close contact at home; separate bathroom if possible
- No shared bedding, towels, or dishes; avoid pets; no sex with direct contact
- Clinic PPE and room cleaning _ local
- Return if eye sxs, trouble breathing or swallowing, or confusion

If severe immunocompromise, skin barrier disease, pregnant, breastfeeding, or <18:

- START tecovirimat via CDC EA-IND, through health department: 600 mg PO q12h x 14 days, within 30 min after a fatty meal
- If 120 kg or more: 600 mg PO q8h. If <40 kg: weight-band dose _
- Severe immunocompromise includes HIV with CD4 <200 and organ transplant

If 25% BSA or more, or airway, neuro, cardiac, or eye disease:

- START tecovirimat via CDC EA-IND, plus combination antivirals per CDC consult
- CDC clinical consult 770-488-7100 after hours; admit _

If close contacts exposed:

- START JYNNEOS 0.5 mL SQ ideally within 4 days, up to 14 days; second dose 28 days later
- Contacts watch for sxs x 21 days

If age 18 or older with ongoing risk, never infected:

- START JYNNEOS 0.5 mL SQ x 2 doses 28 days apart
- Risk: MSM, transgender or nonbinary people with STI, more than 1 partner, or sex at venue or event in past 6 mo
- Also: sex partners of people with these risks
- Vaccine after symptoms start or after recovery not expected to help

body:
#Aspiration
Likely _aspiration pneumonitis given abrupt hypoxemia after vomiting / aspiration pneumonia given dysphagia, fever, cough / aspiration pneumonia given sedation, new infiltrate.
Event _, time since event _. SpO2 _, CXR _, WBC _.

DDx:
>Aspiration pneumonitis; most likely given _, supportive care, often resolves in 24-48 hr
>Bacterial aspiration pneumonia; considered but unlikely given _, abx if persistent or progressive
>Lung abscess or empyema; considered but unlikely given _, CT chest with contrast if concern

- HOB >30 degrees, NPO until swallow assessed
- SLP swallow eval and swallow strategies before oral intake
- Minimize sedating meds
- Oral hygiene and dental care if recurrent aspiration
- No routine systemic corticosteroids

- No abx
- Reassess at 48 hr, START abx if not improving or progressing _

- No added anaerobic coverage unless lung abscess or empyema
- Duration 5-7 days, and until clinically stable

- START levofloxacin 750 mg IV or PO daily

If hospital-onset aspiration:

- START piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV q6h
- START vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q8-12h only with MRSA risk factors, pharmacy to dose

If lung abscess or empyema:

- START ampicillin-sulbactam 3 g IV q6h
- ID consult, drainage for empyema, longer abx course _

body:
#Pleural effusion
Likely _HF effusion given small bilateral effusions, volume overload / parapneumonic effusion given fever, pneumonia, unilateral effusion / malignant effusion given known or suspected cancer.
Side _, size _, US _. Fluid/serum protein _, fluid/serum LDH _, pH _, glucose _.

DDx:
>_; most likely given _, _
>Pulmonary embolism; considered but unlikely given _, CTPA if suspected
>HF effusion on diuretics meeting exudate criteria; considered but unlikely given _, albumin gradient >1.2 g/dL

- Thoracentesis if new, unilateral and more than minimal, or with fever or pleuritic pain
- Thoracentesis if not improving after diuresis, dialysis or treatment of the cause
- No diagnostic thoracentesis for small bilateral effusions with likely HF
- US guidance for every pleural procedure
- Fluid: protein, LDH, pH, cell count with diff, Gram stain, cx, cytology; serum protein and LDH same time
- Add glucose if infection, amylase if pancreatic or esophageal concern, TG and cholesterol if milky
- Add ADA or IGRA if TB risk
- Cytology: send 50-60 mL
- Exudate if fluid/serum protein >0.5, fluid/serum LDH >0.6, or fluid LDH >2/3 ULN of serum LDH
- HF favored if albumin gradient >1.2 g/dL, protein gradient >3.1 g/dL, or pleural NT-proBNP >1500 pg/mL
- Therapeutic tap: up to 1.5 L, stop for chest tightness, chest pain or severe cough
- No routine post-procedure CXR unless sxs, air aspirated, or multiple passes

If parapneumonic:

- Simple, pH >7.2, glucose >60, negative Gram stain and cx: abx and close monitoring
- Chest tube if pH <7.2, glucose <40 (AAFP) or <60 (Merck), + Gram stain or cx, pus, or loculations
- Small-bore chest tube, image guided
- START ampicillin-sulbactam 3 g IV q6h for anaerobic coverage
- Pulm or thoracic surgery consult for complicated effusion or empyema
- Abx duration _ wk, guided by drainage and response

If poor drainage or loculated despite chest tube:

- START tPA 10 mg plus DNase 5 mg intrapleural BID x 3 days, 6 doses
- VATS if intrapleural therapy fails

If malignant:

- Recurrent sxs: indwelling pleural catheter or talc pleurodesis by patient preference
- Indwelling catheter instead of pleurodesis if lung does not re-expand
- Thoracoscopy if cytology negative and suspicion persists

body:
#Pneumothorax

Side _, size _. SpO2 _, HR _, BP _. High-risk features _.

>Primary spontaneous PTX; most likely given _, _
>Secondary spontaneous PTX; considered but unlikely given _, manage as secondary if age >50 with significant smoking history
>Tension PTX; considered but unlikely given stable vitals, needle decompression if hemodynamic compromise

- Repeat CXR in 4 hr _
- Supplemental O2 only if hypoxemic
- Smoking cessation, tobacco and marijuana
- Thoracic surgery referral if air leak persists 5-7 days on chest tube
- Thoracic surgery referral for 2nd ipsilateral or 1st contralateral PTX, or pilot or diver

- No flying until 1 wk or more after CXR shows full resolution
- No diving, permanently, unless bilateral open surgical pleurectomy
- Return now for worse dyspnea

body:
#Alcohol-associated hepatitis

Bili _, AST _, ALT _, INR _, Cr _. MDF _, MELD _. Last drink _, PEth _.

>Alcohol-associated hepatitis; most likely given _, _
>DILI or acetaminophen injury; considered but unlikely given _, drug history and acetaminophen level

- Severe if MELD >20 or MDF 32 or higher
- Infection screen before steroids: blood cx, UA and urine cx, CXR, diagnostic paracentesis if ascites

- Liver biopsy only if dx unclear and result would change mgmt
- Nutrition: 35 kcal/kg/day, protein 1.2-1.5 g/kg/day, dietitian consult
- Oral or enteral nutrition support if intake <21 kcal/kg/day
- START thiamine, B12 and zinc repletion _
- Withdrawal monitoring _
- No pentoxifylline
- Abstinence counseling, addiction medicine or SW consult

If severe and no contraindication to steroids:

- Contraindications: active infection, uncontrolled diabetes, GI bleed, severe renal failure
- START prednisolone 40 mg PO daily x 28 days
- START NAC 150 mg/kg IV over 30 min, 50 mg/kg over 4 hr, 100 mg/kg over 16 hr
- CONT NAC 100 mg/kg IV daily on days 2-5
- Lille score on day 4 or 7
- STOP prednisolone if Lille >0.45
- After 28 days, stop or taper over 3 wk _

- Hepatology consult, early transplant eval in selected pts

- START acamprosate 666 mg PO TID; 333 mg PO TID if CrCl 30-50, avoid if CrCl 30 or less
- START baclofen 5 mg PO TID x 3 days, then 10 mg PO TID
- Avoid disulfiram, and naltrexone if decompensated cirrhosis or liver failure

use: Use for suspected or confirmed infective endocarditis in a hospitalized adult.
body:
#Infective endocarditis
Likely infective endocarditis given _fever, new regurgitant murmur, + blood cx / S. aureus bacteremia w/ vegetation on echo / fever, injection drug use, septic pulmonary emboli.
Blood cx _ of _ sets, organism _. Echo _. _ major and _ minor criteria, _definite / possible / rejected. Predisposition _.

DDx:
>Native valve IE; most likely given _, _
>Prosthetic valve or device infection; considered but unlikely given _, TEE, PET/CT if valve placed >3 mo ago
>Bacteremia from another source; considered but unlikely given _, source imaging

- Blood cx 3 sets from separate venipunctures, first and last 1 hr or more apart, before abx
- Echo within 12 hr, TTE first
- TEE if TTE negative with high suspicion, prosthetic valve, or high complication risk
- Repeat TEE in 3-5 days if suspicion persists without dx
- Major micro: typical organism in 2 or more sets, nontypical organism in 3 or more sets
- Definite: 2 major, 1 major plus 3 minor, or 5 minor. Possible: 1 major plus 1 minor, or 3 minor
- ID consult when starting abx
- START vancomycin 15 mg/kg IV q12h, pharmacy to dose, plus ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h
- Repeat blood cx 2 sets q24-48h until cleared, count abx days from first negative cx
- ECG at baseline and with any change, new AV block suggests perivalvular abscess
- No adjunct aspirin or antiplatelet
- CONT chronic antiplatelet if no bleeding
- Dental exam, especially before valve surgery
- Repeat echo at end of therapy for new baseline
- Cardiac surgery consult for any early surgery criterion _
- Early surgery: HF from valve dysfunction, heart block, annular or aortic abscess, destructive lesion
- Early surgery: fungi or highly resistant organism, bacteremia or fever >5-7 days on correct abx
- Early surgery: recurrent emboli with persistent vegetation, severe regurgitation with mobile vegetation >10 mm

If acute presentation over days, native valve:

- START cefepime 2 g IV q8h in place of ceftriaxone (AHA)

If subacute presentation over weeks, native valve:

- START ampicillin-sulbactam 3 g IV q6h (AHA), or ceftriaxone 2 g IV q24h (Merck)

If prosthetic valve placed within 1 yr:

- START vancomycin, gentamicin 1 mg/kg IV q8h, rifampin 300 mg PO q8h, and cefepime 2 g IV q8h

If mechanical valve and CNS embolic event:

- HOLD all anticoagulation for 2 wk or more

use: Use for suspected or confirmed osteomyelitis, including vertebral and diabetic foot.
body:
#Osteomyelitis
Likely osteomyelitis given _DFU w/ probe to bone or sausage toe / back pain, fever, bacteremia / pain, erythema over bone near wound or hardware.
Site _. ESR _, CRP _, WBC _. Blood cx _. X-ray _, MRI _. Probe to bone _. Bone cx _.

DDx:
>Osteomyelitis, _ site; most likely given _, _
>Soft tissue infection without bone involvement; considered but unlikely given _, MRI to exclude
>_; considered but unlikely given _, _

- Blood cx 2 sets, CBC, ESR, CRP
- Plain X-ray first, MRI if dx still in doubt
- Bone biopsy for cx, percutaneous or operative, unless blood cx and imaging already define it
- Target abx to bone or blood cx
- ID consult _
- IV then highly bioavailable PO abx is acceptable
- Duration 4-6 wk unless site-specific below
- Surgical debridement for necrotic bone, abscess, or infected hardware
- ESR and CRP at about 4 wk
- No routine f/u MRI if improving, repeat MRI if poor response

If stable, no sepsis, normal neuro exam:

- HOLD empiric abx until bone biopsy cx obtained

If sepsis, instability, or severe or progressive neuro deficit:

- START vancomycin 15-20 mg/kg IV q8-12h, pharmacy to dose, plus _ by setting

If MSSA:

- START cefazolin 1-1.5 g IV q6h, or nafcillin or oxacillin 1-2 g IV q4h

If vertebral:

- MRI spine, image-guided aspiration biopsy if blood cx and serology negative
- Duration 6 wk IV or highly bioavailable PO
- Spine surgery for progressive neuro deficit, or persistent or recurrent bacteremia _
- IGRA if subacute with TB risk, Brucella serology if endemic exposure, fungal blood cx if risk

- Probe to bone, X-ray, and ESR or CRP first, MRI if still in doubt
- Bone biopsy ideally 2 wk off abx if safe to wait
- Duration: 6 wk if no resection, 3 wk if positive bone margin after minor amputation
- Duration: 2-5 days if infected bone fully resected
- Abx alone reasonable for forefoot osteomyelitis without PAD, exposed bone, or need for I&D
- Judge remission 6 mo or more after abx end

body:
#Bronchiectasis

- Thin-section CT chest to confirm; CXR and spirometry _
- Cause workup: CBC w/ diff, IgG, IgA, IgM, total IgE, Aspergillus-specific IgE and IgG
- Sputum bacterial and AFB cx when stable and at the start of each exacerbation, before abx
- Sweat chloride or CFTR testing, alpha-1 antitrypsin, RF, ANA, HIV as history suggests _
- Pulmonology referral _
- Airway clearance taught by RT or PT: active cycle of breathing or oscillating PEP device, 1-2x/day
- Increase airway clearance during exacerbations; saline inhalation first if prescribed _
- Pulmonary rehab if limited by breathlessness
- Influenza vaccine yearly, pneumococcal vaccine; COVID-19 and RSV vaccines per schedule _
- No inhaled steroid unless asthma or COPD; LABA or LAMA trial if significant breathlessness _
- Home sputum cup and standby abx for future exacerbations _

- ED if sepsis, respiratory distress, more than streaks of hemoptysis, or IV abx needed

- START amoxicillin-clavulanate 500/125 mg PO TID x 14 days if beta-lactamase organism or Moraxella
- START doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x 14 days if penicillin allergy
- 14 days standard, always if Pseudomonas; 7-10 days may suffice in mild disease

If Pseudomonas on prior cx:

- START ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO BID x 14 days, 750 mg BID if more severe

- Pulmonology to start long-term prophylaxis
- AFB sputum cx negative before macrolide; no chronic macrolide if NTM cultured
- Baseline ECG for QTc if cardiac risk; audiometry if hearing impairment
- START azithromycin 250 mg PO 3x/wk; 250 mg daily or 500 mg 3x/wk also studied
- START brensocatib 10 mg or 25 mg PO daily per pulmonology _

If chronic Pseudomonas with frequent exacerbations:

- Long-term inhaled abx per pulmonology _

If ABPA, immunodeficiency, CF, or PCD found:

- Specialist referral: pulmonology, immunology, or CF center _

body:
#Hemoptysis
Likely 2/2 _bronchitis or pneumonia given cough, fever / bronchiectasis given chronic daily sputum / lung cancer given smoking, age 40 or more.
Volume _ mL/24 hr, SpO2 _, RR _, Hgb _, CXR _. Anticoagulant or antiplatelet _.

DDx:
>_; most likely given _, _
>Pseudohemoptysis from nose, mouth, or upper GI tract; considered but unlikely given _, exam and nasopharyngoscopy if unclear
>Lung cancer; considered but unlikely given _, CT chest _
>PE or TB; considered but unlikely given _, CTA chest or sputum AFB _

- Confirm lower airway source: frothy bright red blood with cough, not coffee-ground or nasal
- CBC, CMP, PT/PTT; type and crossmatch if large volume or anemic
- CXR PA and lateral first
- CT chest w/ IV contrast if CXR abnormal or nondiagnostic, recurrent bleeding, or cancer risk
- CT despite normal CXR if age 40 or more w/ 30 pack-yr or more
- CTA chest if PE suspected or embolization may be needed
- Bronchoscopy, best within 24-48 hr of bleeding, if CT nondiagnostic, endobronchial lesion, or tissue or cx needed
- Sputum AFB smear and cx if TB risk _
- START antitussive _ to limit cough-triggered bleeding
- Abx if infection suspected; reassess in 24-48 hr
- Repeat CXR 6-8 wk after a treated infiltrate; CT if hemoptysis or infiltrate persists
- If CXR, CT and bronchoscopy negative: observe up to 3 yr, CTA if it recurs
- Red flags: RR >30, SpO2 <88% on RA, need >8 L/min O2, hypotension
- Red flags: Hgb <8 or drop >2, >200 mL/48 hr, or >50 mL per episode w/ chronic lung disease

If stable and blood-streaked sputum only:

- Outpatient care, f/u in 24-48 hr _

If admitted with nonmassive hemoptysis:

- START tranexamic acid 500 mg nebulized TID

If massive or unstable:

- ICU; lie bleeding side down, NPO, large-bore IV access, O2
- Airway protection by intubation or rigid bronchoscopy, isolate bleeding side _
- IR consult for bronchial artery embolization, treatment of choice
- Thoracic surgery consult if embolization fails or chest trauma

use: Use for the A&P of biliary colic from gallstones, with labs, surgical referral and signs of cholecystitis or duct stones.
body:
#Symptomatic cholelithiasis
Likely biliary colic given _steady RUQ pain 1-5 hr, resolved / attack after large meal or at night / recurrent attacks, gallstones on US.
US _, CBD _ mm, WBC _, AST/ALT _, alk phos _, bilirubin _, lipase _, Murphy sign _.

DDx:
>Biliary colic; most likely given _, pain resolved within 5 hr
>Acute cholecystitis; considered but unlikely given _, pain >6 hr, fever, Murphy sign, WBC _
>Choledocholithiasis or cholangitis; considered but unlikely given _, bilirubin and CBD _
>Gallstone pancreatitis; considered but unlikely given _, lipase _

- RUQ US first; CT if US negative or equivocal, or complication suspected
- CBC, AST, ALT, alk phos, total bilirubin, lipase
- General surgery referral for elective laparoscopic cholecystectomy _
- Recurrent pain: >90% within 10 yr, two-thirds within 2 yr
- START ibuprofen 400 mg PO q4-6h PRN pain
- NSAIDs as effective as opioids for biliary pain, fewer adverse effects
- Smaller meals; limit fried foods and desserts; lose weight slowly if overweight
- ED if pain >5 hr, fever, chills, jaundice, tea-colored urine, or persistent vomiting
- F/u after surgical consult _

If pain >6 hr, fever, Murphy sign, or leukocytosis:

- ED or direct admission for acute cholecystitis, surgery consult
- HIDA scan if US equivocal; normal gallbladder filling excludes cholecystitis

If CBD >6 mm, bilirubin >4, or fever w/ jaundice:

- ED for choledocholithiasis or cholangitis; IV abx and ERCP if cholangitis

If asymptomatic gallstones found incidentally:

- No surgery; about 2%/yr become symptomatic
- Surgery referral if porcelain gallbladder, stone >3 cm, hemolytic anemia, or transplant planned

If pregnant:

- Supportive care first; laparoscopic cholecystectomy safe in all trimesters if recurrent or complicated

If not a surgical candidate, stones 5 mm or smaller, functioning gallbladder:

- START ursodiol 8-10 mg/kg/day PO divided BID or TID
- US every 6 mo in yr 1; recurrence after dissolution >50%

If rapid weight loss planned, such as bariatric surgery:

- START ursodiol 300 mg PO BID for gallstone prevention

use: Use for the A&P of suspected or confirmed gastroparesis in adults, with workup, diet, prokinetics and GLP-1 RA review.
body:
#Gastroparesis
Likely gastroparesis given _nausea, vomiting, early satiety, postprandial fullness / longstanding DM w/ nausea and bloating / sxs on opioids or GLP-1 RA, no obstruction. _Suspected / confirmed.
EGD _, 4-hr gastric emptying retention _%, A1c _, BMP _, weight _ from _.

DDx:
>Gastroparesis; most likely given _, 4-hr solid gastric emptying study _
>Gastric outlet obstruction or ulcer; considered but unlikely given _, EGD _
>Functional dyspepsia; considered but unlikely given _, normal emptying _
>Medication effect from opioids or GLP-1 RA; considered but unlikely given _, _

- EGD to exclude obstruction before any emptying study
- 4-hr solid-meal gastric emptying scintigraphy; delayed if >10% retained at 4 hr
- Retained food on EGD alone does not diagnose gastroparesis
- Hold opioids and GLP-1 RA before the study per nuclear medicine _ local
- A1c, BMP; tighten glucose control in DM
- No opioids for pain, including tramadol and tapentadol
- Small particle diet: 5-6 small meals/day, soft well-cooked or pureed foods, chew well
- Low fat, low fiber; avoid raw apples, berries, oranges, figs, legumes, potato skins, sauerkraut
- Sit upright 1 hr after meals; avoid alcohol and carbonated drinks
- Liquids on bad days: broth, clear soups, low-fiber juices, ORS, liquid meal supplements
- Dietitian referral; weight at each visit
- GI referral if refractory, weight loss, dehydration, or unable to keep up oral intake
- F/u _ wk

If on a GLP-1 RA:

- STOP GLP-1 RA if sxs significant; semaglutide not recommended in severe gastroparesis

If refractory sxs despite diet:

- START metoclopramide 10 mg PO 30 min before meals and at bedtime, max 40 mg/day
- Avoid metoclopramide >12 wk; stop at the first abnormal movements, tardive dyskinesia risk
- Avoid metoclopramide with bupropion, fluoxetine, or paroxetine

If older adult:

- START metoclopramide 5 mg PO before meals and at bedtime, INCR. to 10 mg if needed

If CrCl <60, Child-Pugh B or C, CYP2D6 poor metabolizer, or on quinidine:

- START metoclopramide 5 mg PO before meals and at bedtime, max 20 mg/day

If metoclopramide not tolerated or contraindicated:

- START erythromycin 125-250 mg PO TID before meals x 2-4 wk

If nausea persists:

- START prochlorperazine 5-10 mg PO TID or QID PRN nausea

If refractory to diet and medicines:

- GI referral for G-POEM or gastric electrical stimulation

use: Use for the A&P of known Barrett's esophagus, with PPI therapy and surveillance intervals by dysplasia grade and segment length.
body:
#Barrett's esophagus
_Nondysplastic / indefinite for dysplasia / low-grade dysplasia / high-grade dysplasia, segment _ cm, _ on current PPI.
Last EGD _, Prague C _ M _, pathology _, confirmed by second GI pathologist _.

- CONT omeprazole 20 mg PO daily before breakfast, or equivalent PPI, long term
- No antireflux surgery for cancer prevention
- Any dysplasia confirmed by a second pathologist with GI expertise
- Surveillance EGD w/ high-definition white light, chromoendoscopy, and structured 4-quadrant biopsies
- No aspirin for chemoprevention; CV indication only _
- Consider stopping surveillance if life expectancy <5 yr or not fit for endoscopic therapy

If nondysplastic, <3 cm:

- EGD every 5 yr

If nondysplastic, 3 cm or longer:

- EGD every 3 yr

If indefinite for dysplasia:

- INCR. PPI to BID if not on high-dose PPI
- Repeat EGD within 6 mo; EGD yearly if still indefinite

If low-grade dysplasia:

- GI referral for endoscopic eradication therapy, preferred over surveillance
- If surveillance chosen: EGD at 6 and 12 mo, then yearly

If high-grade dysplasia or intramucosal cancer:

- GI referral to a high-volume center for endoscopic eradication therapy

If complete eradication after low-grade dysplasia:

- EGD 1 yr and 3 yr after eradication, then every 2 yr

If complete eradication after high-grade dysplasia:

- EGD at 3, 6, and 12 mo after eradication, then yearly

use: Use for the A&P of recurrent uncomplicated cystitis in nonpregnant women, with non-antibiotic and antibiotic prevention options.
body:
#Recurrent UTI
_2 or more culture-proven UTIs in 6 mo / 3 or more in 1 yr, _ on current prevention.
Cultures _, organisms _, menopausal status _, sex-related _, fluid intake _ L/day, eGFR _.

- UA and urine cx with each symptomatic episode, before abx
- Pelvic exam; vaginal atrophy _
- Cystoscopy and upper tract imaging not routine without complicating factors
- Urology referral if complicating factors _
- Treat acute episodes with the shortest effective course, generally 7 days or less
- If drinking <1.5 L/day: add about 1.5 L (50 oz) water daily, cut episodes about in half
- Cranberry juice or tablets daily: about 25% fewer culture-proven UTIs, best dose unknown
- D-mannose not recommended, no benefit over placebo
- F/u _ mo to review episodes and need for prophylaxis

If peri- or postmenopausal:

- START estradiol 10 mcg vaginal insert nightly x 2 wk, then twice weekly
- Vaginal, not oral, estrogen prevents recurrence

If prefers non-antibiotic prophylaxis:

- START methenamine hippurate 1 g PO BID
- Avoid methenamine if renal insufficiency, severe hepatic disease, severe dehydration, or on sulfonamides

If UTIs follow sex:

- START nitrofurantoin 50-100 mg PO once after sex
- START TMP-SMX 40/200 mg PO once after sex as alternative
- START cephalexin 250 mg PO once after sex as alternative

If continuous antibiotic prophylaxis chosen:

- START nitrofurantoin 50-100 mg PO nightly
- START TMP-SMX 40/200 mg PO nightly or 3x/wk as alternative
- START trimethoprim 100 mg PO daily as alternative
- START cephalexin 125-250 mg PO daily as alternative
- Avoid nitrofurantoin if CrCl <60 (FDA label) or <30 (AGS Beers)
- LFTs and CXR at least yearly if nitrofurantoin continued >6 mo
- Recurrence returns to baseline once prophylaxis stops

If reliable and wants self-start therapy:

- Standby abx _ x _ days, start after urine cx sample at sxs onset

use: Use for the A&P of overactive bladder in adults, with bladder training, beta-3 agonists and referral for third-line therapy.
body:
#Overactive bladder
Likely OAB given _urgency w/ frequency, UA negative / urgency w/ urge incontinence / nocturia w/ urgency, normal PVR.
UA _, PVR _, 3-day bladder diary: voids/day _, nocturia _, urge leaks/day _.

DDx:
>OAB; most likely given _, _
>UTI; considered but unlikely given _, UA _
>Retention or obstruction w/ overflow; considered but unlikely given _, PVR _
>Bladder cancer or stone; considered but unlikely given _, hematuria _

- UA for all; PVR by bladder scan if retention risk
- 3-day bladder diary
- Bladder training: timed voiding, urge suppression, lengthen interval by 30-60 min until every 3-4 hr
- Bladder training takes about 6-12 wk
- Pelvic floor muscle training: 3 sets of 8-10 contractions held 6-8 sec, 3-4x/wk, for 15-20 wk or more
- Cut caffeine to improve urgency
- Fluids about 1.5-2 L (50-70 oz)/day; over-restriction can worsen sxs
- Weight loss if overweight
- Urology if hematuria, elevated PVR, or refractory _
- F/u 4-8 wk after any medication change

If behavioral therapy insufficient:

- START mirabegron 25 mg PO daily
- INCR. mirabegron to 50 mg PO daily after 4-8 wk PRN
- Check BP on mirabegron; avoid if severe uncontrolled HTN
- START vibegron 75 mg PO daily as alternative
- Beta-3 agonist preferred over antimuscarinics in older adults given dementia risk

If eGFR 15-29 or Child-Pugh B:

- Mirabegron max 25 mg PO daily

If beta-3 agonist fails and no cognitive impairment:

- START solifenacin 5 mg PO daily, INCR. to 10 mg if tolerated
- Solifenacin max 5 mg if CrCl <30 or Child-Pugh B

If refractory to behavioral therapy and medication:

- Urology for PTNS: weekly sessions x 12 wk, then maintenance if responding
- Urology for onabotulinumtoxinA 100 units intradetrusor; must be willing to self-catheterize
- PVR within 2 wk after onabotulinumtoxinA; UTI risk increases
- Sacral neuromodulation _

use: Use for the A&P of new or suspected nephrotic syndrome in adults, with secondary-cause workup, edema, antiproteinuric therapy and VTE risk.
body:
#Nephrotic syndrome
Likely nephrotic syndrome given _new leg edema, foamy urine, heavy proteinuria / periorbital or generalized edema, weight gain / UPCR >3.5 g/g w/ low albumin.
UPCR _ g/g, albumin _ g/dL, Cr _, eGFR _, LDL _, UA sediment _, BP _.

DDx:
>Membranous nephropathy; most likely given _, PLA2R antibody _
>FSGS or minimal change disease; considered but unlikely given _, kidney biopsy _
>Diabetic kidney disease; considered but unlikely given _, A1c _
>Lupus, amyloidosis, or myeloma; considered but unlikely given _, ANA, C3, C4, SPEP _

- Criteria: proteinuria >3.5 g/day or UPCR >3.5, albumin <3.0 g/dL (some use <2.5), edema
- 24-hr urine protein before starting immunosuppression
- CMP, lipid panel, A1c, UA w/ microscopy for RBC casts
- Secondary causes: ANA, C3, C4, HBV, HCV, HIV, syphilis, SPEP, UPEP, serum free light chains
- PLA2R antibody; positive w/ nephrotic syndrome can confirm membranous without biopsy
- Drug causes: NSAIDs, lithium, interferon, pamidronate, heroin _
- Nephrology referral for biopsy, immunosuppression, and anticoagulation decisions _
- Sodium <2 g/day; protein 0.8-1.0 g/kg/day, no protein restriction
- START lisinopril 10 mg PO daily
- INCR. lisinopril up to 40 mg PO daily, max tolerated dose for proteinuria
- BMP after starting and titrating ACEi; Cr rise of 10-20% expected, do not stop for that
- No ACEi plus ARB combination
- START furosemide 40 mg PO BID; double every 1-3 days if edema persists
- Daily weights, goal loss 1-2 kg (2-4 lb)/day during diuresis
- Influenza vaccine yearly for patient and household, pneumococcal and recombinant zoster vaccines
- ED for one-sided leg swelling, chest pain, or dyspnea, VTE risk
- F/u _ wk for weight, BMP, and UPCR

If diuretic resistant:

- START metolazone _ PO 2-5 hr before loop diuretic; nephrology for IV diuretics

If persistent hyperlipidemia or ASCVD risk:

- START atorvastatin 20 mg PO daily

If albumin <2.5 g/dL (BCG) or <2.0 (BCP), esp membranous:

- Prophylactic anticoagulation if VTE risk exceeds bleeding risk, with nephrology _

If VTE occurs:

- Full anticoagulation _

Chronic HBV, _HBeAg positive / HBeAg negative, _immune active / inactive / immune tolerant / indeterminate, _untreated / on treatment _.
HBsAg _ for 6 mo or more, HBeAg _, anti-HBe _, HBV DNA _ IU/mL, ALT _. Platelets _, INR _, albumin _, FIB-4 _, elastography _ kPa.

- Abdominal US and elastography or FIB-4 to stage fibrosis
- Anti-HDV, anti-HCV, HIV if not done
- ALT upper limit for decisions: 35 men, 25 women (AASLD); 30 men, 19 women (WHO)

- Treat if HBV DNA >2,000 and ALT above ULN, or APRI >0.5 or elastography >7 kPa (WHO)
- Also treat regardless of DNA or ALT: HIV or HCV coinfection, family hx HCC or cirrhosis, immunosuppression, diabetes, extrahepatic disease (WHO)
- Abstain from or limit alcohol; hepatitis A vaccine if anti-HAV negative
- Household and sexual contacts: HBsAg and anti-HBs, vaccinate if negative; barrier protection until partner immune
- Sexual partners: anti-HBs 1 to 2 mo after last vaccine dose
- No sharing razors, toothbrushes, or glucose meters; cover cuts; no blood, organ, or sperm donation
- HCC surveillance: US with AFP q6 mo if cirrhosis, Asian or Black men >40, Asian women >50, first-degree relative with HCC, or HDV
- If HIV coinfection, HCC surveillance for men 18 or older and women 40 or older
- Hepatology referral _

If treating:

- START tenofovir alafenamide 25 mg PO daily with food
- START tenofovir disoproxil fumarate 300 mg PO daily
- START entecavir 0.5 mg PO daily on an empty stomach, 2 hr after and 2 hr before meals
- Renal or bone disease: TAF or entecavir over TDF
- Dose-adjust entecavir and TDF if CrCl <50; TAF not recommended if CrCl <15 unless on dialysis
- Creatinine clearance at baseline; if renal risk, CrCl, phosphate, urine glucose and protein at least annually
- HBV DNA q3 mo until undetectable, then q3 to 6 mo
- Continue until HBsAg loss; antivirals do not remove HCC risk
- If stopping: HBV DNA and ALT q1 to 3 mo x 6 mo
- Restart if HBV DNA 10,000 or more or ALT 5x ULN or more

- START entecavir 1 mg PO daily or tenofovir disoproxil fumarate 300 mg PO daily indefinitely
- Hepatology and transplant referral

- Treat if age >40 or fibrosis F2 or more; optional if younger
- If not treating, HBV DNA and ALT at least q6 mo

If inactive (HBeAg negative, normal ALT, DNA <2,000):

- No treatment; ALT and HBV DNA q3 mo x 1 yr, then q6 to 12 mo
- HBsAg yearly to check for clearance

If HBeAg negative indeterminate:

- Treatment optional; male sex, age >40, and platelets <180,000 favor treating
- If not treating, HBV DNA and ALT q3 to 6 mo x 1 yr, then q6 mo

- START tenofovir disoproxil fumarate 300 mg PO daily, or TAF 25 mg PO daily, from 28 wk to delivery

- If treating only to prevent transmission, stop at delivery; ALT q1 to 3 mo for up to 6 mo

- START entecavir 0.5 mg PO daily or tenofovir disoproxil fumarate 300 mg PO daily before therapy

use: Use for staging and treatment of syphilis in nonpregnant and pregnant adults.
body:
#Syphilis
Likely _primary syphilis given painless chancre / secondary syphilis given palm and sole rash / latent syphilis given reactive screen, no sxs.
RPR 1:_, treponemal test _, prior titer _ on _. HIV _, pregnancy test _. Cranial nerves, vision, hearing _.

DDx:
>Early syphilis (primary, secondary, early latent); most likely given _, infection within 12 mo
>Late latent or unknown duration; considered but unlikely given _, 3 weekly doses if infection not proven within 12 mo
>Neurosyphilis, ocular, or otosyphilis; considered but unlikely given normal neuro, eye, and ear exam _

- Early latent if within 12 mo: seroconversion, sustained fourfold titer rise, primary or secondary sxs, or partner with early syphilis
- HIV test at dx; offer PrEP if negative
- Jarisch-Herxheimer counseled: fever, headache, myalgia within 24 hr; antipyretics; not a penicillin allergy
- No azithromycin or other macrolides; resistance is near universal
- Partners exposed within 90 days of early syphilis: treat presumptively even if seronegative
- Partner notification window: primary 3 mo plus sx duration, secondary 6 mo plus sx duration, early latent 1 yr
- Long-term partners of late latent: exam and serology, treat by results
- Health department report and partner services _ local
- Repeat RPR: 6 and 12 mo if primary or secondary, 6, 12, and 24 mo if latent
- Failure: persistent or recurrent sxs, or sustained fourfold titer rise; CSF exam, retest HIV, then retreat
- Retreat with benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly x 3 unless CSF shows neurosyphilis
- Primary or secondary with titer not down fourfold by 12 mo: seen in 10 to 20%, close f/u _
- Latent with titer >1:32 not down fourfold by 24 mo: consider CSF exam

If primary, secondary, or early latent:

- START benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM once

If late latent or unknown duration:

- START benzathine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM weekly x 3 doses
- Missed dose: 7 to 9 days apart preferred, 10 to 14 days may be acceptable, else restart series
- CSF exam if neuro findings

If pregnant:

- Benzathine penicillin G by stage is the only recommended treatment
- Penicillin allergy: desensitize, then treat with penicillin
- Any dose delayed >9 days: repeat the full course

If nonpregnant with penicillin allergy or benzathine shortage:

- START doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x 14 days if early syphilis
- START doxycycline 100 mg PO BID x 28 days if late latent or unknown duration
- Benzathine penicillin if adherence or f/u uncertain; desensitize if allergic
- Shortage: reserve benzathine penicillin for pregnancy and doxycycline contraindication

If neuro, eye, or ear signs:

- Neuro signs (cranial nerve palsy, meningitis, stroke, cognitive change, motor or sensory deficit): CSF exam
- Eye signs (uveitis, retinitis, optic neuritis): same-day ophthalmology, treat as neurosyphilis even if CSF normal
- Ear signs (hearing loss, tinnitus, vertigo): otology exam, treat as neurosyphilis, CSF not needed
- START aqueous penicillin G 3 to 4 million units IV q4h (18 to 24 million units/day) x 10 to 14 days
- START procaine penicillin G 2.4 million units IM daily plus probenecid 500 mg PO QID x 10 to 14 days if adherence assured

body:
#Chronic venous insufficiency
Likely chronic venous insufficiency given _leg heaviness worse standing, better elevated / varicose veins with ankle swelling / ankle skin pigmentation or healed ulcer.
CEAP _C1 / C2 / C3 / C4a / C4b / C4c / C5 / C6. Pulses _, ABI _, duplex reflux _. Ulcer size _ cm, duration _.

DDx:
>Chronic venous insufficiency; most likely given _, duplex reflux study
>DVT; considered but unlikely given _, duplex ultrasound
>Peripheral artery disease; considered but unlikely given pulses _, ABI before compression
>Heart failure, kidney, liver, or medication edema; considered but unlikely given _, _

- CEAP: C1 spider or reticular veins, C2 varicose veins 3 mm or more, C3 edema
- CEAP: C4 skin changes (a pigment or eczema, b lipodermatosclerosis, c ankle flare), C5 healed ulcer, C6 active ulcer
- Duplex with reflux study, standing, if symptomatic C2 or higher
- ABI before compression; no compression if ABI <0.5
- ABI 0.5 to 0.8: reduced compression only with vascular input
- Compression stockings 20 to 30 mmHg, on at waking, off at bedtime, replace q6 mo
- Higher stocking pressures add no clear symptom benefit
- Legs above heart level when resting, avoid long standing or sitting
- Daily walking and calf raises for the calf pump; progressive resistance exercise
- Weight loss if overweight
- START horse chestnut seed extract standardized to escin 50 mg PO BID x up to 12 wk for pain and swelling
- Vein specialist referral if symptomatic varicose veins with saphenous reflux; ablation beats long-term stockings
- No 3-mo compression trial needed before ablation; insurer requirement _
- Bleeding varicose vein: elevate, direct pressure, prompt vein referral
- F/u in _ mo

If venous ulcer:

- Multicomponent compression bandage or stockings 30 to 40 mmHg, at least 20 to 30 mmHg
- Moist dressing chosen by exudate, comfort, cost; no single dressing is superior
- Sharp debridement of slough at visits _
- START pentoxifylline 400 mg PO TID with compression
- Abx only for clinical infection, oral, 2 wk or less
- Early endovenous ablation of superficial reflux speeds healing; vein referral now
- Wound clinic referral if large, long-standing, or no improvement after 4 wk _ local
- Biopsy if atypical or healing stalls
- After healing: stockings indefinitely; leg elevation 1 hr/day, 6 days/wk lowers recurrence

use: Use for arm or leg lymphedema, including after cancer surgery or radiation.
body:
#Lymphedema
Likely lymphedema given _arm swelling after node dissection or radiation / leg swelling, positive Stemmer sign / limb heaviness not relieved by elevation.
Stage _0 / I / II / III. Limb circumference difference _ cm at _, Stemmer _, pitting _, skin _. Cellulitis episodes in past yr _.
